definition_zh: 稳定；稳定化；使趋于平稳的过程；（经济、政治）稳定措施
definition_en: the process of making something firm, steady, or unlikely to move, change or fail
core_image: 一名工人把晃动的三脚架逐条腿拧紧，直到水平仪的气泡停在中央
scene: 这里指「稳定」。 The central bank's stabilization program slowed inflation within a year.
sceneCN: 这里 stabilization 是「稳定化」（第 2 个义项：用政策手段让价格、货币或经济趋于平稳）；句意：中央银行的稳定化计划在一年内让通胀放缓。图中可辨识物件：三脚架、水平仪气泡、拧紧的旋钮、趋于水平的平台。

pos.zh: 稳定；稳定化；（经济、政治）稳定措施（指过程时多不可数，指多项措施时可用复数 stabilizations）

senses.title: The act of making something steady
senses.titleCN: 稳定化：使某物趋于稳固的过程
senses.definition: the process of making something firm, steady, or less likely to move, change or fail
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变得稳固、平稳、不易移动、变化或失败的过程
senses.example: The stabilization of the scaffolding took two hours before the painters climbed up.
senses.exampleCN: 为了让油漆工登上去，脚手架的加固稳定花了两个小时。
senses.why: Latin stabilis meant 'firm, steadfast', and the noun ending -ation names the action of producing that state, so the word begins with the picture of something wobbling and being held still.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 stabilis 意为「稳固的、坚定的」，名词词尾 -ation 命名制造这种状态的动作，因此词义起点是「某物在晃、被扶稳」的画面。

senses.title: Policy action that steadies an economy
senses.titleCN: 经济稳定化：用政策稳住价格与货币
senses.definition: the use of official policy, such as interest rates or fiscal measures, to keep prices, currency or output from swinging sharply
senses.definitionCN: 运用利率、财政措施等官方政策，使价格、货币或产出不出现剧烈波动的做法
senses.example: The stabilization program combined tight spending with a fixed exchange rate.
senses.exampleCN: 这项稳定化计划把紧缩开支与固定汇率结合在一起。
senses.why: In the twentieth century governments and international lenders turned the general idea of steadying into a named policy package, so stabilization came to mean the measures themselves, especially after wartime inflation.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪，各国政府与国际贷款机构把「稳住」这一一般概念变成有名称的政策组合，于是 stabilization 开始指这些措施本身，尤其在战时通胀之后。

senses.title: Restoring order to a government or region
senses.titleCN: 政治稳定化：恢复政权或地区的秩序
senses.definition: the process of bringing a government, region or institution back to order after unrest, conflict or collapse
senses.definitionCN: 在动荡、冲突或崩溃之后，使政府、地区或机构恢复秩序的过程
senses.example: The peace mission focused on political stabilization rather than reconstruction.
senses.exampleCN: 这支和平使团把重点放在政治稳定，而不是重建。
senses.why: Because a state can wobble like a structure, the same noun was extended from physical steadiness to the steadiness of public order, a use that became common in diplomacy.
senses.whyCN: 国家也会像结构物一样摇晃，于是同一个名词从物理上的稳固扩展到公共秩序的稳固，这一用法在外交领域变得常见。

senses.title: Reinforcing a building, slope or bridge
senses.titleCN: 结构加固：让建筑、坡体或桥梁不再失稳
senses.definition: engineering work that makes a structure or a mass of ground able to stand without shifting or collapsing
senses.definitionCN: 使建筑物或土体能够站住、不位移、不坍塌的工程处理
senses.example: Slope stabilization with concrete anchors prevented a landslide above the road.
senses.exampleCN: 用混凝土锚杆进行的坡体加固防止了公路上方的滑坡。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense applied to large objects: the thing is given the firmness that Latin stabilis named, and the noun describes the work that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的物理义项在大尺度物体上的应用：对象被赋予拉丁 stabilis 所指的稳固，名词则描述产生这种稳固的工程。

senses.title: Bringing a patient to a safe condition
senses.titleCN: 医疗稳定：把病人的生命体征拉到安全范围
senses.definition: the medical process of bringing a patient's breathing, blood pressure and heart rate to a level that is safe enough for further treatment
senses.definitionCN: 把病人的呼吸、血压与心率调整到足以接受后续治疗的安全水平的医疗过程
senses.example: The paramedics achieved stabilization before moving the injured climber.
senses.exampleCN: 急救人员在搬运受伤的登山者之前先完成了生命体征稳定。
senses.why: A body in crisis is described as unstable, so the act of holding its vital signs within safe limits takes the same noun; the metaphor treats physiology as a system that can be propped up.
senses.whyCN: 处于危机的身体被称为不稳定，因此把生命体征维持在安全范围内的动作沿用同一个名词；这一比喻把生理状态看作可以被支撑住的系统。

senses.title: Treating a substance so it does not change
senses.titleCN: 化学稳定：处理物质使其不易变质或反应
senses.definition: the treatment of a chemical or material so that it resists decay, separation or unwanted reaction
senses.definitionCN: 对化学品或材料进行处理，使其不易腐败、分离或发生不需要的反应
senses.example: The stabilization of the vaccine required a strict cold chain.
senses.exampleCN: 疫苗的稳定化处理需要严格的冷链。
senses.why: Chemists borrowed the word because a compound that decomposes is literally not standing firm; adding a stabilizer makes its bonds hold, and the process is called stabilization.
senses.whyCN: 化学家借用这个词，是因为会分解的化合物字面上就「站不稳」；加入稳定剂让化学键保持住，这一过程便称为稳定化。

senses.title: Removing jitter from an image or signal
senses.titleCN: 图像或信号防抖：消除抖动与漂移
senses.definition: the reduction of unwanted shake or drift in a camera image, a recording or a stream of data
senses.definitionCN: 减少相机画面、录音或数据流中不需要的抖动或漂移
senses.example: Optical stabilization keeps handheld video smooth at long focal lengths.
senses.exampleCN: 光学防抖让长焦段的手持视频保持平稳。
senses.why: This technical sense keeps the core image almost literally: a shaking frame is steadied, and the noun names the mechanism or the correction, not the physical support.
senses.whyCN: 这一技术义项几乎字面保留核心意象：晃动的画面被稳住，名词指机制或校正，而不是物理支撑。

senses.title: A population that stops growing
senses.titleCN: 人口稳定：数量停止增长并保持水平
senses.definition: the point at which births and deaths balance so that a population stops rising and holds roughly level
senses.definitionCN: 出生与死亡达到平衡、人口停止上升并大致保持水平的状态
senses.example: Demographers expect global population stabilization later this century.
senses.exampleCN: 人口学家预计全球人口将在本世纪后期趋于稳定。
senses.why: Here the thing being held level is a number rather than an object, an extension of the same idea of stopping a movement, common in demography and ecology.
senses.whyCN: 这里被保持在水平线上的是数字而不是物体，仍是「止住某种移动」这一思路的延伸，常见于人口学与生态学。

intro.en: Stabilization is an English noun of action built on the verb stabilize, whose base is Latin stabilis 'firm', from stare 'to stand'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: stabilization 是英语动作名词，建立在动词 stabilize 之上；其词基为拉丁 stabilis「稳固的」，出自 stare「站立」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin stabilis meant 'firm, steadfast, able to stand'. It is an adjective in -bilis built on stare 'to stand', a root shared by status, station and constant.
items.cn: 拉丁 stabilis 意为「稳固的、坚定的、站得住的」，是加 -bilis 的形容词，建立在 stare「站立」之上；status、station、constant 共享这个词根。

items.en: The verb stabilire 'to make firm, establish' is attested in Latin and supplies the action behind the English verb. Its past participle stabilis is the source of the adjective.
items.cn: 动词 stabilire「使稳固、确立」在拉丁文献中有记录，为英语动词提供动作基础；其分词形式与形容词 stabilis 同源。

items.en: French stabiliser and English stabilize appear in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, built on the adjective with the verb suffix -ize.
items.cn: 法语 stabiliser 与英语 stabilize 分别出现在十八、十九世纪，由形容词加动词词尾 -ize 构成。

items.en: Stabilization adds -ation, the noun-of-action ending that reached English through French. It names the act of stabilizing rather than the state, which is stability.
items.cn: stabilization 加上了经法语进入英语的动作名词词尾 -ation，命名「使稳定」的动作，而不是状态；状态由 stability 表示。

items.en: The economic and political senses became fixed in the twentieth century through phrases such as stabilization fund, stabilization program and macroeconomic stabilization.
items.cn: 经济与政治义项在二十世纪通过 stabilization fund、stabilization program、macroeconomic stabilization 等短语固定下来。

items.en: The exact first English citation of stabilization is uncertain. The deeper root of stare is reconstructed as Indo-European *sta-, so the form is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：stabilization 的英语最早书证年代不明。stare 的更深词根被重构为印欧语 *sta-，属重构形式，而非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: The first group separates members of the same Latin family that differ in part of speech; the second gives near-synonyms for the result or the process.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一拉丁词族中词性不同的成员；第二组给出表示结果或过程的近义词。

entries.definition: The state of being steady. You can measure the stability of a bridge, but stabilization is the work done to produce it.
entries.definitionCN: 指稳固的状态：可以测量桥的稳定性，而 stabilization 是产生这种稳定性所做的工作。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to make or become steady; stabilization is the corresponding action noun.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为使稳定或变得稳定；stabilization 是相应的动作名词。

entries.definition: Describes a thing that stands firm; it is the quality word, not the process word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述站得稳的事物；它是性质词，不是过程词。

entries.definition: The object that produces steadiness, such as a camera stabilizer or a chemical additive; stabilization is the process, not the object.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生稳定效果的物件，如相机稳定器或化学稳定剂；stabilization 是过程，不是物件。

entries.definition: The act of combining parts into one solid whole. Stabilization keeps something from moving; consolidation makes it one body.
entries.definitionCN: 把各部分合并成一个坚固整体的动作：stabilization 让某物不再移动，consolidation 让它成为一个整体。

entries.definition: A state in which opposing forces cancel. It is a condition that can exist without any action, while stabilization implies an effort to reach it.
entries.definitionCN: 指相反力量相互抵消的状态；这种状态可以自然存在，而 stabilization 隐含达到它的努力。

entries.definition: Protection from threat, especially military or financial. It is broader and more subjective than the technical steadiness of stabilization.
entries.definitionCN: 指免受威胁，尤指军事或金融方面；它比 stabilization 的技术性「平稳」更宽泛、更主观。

entries.definition: The everyday quality of not shaking or changing. It is close to stability but lacks the technical and policy senses of stabilization.
entries.definitionCN: 日常意义上的「不晃、不变」，接近 stability，但没有 stabilization 的技术与政策义项。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: stable + -ize + -ation: first make steady, then name the making.
normal.cn: stable + -ize + -ation：先使稳固，再为「使稳固」这一动作命名。

normal.en: The family runs stable, stability, stabilize, stabilizer, instability, destabilize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 stable、stability、stabilize、stabilizer、instability、destabilize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the policy sense: stabilization program, stabilization fund, price stabilization, macroeconomic stabilization.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出政策义项：稳定化计划、稳定基金、价格稳定、宏观经济稳定。

normal.en: A camera lens advertises image stabilization; a central bank advertises price stabilization.
normal.cn: 相机镜头宣传图像防抖，中央银行宣传价格稳定，二者用的是同一个词。

normal.en: Stability is the state; stabilization is the work; a stabilizer is the tool.
normal.cn: stability 是状态，stabilization 是工作过程，stabilizer 是工具。

abstract.en: Picture a tower of blocks wobbling and a hand pressing the top flat.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆积木在摇晃，一只手把顶部压平。

abstract.en: Picture a climbing line on a chart that suddenly turns into a horizontal rule.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上一条攀升的线突然变成水平直线。

abstract.en: Picture a ship's gyroscope holding the deck level while the sea moves.
abstract.cn: 想象船用陀螺仪在波涛中让甲板保持水平。

examples.en: The stabilization of the currency required both higher interest rates and spending cuts.
examples.cn: 货币的稳定化既需要提高利率，也需要削减开支。

examples.en: Engineers completed the slope stabilization before the rainy season began.
examples.cn: 工程师在雨季开始前完成了坡体加固。

examples.en: Optical stabilization lets a handheld camera take sharp pictures in dim light.
examples.cn: 光学防抖让手持相机在弱光下也能拍出清晰照片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「stable（稳的）+ ization」——把晃动的东西扶稳 → stabilization 稳定化

root: 拉丁 stabilis「稳固的」（出自 stare「站立」）→ 拉丁 stabilire「使稳固」→ 法语 stabiliser → 英语 stabilize + -ation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea at different scales: a tripod steadied, a currency held level, a region restored to order, a slope anchored, a patient kept alive, a compound kept from decaying, a frame kept from shaking, and a population that stops growing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一思路在不同尺度上的展开：扶稳三脚架、稳住货币、恢复地区秩序、锚固坡体、维持病人生命、防止化合物变质、让画面不抖，以及人口停止增长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wobbling object is caught and held level.
core.cn: 核心意象：晃动的物体被抓住并保持在水平线上。

branches.en: PLAIN ACTION: any effort that turns a shaky thing into a firm one.
branches.cn: 一般动作：任何把摇晃之物变为稳固之物的努力。

branches.en: HOLDING A QUANTITY FLAT: prices, currency and population stop swinging or rising.
branches.cn: 把数量压平：价格、货币与人口停止波动或上升。

branches.en: ORDER IN A STATE: public authority is restored after unrest.
branches.cn: 国家秩序：动荡之后恢复公共权威。

branches.en: PHYSICAL SUPPORT: ground, bridges and buildings are anchored so they cannot fail.
branches.cn: 物理支撑：土体、桥梁与建筑被锚固，因而不致失稳。

branches.en: FRAGILE SYSTEMS: vital signs, chemical bonds and image frames are kept from failing or drifting.
branches.cn: 脆弱系统：生命体征、化学键与画面帧被维持住，不致崩溃或漂移。

intro.en: Stabilization is layered: a Latin adjective of standing firm, a Latin verb of making firm, an English verb in -ize, and the action-noun ending -ation.
intro.cn: stabilization 是分层构成的：表示「站得稳」的拉丁形容词，表示「使稳固」的拉丁动词，加 -ize 的英语动词，以及动作名词词尾 -ation。

latinIntro.en: Latin stabilis and stabilire come from stare 'to stand', the root behind stable, stability, constant, status and station; the noun ending -atio reached English as -ation through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 stabilis 与 stabilire 出自 stare「站立」，这一词根也见于 stable、stability、constant、status、station；名词词尾 -atio 经法语进入英语作 -ation。

items.example: Currency stabilization was the first goal of the new government.
items.exampleCN: 货币稳定是新政府的首要目标。

items.example: Doctors worked to stabilize the patient's breathing.
items.exampleCN: 医生努力稳定病人的呼吸。

items.example: The table felt stable once the fourth leg was fitted.
items.exampleCN: 装上第四条腿后，桌子就稳了。

items.example: Political stability encouraged foreign investment.
items.exampleCN: 政治稳定吸引了外国投资。

items.meaning: a device or substance that keeps something steady
items.meaningCN: 保持稳定的装置或物质
items.example: A stabilizer in the fuel prevents it from separating.
items.exampleCN: 燃料中的稳定剂防止其分层。

items.example: Currency instability made long-term planning difficult.
items.exampleCN: 货币不稳定使长期规划变得困难。

items.example: Rumors can destabilize a fragile government.
items.exampleCN: 谣言能动摇一个脆弱的政府。

items.meaning: the act of making something unsteady
items.example: The report warned of regional destabilization.
items.exampleCN: 报告警告了地区动荡的风险。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 稳固的；坚定的；站得住的

latinEntries.meaning: suffix naming an action or its result
latinEntries.meaningCN: 命名动作或其结果的词尾

definition_zh: 画家；油漆工；粉刷工
definition_en: an artist who paints pictures, or a worker who paints surfaces
core_image: 同一只手，一边在画布上安排颜色，一边在墙上把颜色铺平
scene: 装修现场，工人把梯子挪到墙边，准备刷第二遍。 The painter moved the ladder and began the second coat.
sceneCN: 这里 painter 指「以粉刷、涂漆为业的工人」（第 2 个义项：给建筑表面涂漆的油漆工）；句意为油漆工挪好梯子，开始刷第二遍；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 画家；油漆工；粉刷工

derivatives.zh: paint + -ing（动作或结果）→ 绘画；从「人」转到「活动与产物」
painter + -ly（形容词）→ 有笔触感的；从「人」转到「画面风格」
paint + work（成品）→ 漆面；从「动作」转到「表面结果」
paint + -ed（分词）→ 上过漆的；从「动作」转到「状态」

senses.title: An artist who paints pictures
senses.definition: a person who makes pictures with paint as an artist
senses.definitionCN: 以绘画为艺术创作的人
senses.example: The painter worked standing up, with the canvas on an easel.
senses.exampleCN: 这位画家站着作画，画布放在画架上。
senses.why: The agent suffix -er turns paint into 'one who paints'; in the art world that person is the maker of pictures.
senses.whyCN: 施事后缀 -er 把 paint 变成「涂绘的人」；在艺术界，这个人就是图画的制作者。

senses.title: A worker who paints surfaces
senses.definition: a tradesperson who applies paint to buildings and other surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 给建筑及其他表面涂漆的行业工人
senses.example: The painter moved the ladder and began the second coat.
senses.exampleCN: 油漆工挪好梯子，开始刷第二遍。
senses.why: The verb's everyday sense is 'coat a surface', so the same agent noun also names the trade that does it for pay.
senses.whyCN: 动词的日常义是「涂覆表面」，因此同一个施事名词也命名以此为报酬的行业。

senses.title: An artist known for a subject
senses.titleCN: 以某类题材著称的画家
senses.definition: an artist identified with a particular subject or genre
senses.definitionCN: 与某一题材或画类紧密相连的艺术家
senses.example: He was a painter of harbours before he was a painter of battles.
senses.exampleCN: 他先是画港口的画家，后来才画战役。
senses.why: The of-phrase narrows the artist's identity to what he habitually depicts, a common way of naming artistic specialism.
senses.whyCN: of 短语把艺术家的身份收窄到他惯常描绘之物，这是命名艺术专长的常见方式。

senses.title: An artist known for a medium
senses.titleCN: 以某种媒介著称的画家
senses.definition: an artist identified with a particular medium, as in oil painter
senses.definitionCN: 与某种媒介相连的艺术家，如油画家
senses.example: As an oil painter she distrusted quick sketches.
senses.exampleCN: 作为油画家，她不信任快速素描。
senses.why: Compounds put the medium before the agent, so the painter is defined by the material whose craft he has mastered.
senses.whyCN: 复合词把媒介放在施事者前，因此画家由他所精通的材料来界定。

senses.title: A painter in art history
senses.definition: a painter as a historical figure studied in art history
senses.definitionCN: 作为艺术史研究对象的历史人物
senses.example: The catalogue lists every painter represented in the collection.
senses.exampleCN: 图录列出了收藏中出现的每一位画家。
senses.why: The discipline turns individual makers into catalogue entries and attributions, so painter becomes a historical category.
senses.whyCN: 学科把个体创作者变成图录条目与归属判断，因此 painter 成为历史类别。

senses.title: An amateur or hobby painter
senses.definition: a person who paints for pleasure rather than professionally
senses.definitionCN: 为乐趣而非职业作画的人
senses.example: My uncle is a painter on Sundays and a clerk all week.
senses.exampleCN: 我叔叔周日是画家，其余时间是小职员。
senses.why: An agent noun does not require payment, so anyone who performs the action can be called a painter, including a hobbyist.
senses.whyCN: 施事名词不要求报酬，因此任何执行该动作的人都能被称为 painter，包括业余爱好者。

senses.title: A sign or lettering painter
senses.definition: a craftsman who paints signs, lettering or decorative surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 绘制招牌、字体或装饰表面的工匠
senses.example: The sign painter lettered the shop window by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 招牌画工用手工给橱窗写字。
senses.why: Compound specialisms preserve older workshop senses: the painter is the skilled hand in a named trade, not necessarily a fine artist.
senses.whyCN: 复合专名保留较早的工坊义：painter 是某个具名行当里的熟练手，不一定是纯艺术家。

senses.title: A workshop painter
senses.definition: a painter employed in a master's workshop to execute parts of works
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于名家工坊、执行作品局部的画师
senses.example: Many panels were finished by a workshop painter rather than the master.
senses.exampleCN: 许多木板画是由工坊画师而非名家本人完成的。
senses.why: Before the modern studio, paintings were made by teams; the word names each hand in the division of labour.
senses.whyCN: 在现代工作室出现之前，绘画由团队完成；这个词命名分工中的每一只手。

intro.en: Painter comes from Old French peintor, from Latin pictor, an agent noun from pingere 'to paint'; a separate homograph for a boat rope has a different origin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: painter 来自古法语 peintor，上溯拉丁 pictor，即 pingere「绘画」的施事名词；另有一个指船缆的同形词，来源不同。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pingere meant 'to paint, depict, stain'; its deeper root is reconstructed as *peig- 'to cut, mark'.
items.cn: pingere 意为「绘画、描绘、染色」；其更早词根拟为 *peig-「切、刻痕」。

items.en: Pictor was the agent noun 'painter', formed from the stem of pingere; it named both the artist and the craftsman.
items.cn: pictor 是施事名词「画家」，由 pingere 的词干构成；既指艺术家，也指工匠。

items.en: Old French peintor carried the word into English; the same French form also named a rope on a boat, a confusing coincidence of spelling.
items.cn: 古法语 peintor 把这个词带入英语；同一法语形式还指船上的一条缆绳，这是令人困惑的拼写巧合。

items.en: English painter is recorded in the early fourteenth century as 'artist who paints pictures'.
items.cn: 英语 painter 于 14 世纪初有记录，指「作画的艺术家」。

items.en: By about 1400 the word also meant 'workman who colours surfaces with paint'.
items.cn: 到约 1400 年，这个词也指「用颜料给表面着色的工人」。

items.en: The rope painter of the mid-fourteenth century probably comes from a different Old French word and ultimately from Latin pendere 'to hang'; that path is uncertain, and the two words are unrelated despite identical spelling.
items.cn: 14 世纪中叶指缆绳的 painter 可能来自另一个古法语词，最终上溯拉丁 pendere「悬挂」；这条路径不确定，两个词尽管拼写相同却并不同源。

note.en: Group one holds the same-stem words and the unrelated rope homograph; group two holds occupations and art roles that overlap but stress a different material or setting.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干词以及无关的缆绳同形词；第二组是重叠但强调不同材料或场景的职业与艺术角色。

entries.definition: A rope used to tie a boat; it is a homograph, not a sense of the artist word, and comes probably from Latin pendere 'to hang'.
entries.definitionCN: 系船的缆绳；是同形异源词，不是艺术家一词的义项，可能来自拉丁 pendere「悬挂」。

entries.definition: A picture or the activity of painting; painter is the person who performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 画作或绘画活动；painter 是执行它的人。

entries.definition: To coat or depict, or the coloured substance; painter is the agent.
entries.definitionCN: 涂覆或描绘，或彩色材料；painter 是施事者。

entries.definition: Having visible brushwork or a soft, painted quality; it describes a surface, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 有可见笔触或柔和绘画感的；描述表面，而非人。

entries.definition: A maker of art in any medium; painter is the narrower word for one who works in paint.
entries.definitionCN: 任何媒介的艺术创作者；painter 是专指用颜料者的较窄词。

entries.definition: A worker who paints and papers interiors; painter stresses the paintwork, decorator the whole finish.
entries.definitionCN: 给室内刷漆贴墙纸的工人；painter 强调涂漆，decorator 强调整体饰面。

entries.definition: A painter who works on walls; painter is neutral about scale or support.
entries.definitionCN: 在墙上作画的画家；painter 对尺幅与支撑物不加限定。

entries.definition: A painter or photographer specialising in portraits; painter names no subject.
entries.definitionCN: 专攻肖像的画家或摄影师；painter 不限定题材。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: paint + -er 'one who': the person who paints, whether canvas or wall.
normal.cn: paint + -er「从事者」：涂绘的人，无论画布还是墙面。

normal.en: Latin pictor is the ancestor, and picture and pigment share the stem.
normal.cn: 祖先是拉丁 pictor，picture 与 pigment 共享同一词干。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: portrait painter, house painter, sign painter.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：肖像画家、房屋油漆工、招牌画工。

normal.en: The family runs paint, painter, painting, painted and painterly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 paint、painter、painting、painted 与 painterly。

normal.en: The rope painter is a different word: same spelling, different origin, no family relation.
normal.cn: 指缆绳的 painter 是另一个词：拼写相同、来源不同、没有亲缘关系。

abstract.en: Picture one hand that can both compose a face and flatten a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象同一只手既能安排一张脸，也能把一面墙铺平。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder standing where an easel might also stand.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子立在本可放画架的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a name that two unrelated things have learned to share.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被两件无关之物共用的名字。

examples.en: The painter left the canvas unfinished when the light changed.
examples.cn: 光线一变，画家就停下未完成的画。

examples.en: A painter and decorator was repainting the stairwell.
examples.cn: 一位油漆装饰工正在重刷楼梯间。

examples.en: The workshop painter filled in the background while the master worked on the face.
examples.cn: 名家画脸时，工坊画师补画背景。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「paint（涂颜料）+ -er（人）」——涂颜料的人 → 画家／油漆工

root: 拉丁 pingere「绘画、染色」的施事名词 pictor，经古法语 peintor 进入英语，14 世纪初指画家，约 1400 年兼指油漆工。指船缆的 painter 为同形异源词，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses distinguish the fine artist from the trade worker, then split by subject, medium, historical role, amateur status, sign work and workshop division of labour.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把纯艺术家与行业工人分开，再按题材、媒介、历史角色、业余身份、招牌工作与工坊分工细分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand arranges colour on a canvas and flattens colour on a wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一只手在画布上安排颜色，也在墙上把颜色铺平。

branches.en: THE PICTURE MAKER: the artist whose product is an image.
branches.cn: 作画者：产物是一幅图像的艺术家。

branches.en: THE SURFACE COATER: the same agent noun in the building trade.
branches.cn: 表面涂覆者：同一施事名词在建筑行业中的用法。

branches.en: SUBJECT: identity narrowed to what is depicted.
branches.cn: 题材：身份被收窄到所描绘之物。

branches.en: MEDIUM AND HISTORY: the material mastered, then the figure in the catalogue.
branches.cn: 媒介与历史：所精通的材料，然后是图录中的人物。

branches.en: ROLES AROUND THE CRAFT: amateur, sign worker and workshop hand.
branches.cn: 手艺周边的角色：业余者、招牌工与工坊画师。

intro.en: Painter is a verb stem plus the agent suffix -er; the stem's Latin ancestor builds a whole family of images, materials and actions.
intro.cn: painter 是动词词干加施事后缀 -er；其词干的拉丁祖先构成一整族图像、材料与动作词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pictor is the direct model; pingere also yields picture, pigment, depict and pictorial.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pictor 是直接模板；pingere 还给出 picture、pigment、depict 与 pictorial。

items.structure: Old French peindre, from Latin pingere
items.example: She paints in the morning.
items.exampleCN: 她在上午作画。

items.example: Painter follows the pattern of builder.
items.exampleCN: painter 沿用了 builder 的模式。

items.example: The painter signed the lower corner.
items.exampleCN: 画家在下角签了名。

items.example: Painting was her only subject.
items.exampleCN: 绘画是她唯一的科目。

items.example: The sky is handled in a painterly way.
items.exampleCN: 天空以绘画式手法处理。

items.example: The painted cloth hung behind the altar.
items.exampleCN: 画过的布挂在祭坛后。

items.example: The paintwork needs repair.
items.exampleCN: 漆面需要修补。

items.example: The frieze depicts a procession.
items.exampleCN: 壁带描绘一支游行队伍。

items.example: The pigment is ground by hand.
items.exampleCN: 颜料用手工研磨。

items.example: The picture is older than the frame.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画比画框更古老。

definition_zh: 耕种；栽培；（微生物的）培养；修养；培养（能力、关系）
definition_en: the act of tilling land, growing crops or organisms, or developing a quality, person or relationship through sustained care
core_image: 一块被反复翻土、除草、浇水的田，土面松软，作物按行生长，田边放着种子袋与记录本
scene: 田垄被翻得松软，农人蹲下检查幼苗的根系，远处水渠正缓缓放水。 Careful cultivation keeps the seed bed open to air and water.
sceneCN: 这里指「对土地反复翻耕与照管」（第 1 个义项：耕作土地）；句意为细致的耕作让苗床保持通气与水分。

pos.zh: 耕种；栽培；（微生物）培养；修养（多作不可数名词）

derivatives.zh: cultivate + -able（能……的）→ 可耕种的；可培养的
cultivate + -or（施动者或工具）→ 耕作的人；中耕机
cultivate + -ar（名词后缀，二十世纪园艺用语）→ 栽培品种（语义偏移：从动作转为被栽培的品系）
cultivate + -ed（过去分词作形容词）→ 耕作的；有教养的
un-（否定）+ cultivated → 未开垦的；未受教育的
re-（重新）+ cultivate → 重新耕作（语义偏移：荒废之后再翻种）

senses.title: Break and tend the soil
senses.definition: to prepare land by ploughing, digging and weeding so that crops can grow
senses.definitionCN: 通过犁翻、挖掘与除草备好土地，使作物得以生长
senses.example: Cultivation of the heavy clay begins in early spring.
senses.exampleCN: 对这种重黏土的耕作从早春开始。
senses.why: The Latin root colere meant to till and to dwell on land, so the first sense is simply the farmer's work on the soil.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 colere 本义是耕作、居住于土地，因此第一义就是农人对土壤的劳作。

senses.title: Growing a named crop
senses.definition: the raising of a particular crop on prepared land, as in rice cultivation
senses.definitionCN: 在备好的土地上种植特定作物，如水稻种植
senses.example: Rice cultivation requires level fields and steady water.
senses.exampleCN: 水稻种植需要平整的田块与稳定的水。
senses.why: Once land is prepared, the same word names the crop put into it, because the whole cycle counts as one practice.
senses.whyCN: 土地备好之后，同一个词就指种进去的作物，因为整个周期算作一项实践。

senses.title: Raising garden plants or trees
senses.definition: the deliberate growing of ornamental plants, fruit trees or forest seedlings
senses.definitionCN: 有意栽培观赏植物、果树或林木幼苗
senses.example: The cultivation of olives spread along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 橄榄的栽培沿海岸传播开来。
senses.why: The verb extended from field crops to any plant that people tend rather than gather wild.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词从田里的作物扩展到任何由人照管、而非野外采集的植物。

senses.title: Growing microorganisms in a medium
senses.titleCN: 在培养基中培养微生物
senses.definition: the controlled growth of bacteria, cells or tissue in a prepared medium
senses.definitionCN: 在配好的培养基中受控地培养细菌、细胞或组织
senses.example: Cultivation of the sample revealed two distinct bacterial colonies.
senses.exampleCN: 对样本的培养显示出两种不同的菌落。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century microbiology borrowed the agricultural word because a culture dish is a small field where organisms are fed and grown.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的微生物学借用了农业词，因为培养皿就是一块喂养、培育生物的小田。

senses.title: Developing a skill or habit
senses.definition: the gradual development of an ability, habit or quality through repeated practice
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复练习逐步发展某种能力、习惯或品质
senses.example: Cultivation of patience takes longer than learning the rules.
senses.exampleCN: 培养耐心比学会规则要花更长时间。
senses.why: Growing a plant and growing a habit share one shape: small repeated acts of care produce a result that cannot be rushed.
senses.whyCN: 种植植物与培养习惯形状相同：反复的小小照料产生无法催快的结果。

senses.title: Keeping a relationship or contact
senses.definition: the deliberate effort to maintain a friendship, contact or useful connection
senses.definitionCN: 有意维持友谊、联系或有用的关系
senses.example: The diplomat's cultivation of local leaders lasted years.
senses.exampleCN: 这位外交官对当地领袖的经营持续多年。
senses.why: A relationship, like a crop, needs regular attention; neglect is the weed that takes it over.
senses.whyCN: 关系如同作物，需要定期照料；疏忽就是接管它的杂草。

senses.title: Refinement of mind and manners
senses.definition: the refined state of a person's mind, taste or manners, produced by education and good company
senses.definitionCN: 由教育与良好交往造就的心智、趣味或举止上的修养
senses.example: Her cultivation showed in the way she listened before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 她的修养体现在先听完再回答的方式上。
senses.why: The metaphor turns inward: what is tilled is no longer soil but the person, and the harvest is poise rather than grain.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻转向内部：被耕的不再是土壤而是人，收获的也不是谷物而是从容。

senses.title: Guiding a person's growth
senses.definition: the work of developing someone's abilities and character under sustained guidance
senses.definitionCN: 在持续指导下发展某人的能力与品格
senses.example: The older musician's cultivation of young players saved the ensemble.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年长音乐家对年轻乐手的培养拯救了整个乐团。
senses.why: The agricultural image completes itself: a gardener who tends seedlings is a mentor who tends beginners.
senses.whyCN: 农业意象在此闭合：照看幼苗的园丁，就是照看初学者的师长。

intro.en: Cultivation comes from Latin cultura, a tilling or care, built on cultus, the past participle of colere, to till, inhabit or worship. The noun reached English through Middle French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cultivation 来自拉丁 cultura「耕作、照料」，其基础是 colere「耕作、居住、敬奉」的过去分词 cultus。这个名词经中古法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Colere meant to till the soil, to dwell on land and to honour a god; Roman usage treated these as one act of tending. Its deeper root is generally connected with a verb meaning to turn or move around, but that link is a reconstruction.
items.cn: colere 意为耕作土地、居住于土地、敬奉神明；罗马用法把这三者视为同一种照料。它更深的词根一般认为与表示「转动、绕行」的动词有关，但这一联系属重构形式。

items.en: The past participle cultus described land that had been worked and a life that had been ordered; it also named care and worship.
items.cn: 过去分词 cultus 描述被耕作过的土地与被整理过的人生，也指照料与敬奉。

items.en: Cultura named the act of tilling and the care given to a field, a body or a mind; it is the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: cultura 指耕作的行为，以及对田地、身体或心智的照料；它是这个英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: Middle French cultivation carried the learned noun into English in the fifteenth century, first in agricultural and religious writing.
items.cn: 中古法语 cultivation 在十五世纪把这个学术名词带入英语，最初用于农业与宗教文本。

items.en: From the late nineteenth century the word was used for growing microorganisms in a prepared medium, a sense borrowed from the image of a small cultivated field.
items.cn: 从十九世纪后期起，这个词用于在配好的培养基中培养微生物，这一义借自「一小块被耕作的田」的意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the pre-Latin origin of colere is reconstructed rather than attested, and the earliest English use is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：colere 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式，并非有据可查；英语最早用例的年代也只有约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin root that name neighbouring things; group two holds verbs and nouns for the work of raising plants.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词根、指相邻事物的词；第二组是表示「培育植物」这项工作本身的动词与名词。

entries.definition: From the same Latin cultura but naming the whole way of life, arts and beliefs of a group, not the act of tilling.
entries.definitionCN: 同出拉丁 cultura，却指一个群体的生活方式、艺术与信念整体，而非耕作行为。

entries.definition: From Latin cultus, it names a religious system or a devoted following, preserving the worship sense that agriculture dropped.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 cultus，指宗教体系或狂热的追随群体，保留了农业义所丢弃的「敬奉」义。

entries.definition: Latin ager, field, plus cultura: the science and business of farming, broader than the care of one plot.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 ager「田地」加 cultura：农业的科学与产业，比单块土地的耕作更广。

entries.definition: Latin hortus, garden, plus cultura: the art of growing garden plants, narrower than cultivation in general.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 hortus「园子」加 cultura：栽培园艺植物的技艺，比泛指的 cultivation 更窄。

entries.definition: The mechanical working of soil, such as ploughing and harrowing; it stops at the soil and does not cover crops, microbes or manners.
entries.definitionCN: 对土壤的机械作业，如犁耕与耙地；只到土壤为止，不涵盖作物、微生物或举止。

entries.definition: The whole business of raising crops and animals; cultivation is one part of it, the care of soil and plants.
entries.definitionCN: 种植作物与饲养动物的整个产业；cultivation 只是其中一部分，即对土壤与植物的照料。

entries.definition: Care given to something while it grows, especially a child or a talent; it stresses the caring relationship rather than the technique.
entries.definitionCN: 对生长中之物的照料，尤指孩子或才能；强调照料关系而非技术。

entries.definition: The controlled reproduction of plants or animals to select desired traits; cultivation grows them, breeding chooses the stock.
entries.definitionCN: 为选育理想性状而控制植物或动物的繁殖；cultivation 负责栽培，breeding 负责选种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: colere 'to till' plus -ation 'the act': the act of tilling, and then of tending anything else.
normal.cn: colere「耕作」加 -ation「行为」：耕作的行为，随后扩展到照管别的东西。

normal.en: The family runs cultivate, cultivation, cultivator, cultivable, cultivar, cultivated.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cultivate、cultivation、cultivator、cultivable、cultivar、cultivated。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: rice cultivation, shifting cultivation, intensive cultivation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出田间义：水稻种植、轮歇耕作、集约耕作。

normal.en: Laboratory use keeps the field image: a culture dish is a small plot for microbes.
normal.cn: 实验室用法保留田地意象：培养皿就是给微生物的一小块地。

normal.en: The inward sense appears in the fixed phrase cultivation of the mind.
normal.cn: 内向义出现在固定搭配「心性修养」中。

abstract.en: Picture a library where every shelf is a row of seedlings and the reader is the farmer.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，每一排书架都是一行幼苗，读者就是农夫。

abstract.en: Picture a friendship watered once a week, never flooded and never left dry.
abstract.cn: 想象一段每周浇一次水的关系，既不被淹没，也不被晒干。

abstract.en: Picture a violin teacher adjusting a beginner's hand as a gardener ties a young tree to a stake.
abstract.cn: 想象小提琴老师调整初学者的手，如同园丁把小树绑在支柱上。

examples.en: Terrace cultivation holds the soil on slopes that would otherwise wash away.
examples.cn: 梯田耕作保住了那些本来会被冲走的山坡土壤。

examples.en: The cultivation of bacteria requires sterile tools and a controlled temperature.
examples.cn: 培养细菌需要无菌器具与受控温度。

examples.en: His cultivation of the committee's trust made the reform possible.
examples.cn: 他对委员会信任的经营使改革成为可能。

dict_mnemonic.text: cult（耕种、培育）+ -ivation（行为）→ 反复照管让东西长起来；土地、细菌、才能、关系都能被培育，名词就是这一过程。

root: 拉丁 colere「耕作、居住、敬奉」→ cultus「耕过的、受照料的」→ cultura「耕作、培育」→ 中世纪拉丁 cultivatio；colere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: soil is broken, a crop is tended, and the same tending is then applied to microbes, skills, contacts, manners and a pupil.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：先翻土，再照管作物，随后把同一种照管用于微生物、技能、人脉、举止与学生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field is broken, sown and weeded until the soil, the crop and finally the farmer's own mind are all under care.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块田被翻、被种、被除草，直到土壤、作物以及农夫自己的心智都处在照料之下。

branches.en: THE FIELD CYCLE: preparing ground and putting a named crop into it.
branches.cn: 田间周期：先备好地，再把某一种作物种进去。

branches.en: THE GARDEN: the same care applied to plants that are not field crops.
branches.cn: 园圃：把同一种照料用于并非田间作物的植物。

branches.en: THE DISH: a laboratory medium is a small field for invisible organisms.
branches.cn: 培养皿：培养基就是给看不见的生物的一小块田。

branches.en: REPEATED CARE: habits and friendships both grow by regular, unhurried attention.
branches.cn: 反复照料：习惯与友谊都靠规律而不急躁的关注生长。

branches.en: THE INWARD HARVEST: manners and pupils are the last crops, ripened by the same patience.
branches.cn: 内在的收获：举止与学生是最后的作物，由同一种耐心催熟。

intro.en: Cultivation is a Latin noun built from a verb root and a suffix, and both parts also build a large English family, so the word can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: cultivation 是由动词词根与后缀构成的拉丁名词，这两部分还构成一个庞大的英语词族，因此可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin colere supplies cultus, cultura and cultivare; the suffix -ation turns a verb of tending into the name of the work or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 colere 衍生出 cultus、cultura 与 cultivare；后缀 -ation 把表示照管的动词变成工作或其结果的名称。

items.meaning: to till; to dwell; to worship
items.example: The root names the whole act of tending land.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名照料土地的全部动作。

items.example: The participle became a noun for care and worship.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词转为表示照料与敬奉的名词。

items.example: Cultura is the direct ancestor of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: cultura 是这个英语名词的直接祖先。

items.example: Medieval Latin built a new verb from the old participle.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语从旧分词造出一个新动词。

items.meaning: the work of tilling or tending
items.example: The noun names the work and its result.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指工作及其结果。

items.example: The suffix also builds preservation and navigation.
items.exampleCN: 同一后缀还构成 preservation 与 navigation。

items.structure: cultivate + -or (one who acts or a tool)
items.meaning: a person or machine that tills
items.example: The cultivator loosened the rows between the vines.
items.exampleCN: 中耕机松开了藤行之间的土。

items.meaning: able to be tilled or grown
items.example: Only the valley floor is cultivable.
items.exampleCN: 只有谷底可以耕种。

items.example: The cultivated slope held its soil.
items.exampleCN: 这块被耕作的坡地保住了土壤。

items.example: The new cultivar resists mildew.
items.exampleCN: 这个新品种抗白粉病。

definition_zh: 有机的；与生物体有关的；含碳骨架的（化学）；不用化肥农药的（农业）；自然生长而成的
definition_en: relating to living things or to carbon-based compounds, and by extension grown without synthetic chemicals or developed naturally as a whole
core_image: 一棵植物从土壤里长出来，根、茎、叶彼此相连，整株像一件长成的器官而不是拼装的零件
scene: 这些蔬菜不用合成农药和可溶性化肥，摊位上挂着醒目的标签。 Organic vegetables are grown without synthetic pesticides or soluble fertilizers.
sceneCN: 这里 organic 指「有机的（不用化肥农药的）」（第 3 个义项：农业上指以有机方式种植）；蔬菜不用合成农药与可溶化肥。图中可辨识物件：植物、土壤、根茎叶的连通、无化学瓶罐；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 有机食品；有机作物（作名词时多用于复数 organics，或 the organic 指有机农业）
有机的；生物体的；含碳的；有机耕作的；自然演成的

senses.title: Of living things
senses.definition: relating to living organisms or to the structures they build
senses.definitionCN: 与活生物或其构成的构造相关
senses.example: Soil organic matter feeds the whole food web.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤有机物养活了整个食物网。
senses.why: Greek organon named a tool, and a body's tools are its organs; 'organic' therefore starts as 'having organs', that is, belonging to a living body.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 organon 指工具，而身体的工具就是器官；因此 organic 起初意为「有器官的」，即属于活体。

senses.title: Carbon-based chemistry
senses.titleCN: 有机化学义：含碳骨架的化合物
senses.definition: describing compounds built on carbon skeletons, the chemistry once thought to require life
senses.definitionCN: 描述以碳骨架为基础的化合物，这一化学领域曾被以为只能由生命产生
senses.example: Methane is the simplest organic compound.
senses.exampleCN: 甲烷是最简单的有机化合物。
senses.why: because such compounds were first obtained only from living things, the word was carried over to the whole class even after they were synthesized in the lab.
senses.whyCN: 由于这类化合物最初只能从生物得到，即使后来能在实验室合成，这个词仍被沿用到整类物质上。

senses.title: Grown without synthetics
senses.titleCN: 农业义：不用化肥农药的
senses.definition: describing food grown without synthetic pesticides or soluble mineral fertilizers
senses.definitionCN: 描述不用合成农药或可溶矿物肥料的种植方式
senses.example: Organic apples cost more because the orchard yields less.
senses.exampleCN: 有机苹果更贵，因为果园产量更低。
senses.why: the farming sense borrows the idea of a whole living system, treating the soil as something to be fed rather than dosed.
senses.whyCN: 农业义借用「活着的整体系统」这一观念，把土壤当作需要喂养的东西，而不是投药的对象。

senses.title: Grown as a whole, not assembled
senses.titleCN: 演化义：自然生长、整体关联的
senses.definition: describing something that develops naturally as an interconnected whole rather than being assembled from parts
senses.definitionCN: 描述作为相互关联的整体自然发展，而非由零件拼装
senses.example: The firm's growth was organic, not the result of acquisitions.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司的增长是自然生长，而非并购的结果。
senses.why: since the body grows from within, 'organic' also means growth by inner development rather than by outside assembly, and business borrowed that.
senses.whyCN: 由于身体是从内部长成的，organic 也指由内在发展而非外部拼装的成长，商业领域借用了这一层。

senses.title: Of the organs in medicine
senses.definition: describing disease that has a structural change in an organ rather than a purely functional one
senses.definitionCN: 描述器官有结构改变、而非纯功能性的疾病
senses.example: The scan ruled out organic disease of the stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描排除了胃的器质性病变。
senses.why: medicine must separate damage to an organ from symptoms without a lesion, so 'organic' marks the structural case.
senses.whyCN: 医学必须把器官的结构损伤与无病灶的症状分开，因此 organic 标记结构性的那一类。

senses.title: Parts that belong together
senses.titleCN: 结构义：组织上相互关联的
senses.definition: describing a structure whose parts are interdependent, like the organs of a body
senses.definitionCN: 描述各部分相互依赖的结构，如同身体的器官
senses.example: The report describes an organic link between the two agencies.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把两个机构之间的关系描述为有机联系。
senses.why: if organs serve one body, then any set of parts serving one end can be called organic.
senses.whyCN: 如果各器官服务于同一个身体，那么任何共赴一目的的一组部件都可以叫 organic。

senses.title: Foundational law and acts
senses.titleCN: 根本性义：作为根本法规的
senses.definition: describing a basic constitutional document or act, as in organic law
senses.definitionCN: 描述根本性的宪制文件或法令，如「组织法」
senses.example: The status of the territory is set by an organic act.
senses.exampleCN: 该领地的地位由一部组织法规定。
senses.why: a body needs a skeleton, so a state's founding instrument is called organic: it is what the rest is built onto.
senses.whyCN: 身体需要骨骼，因此国家的立国文件被称为「有机的」：其余一切都建在它之上。

senses.title: Whole food, whole system
senses.titleCN: 食品义：作为整体未被拆解的
senses.definition: describing food or a system treated as an intact whole rather than as isolated components
senses.definitionCN: 描述被当作完整整体、而非孤立成分处理的食品或系统
senses.example: The shop sells organics alongside conventional produce.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店把有机产品与常规农产品并排出售。
senses.why: the market turned the adjective into a noun, so 'organics' now names the goods themselves.
senses.whyCN: 市场把这个形容词变成名词，因此 organics 现在指商品本身。

intro.en: Organic comes from Greek organon 'tool, instrument', through Latin organum and the medieval adjective organicus. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: organic 出自希腊 organon「工具、器具」，经拉丁 organum 与中世纪形容词 organicus 而来。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: organon named a tool or instrument, and in philosophy a means of doing something. From it comes the sense of a body part that does work.
items.cn: organon 指工具或器具，也指哲学上达成某目的的手段。由它引申出「做工作的身体部件」这一义。

items.en: Latin borrowed organum for an instrument and, in later use, a musical instrument; the body-part sense developed in anatomy.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 organum 指器具，后亦指乐器；身体部件的义项在解剖学中发展起来。

items.en: Medieval Latin organicus meant 'of an organ' or 'having organs'; English took the adjective in this anatomical sense first.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 organicus 意为「器官的」或「有器官的」；英语先在这个解剖学意义上使用该形容词。

items.en: Around 1800 chemists divided compounds into organic, from living things, and inorganic; urea's laboratory synthesis in 1828 weakened the boundary but the name stayed.
items.cn: 约 1800 年，化学家把化合物分为来自生物的 organic 与 inorganic；1828 年尿素在实验室被合成，动摇了这条界线，但名称保留。

items.en: The twentieth century applied the word to farming that avoids synthetic inputs, treating soil as a living system.
items.cn: 20 世纪把这个词用于避免合成投入物的耕作方式，把土壤当作活系统。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): organon's pre-Greek origin is not established, so any Indo-European form behind it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：organon 在希腊语之前的来源并无定论，其背后的任何印欧形式都是重构，而非有记录的实际词。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Greek stem that name different things; group two holds words often used where organic could be chosen.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊词干、但指不同事物的词；第二组是常与 organic 互换使用的词。

entries.definition: A part of a body or an organisation, not a quality; organic is the adjective describing such a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体或机构的部件，不是性质；organic 是描述这类整体的形容词。

entries.definition: A complete living being; it shares organon but names an entity, not a property.
entries.definitionCN: 指完整的生物体；共享 organon，但命名实体而非性质。

entries.definition: A structured group of people, from the same stem via 'organize'. It names an institution, not a growing whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指有结构的人群，由同一词干经 organize 而来；命名机构，不是生长的整体。

entries.definition: Not built on carbon and not from life; it is the direct opposite in chemistry and farming.
entries.definitionCN: 不以碳为基础、非来自生命；在化学与农业中与 organic 直接相对。

entries.definition: Not made or altered by humans; organic in farming also implies natural methods, but natural says nothing about certification.
entries.definitionCN: 非人力制造或改动的；农业中的 organic 也含自然方式，但 natural 不涉及认证。

entries.definition: Relating to biology or to living processes; it names the science, while organic names a property of matter.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物学或生命过程相关；命名学科，而 organic 命名物质属性。

entries.definition: Good for health or morally sound; organic food is often called wholesome, but the words answer different questions.
entries.definitionCN: 有益健康或品德端正；有机食品常被称 wholesome，但两词回答不同问题。

entries.definition: Arranged by an outside plan; organic growth is the opposite of planned assembly.
entries.definitionCN: 按外部方案安排；organic growth 恰与计划拼装相反。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek organon 'tool': a body's tools are its organs, so organic first means 'having organs'.
normal.cn: 希腊 organon「工具」：身体的工具就是器官，所以 organic 起初意为「有器官的」。

normal.en: The family runs organ, organism, organization, organic, organically, inorganic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 organ、organism、organization、organic、organically、inorganic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: organic matter, organic compound, organic farming, organic growth, organic chemistry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：有机物、有机化合物、有机农业、自然增长、有机化学。

normal.en: Chemistry pairs it with inorganic; farming pairs it with conventional.
normal.cn: 化学中与 inorganic 相对；农业中与常规耕作相对。

normal.en: The business sense is 'grown from within', the opposite of bought through acquisitions.
normal.cn: 商业义是「从内部长成」，与靠并购得来相反。

abstract.en: Picture a plant whose root, stem and leaf all serve one life.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物，根、茎、叶都服务于同一条生命。

abstract.en: Picture a city that grew along its roads instead of being stamped out at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市沿道路长出来，而不是一次压印成形。

abstract.en: Picture a table whose legs are not attached but grown from the same wood.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，桌腿不是装上去的，而是与桌面同一块木料长出来的。

examples.en: Organic matter in the soil holds water between grains.
examples.cn: 土壤中的有机物在颗粒之间持水。

examples.en: Organic chemistry began with compounds isolated from plants and animals.
examples.cn: 有机化学始于从动植物中分离出的化合物。

examples.en: The company preferred organic growth to borrowing for acquisitions.
examples.cn: 公司更愿自然增长，而不是借钱并购。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「有器官（organ）的」——凡活物长成的、含碳的、不用化肥的 → 有机的

root: 希腊 organon「工具、器具」→ 拉丁 organum → 中世纪拉丁 organicus「有器官的」→ 英语 organic；19 世纪扩展为化学义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: a body's parts all serve one life; that image is read as living matter, as carbon chemistry, as chemical-free farming, as growth from within, as structural disease, as interdependence, as a founding law, and as goods sold under that label.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个意象展开：身体的各部分都服务于同一条生命；这一意象依次被读成生命物质、碳化学、无合成投入的耕作、由内生长、器质性疾病、相互依赖、立国根本法，以及以此标签出售的商品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: root, stem and leaf all serving one living whole, with nothing bolted on.
core.cn: 核心意象：根、茎、叶都服务于同一个活的整体，没有一件是外装的。

branches.en: LIVING MATTER: the oldest sense, matter that belongs to a body.
branches.cn: 生命物质：最古老的义项，属于身体的物质。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY: the carbon class, named when such compounds came only from life.
branches.cn: 化学：碳化合物这一类，命名时它们只来自生命。

branches.en: FARMING AND GOODS: soil fed as a living system, and produce sold as organics.
branches.cn: 农业与商品：把土壤当活系统来养，以及作为 organic 产品出售。

branches.en: GROWTH: development from within, borrowed by business for unplanned expansion.
branches.cn: 生长：由内发展，商业借指非计划性扩张。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: organ damage in medicine, interdependent parts, and a state's founding law.
branches.cn: 结构：医学上的器官损伤、相互依赖的部件，以及国家的立国根本法。

intro.en: Organic is Greek organon plus the Latin adjectival ending -icus, kept in English as -ic; the family also uses -ism and -ize.
intro.cn: organic 是希腊 organon 加拉丁形容词词尾 -icus，在英语中保留为 -ic；词族还用 -ism 与 -ize。

latinIntro.en: Latin organum is a borrowed Greek word, and medieval organicus is a Latin formation on it; both are real Latin, though the root is Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 organum 是借自希腊语的词，中世纪 organicus 是在其上形成的拉丁词；二者都是真实的拉丁语，但词根属希腊语。

items.meaning: of organs, of living things; carbon-based
items.example: Organic waste can be composted.
items.exampleCN: 有机废物可以堆肥。

items.example: The farm is organically certified.
items.exampleCN: 该农场获得有机认证。

items.meaning: a body part that does work
items.example: The liver is the largest internal organ.
items.exampleCN: 肝脏是最大的内部器官。

items.example: A single organism can be a whole forest patch.
items.exampleCN: 单个生物体可以是一整片林地。

items.example: The organization rewrote its charter.
items.exampleCN: 该组织重写了章程。

items.meaningCN: 非碳基的、非来自生命的
items.example: Inorganic salts dissolve in the water.
items.exampleCN: 无机盐溶于水。

items.meaning: dead or living material from organisms
items.meaningCN: 来自生物的活或死的物质
items.example: Organic matter improves soil texture.
items.exampleCN: 有机物改善土壤质地。

items.example: Organic chemistry began with natural products.
items.exampleCN: 有机化学始于天然产物。

items.meaning: a small organ of a cell
items.example: The chloroplast is an organelle.
items.exampleCN: 叶绿体是一种细胞器。

latinEntries.structure: organum, organi (n., second declension; Greek loanword)

definition_zh: 复制；重复（实验或研究）；重现（结果）；自我复制；折叠回折（书面古义）；答复（古义）；重复实验中的一次平行试验
definition_en: to make an exact copy of something, or to repeat an experiment or process so as to obtain the same result
core_image: 一枚半透明的模子扣在原件上，压出的纹路与原件分毫不差，连凹痕的深浅都一样
scene: 实验室换了另一批人，却仍照着原来的步骤把同一项研究从头做了一遍。 A second team tried to replicate the study with fresh samples.
sceneCN: 这里指把同一项研究再做一遍，看能否得到一致的结果（第 2 个义项：重复实验）；句意为另一个团队用新的样本重复了这项研究。场景图取象：模子压出的纹路与原件一模一样。

pos.zh: 复制；重现；重复（实验）
自我复制（细胞、遗传物质层面）
（书面）折叠回折；答复（古义）
重复实验中的一次平行试验（统计学用语）

derivatives.zh: 复制；重复实验；自我复制（由动词加表示「行为、过程」的拉丁后缀构成，指动作本身或一次复现）
复制品；仿制品（由拉丁词干加表示「成品」的名词后缀构成，从「折回之物」转为「照原样做出的东西」）
可复制的；可重复的（加表示「能够被……」的形容词后缀，指结果别人也做得出来）
可重复性（在可重复的形容词后加表示「性质」的名词后缀，科学界用来衡量结果能否被他人复现）
复制性的；与复制有关的（加表示「属于、倾向于」的形容词后缀，多用于描述细胞或病毒的复制活动）
复制者；复制装置（加表示「施动者」的名词后缀，指执行复制的主体或仪器）
复制子（分子生物学用语，指能独立复制的一段遗传物质，由复制一词加表示「单位」的后缀构成）

senses.title: Make an exact copy
senses.definition: to produce an exact copy of a thing, so that the copy matches the original in every detail
senses.definitionCN: 精确地复制某物，使副本与原件的每一处细节都相同
senses.example: The workshop can replicate a carved panel that broke off a century ago.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工坊能复制一块一个世纪前断裂的雕花板。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to fold back, and folding a sheet back over its source traces the same line twice.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义为折回；把一张纸沿原样折回叠在源头上，等于把同一条线描了第二遍。

senses.title: Run the study again
senses.definition: to repeat an experiment or study in order to see whether the same result appears
senses.definitionCN: 把一项实验或研究再做一次，以检验能否得到相同的结果
senses.example: No other laboratory could replicate the finding.
senses.exampleCN: 没有其他实验室能重现这一发现。
senses.why: Repeating a procedure is going over it again, which the fold image captures: the same line, drawn a second time.
senses.whyCN: 重复一套程序就是把它再走一遍，折回的意象正好对应：同一条线，再描第二次。

senses.title: Copy itself
senses.definition: to make copies of itself, as genetic material or a cell does before division
senses.definitionCN: 自身制造副本，如遗传物质或细胞在分裂前所做的那样
senses.example: The virus replicates inside the host cell.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒在宿主细胞内自我复制。
senses.why: Molecular biology borrowed the word because a strand that copies itself repeats its own sequence exactly.
senses.whyCN: 分子生物学借用了这个词，因为一条链复制自身时，把自己的序列原样重复了一遍。

senses.title: Carry a result into a new setting
senses.titleCN: 把结果搬到新环境里重现
senses.definition: to reproduce a result, pattern or success in a different place or under different conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在不同的地点或条件下再现某一结果、模式或成功经验
senses.example: The school tried to replicate its reading programme in three rural districts.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校试着把它的阅读课程推广到三个乡村学区。
senses.why: If a pattern holds in a new place, the second case repeats the first like a fold laid over it.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个模式在新地方照样成立，第二个例子就像一层折过来盖住第一个。

senses.title: Copy data to another system
senses.titleCN: 把数据复制到另一套系统
senses.definition: to copy data continuously or on demand from one store to another so that both stay identical
senses.definitionCN: 把数据持续或按需从一个存储位置复制到另一处，使两边保持一致
senses.example: The database replicates every record to a backup server.
senses.exampleCN: 这个数据库把每条记录都复制到备份服务器上。
senses.why: Computing keeps the oldest sense: an exact duplicate kept somewhere else against loss.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域保留了最古老的含义：在别处留一份一模一样的副本，以防丢失。

senses.title: Fold back, as a leaf
senses.definition: to fold back on itself, as a leaf edge, petal or membrane does
senses.definitionCN: 自身向后折转，如叶缘、花瓣或膜片所做的那样
senses.example: The petals replicate at the tip and form a small hood.
senses.exampleCN: 花瓣在尖端向后折，形成一个小小的兜状结构。
senses.why: This is the literal Latin sense, still used in botanical and anatomical description.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语本义，至今仍用于植物学与解剖学的形态描述。

senses.title: Answer, in older usage
senses.definition: to reply or answer, a sense common in older English and in diplomacy
senses.definitionCN: 回答、答复；这是旧时英语与外交文书中的常见用法
senses.example: The envoy replicated that the terms were refused.
senses.exampleCN: 使节答复说这些条件已被拒绝。
senses.why: The same Latin verb also meant to reply, because answering turns the question back toward the asker.
senses.whyCN: 同一个拉丁动词也有答复之义，因为回答就是把问题朝提问者转回去。

senses.title: One repeated run
senses.definition: one of several repeated runs or samples in an experiment, treated as a unit for analysis
senses.definitionCN: 实验中若干次重复操作或样本之一，作为分析时的一个单位
senses.example: Each replicate was measured at a different temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 每一次平行试验都在不同的温度下测量。
senses.why: Statistics turned the verb into a noun for a single repeat among several, so the count could be discussed.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把这个动词变成名词，指若干重复中的一次，好把次数说清楚。

senses.title: Reproduce a work of art
senses.titleCN: 把一件作品照样做出来
senses.definition: to reproduce a painting, object or design as a faithful copy for study, display or replacement
senses.definitionCN: 把绘画、器物或设计照原样复制出来，用于研究、陈列或替换原件
senses.example: Students replicated the fresco on a smaller panel.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们在一块较小的板上复制了那幅壁画。
senses.why: Museums and craftsmen use the word for stand-in copies that carry the look of the original.
senses.whyCN: 博物馆与工匠用这个词指代用品，它承袭了原件的样子。

intro.en: Replicate goes back to Latin replicare, built from re- 'back' and plicare 'to fold'. The chain of form and meaning is clear, though the exact century in which each English sense appeared is less certain.
intro.cn: replicate 可追溯至拉丁语 replicare，由表示「向后」的前缀与表示「折叠」的词根构成。词形与词义的链条清楚，只是各个英语义项出现的确切年代较难确定。

items.en: Replicare meant to fold back, to turn a thing over, and from that to go over something again.
items.cn: replicare 意为折回、翻转某物，由此引申为把某事再过一遍。

items.en: The root plicare also built complicate, explicit, imply, duplicity and supple, all through the image of folding or plaiting.
items.cn: 词根 plicare 还构成 complicate、explicit、imply、duplicity 与 supple，全都经由折叠或编织的意象。

items.en: Because a reply turns a question back to the asker, replicare also took the sense of answering, which English kept as a rare older use.
items.cn: 回答是把问题朝提问者转回去，replicare 因此也有答复之义，英语保留了这一罕见的旧用法。

items.en: The word came into English through learned Latin in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, first describing folded leaves and membranes.
items.cn: 这个词在十五、十六世纪经由学术拉丁语进入英语，最初用来描述折转的叶片与膜片。

items.en: The modern senses of repeating an experiment and of making a copy are nineteenth-century developments, pushed by laboratory practice and printing.
items.cn: 重复实验与制作副本这两个现代义项是十九世纪的发展，由实验室实践与印刷需求推动。

items.en: In the twenty-first century replication became a public word, as whole fields argued over which published results could be reproduced.
items.cn: 二十一世纪，replication 成了公共词汇，因为多个学科都在争论哪些已发表的结果能够被重现。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin folding root or looks close; the second group names the practical acts that stand beside replicate.
note.cn: 第一组或共享拉丁语折叠词根，或字形相近；第二组是实践中与「复制、重复」相邻的说法。

entries.definition: A copy of an object, especially one made to look exactly like the original.
entries.definitionCN: 器物的复制品，尤指外观与原件完全相同者。

entries.definition: The act or process of copying, or a single repeat of an experiment.
entries.definitionCN: 复制的行为或过程，也指实验的一次重复。

entries.definition: To make a second copy; built on the same folding root with the idea of two.
entries.definitionCN: 做出第二份；同用折叠词根，只是取「二」之意。

entries.definition: To make something harder by adding parts; literally to fold everything together.
entries.definitionCN: 因加入部分而变复杂；字面即把所有东西折在一起。

entries.definition: To involve someone in a matter, literally to fold a person into it.
entries.definitionCN: 使人牵连其中，字面即把人折进去。

entries.definition: To produce a copy or to bring a result back into existence, the broad everyday verb.
entries.definitionCN: 造出副本或使结果再次出现，是最宽泛的日常说法。

entries.definition: To make something identical, the plain word that needs no method behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 照原样做出相同之物，最朴素、不含方法意味的词。

entries.definition: To do or say again, without the suggestion of checking a result.
entries.definitionCN: 再做或再说一遍，不含检验结果的意思。

entries.definition: To establish that something is true, the purpose behind repeating a study.
entries.definitionCN: 确证某事为真，正是重复研究的用意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin folding root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁语折叠词根、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Re- means back and plicare means fold, so replicate is literally to fold a thing back onto itself.
normal.cn: 前缀意为向后，词根意为折叠，合起来就是把它折回自身。

normal.en: The folding root also built complicate and imply, so the family is one image with different directions.
normal.cn: 折叠词根还造出 complicate 与 imply，同族词是同一意象的不同走向。

normal.en: Botany still says a petal replicates, using the literal sense of folding back.
normal.cn: 植物学至今仍说花瓣向后折，用的就是折回的本义。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the science: replicate a study, replicate the results, fail to replicate.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出科研用途：重复一项研究、重现结果、未能重现。

normal.en: The noun replicate counts one repeated run, and the noun replication names the whole act.
normal.cn: 名词 replicate 指一次重复，名词 replication 指整个复制行为。

abstract.en: To replicate is to insist that the same thing can happen twice, which is the wager of every experiment.
abstract.cn: 复制就是坚持同一件事能够发生第二次，这正是每次实验押下的赌注。

abstract.en: The second copy is never quite the same object, only the same shape pressed again.
abstract.cn: 第二份从来不是同一个物件，只是同一形状又被压了一次。

abstract.en: A result that cannot be folded back onto itself stays a story rather than a finding.
abstract.cn: 无法折回自身重现的结果，只能算一个说法，算不得发现。

examples.en: Her team replicated the survey in two other provinces.
examples.cn: 她的团队在另外两个省重复了这项调查。

examples.en: A printed page can be replicated down to the grain of the paper.
examples.cn: 一页印刷品能复制到连纸纹都一致的程度。

examples.en: Cells replicate their DNA before they divide.
examples.cn: 细胞在分裂前先复制自己的遗传物质。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑞普利凯特」——把原件照原样再压一遍，压出来的就是副本：复制、重复

root: 拉丁语 replicare「折回、翻转」← re-「向后」＋ plicare「折叠」；同根词有 complicate、explicit、imply、duplicity、supple。古义含「答复」，今义「重复实验」「复制」为十九世纪以后的扩展，各义项确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses trace one fold: an exact copy, a repeated study, a cell copying itself, a result carried to a new place, data copied to a second store, a leaf folded back, an old reply, one repeated run, and a copy of a work of art.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着同一次折叠展开：分毫不差的副本、重复的研究、细胞的自我复制、被搬到新环境的结果、复制到另一处的数据、向后折的叶片、旧时的答复、一次平行试验，以及艺术品的照样复制。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mould pressed onto an original, leaving the same lines in a second material.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚模子扣在原件上，在另一种材料里留下同样的纹路。

branches.en: THE COPY: a second version made to match a thing or a work of art detail for detail.
branches.cn: 副本：照着原物或艺术品逐处做出的第二份。

branches.en: THE REPEATED RUN: the procedure is gone through again, once or several times, to see whether the result holds.
branches.cn: 重复的运行：把程序再走一遍或几遍，看结果是否站得住。

branches.en: THE SELF-COPY: a cell or a strand of genetic material makes its own duplicate.
branches.cn: 自我复制：细胞或遗传物质链制造自己的副本。

branches.en: THE CARRIED PATTERN: a result or success is reproduced in another place and still holds.
branches.cn: 被带走的花样：结果或成功经验在另一处再现而仍然成立。

branches.en: THE FOLD, THE DATA AND THE OLD REPLY: the literal folded leaf, the duplicate kept on another server, and the archaic answer.
branches.cn: 折叶、数据与旧日答复：字面意义上向后折的叶片、存在另一台服务器上的副本，以及古老的答复之义。

intro.en: Replicate is a Latin verb of folding; its parts are still productive in English and its derived nouns carry the laboratory sense.
intro.cn: replicate 是一个表示折叠的拉丁动词，其构件在英语中仍有构词力，派生名词则带上实验室里的含义。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb replicare is the direct source, with the prefix re- and the root plicare visible in related English words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 replicare 是直接来源，前缀与词根在相关英语词中仍看得见。

items.example: The verb carries both the fold and the repeat.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词同时带着折叠与重复两层意思。

items.example: It marks a movement back toward the starting point.
items.exampleCN: 它标出朝起点折返的动作。

items.example: The root supplies the physical image behind the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供词语背后的具体意象。

items.meaning: the act of copying or repeating
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into the name of a process.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把动词变成过程之名。

items.example: The noun names the finished copy rather than the act.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指做成的副本，而非动作。

items.meaning: able to be copied or repeated
items.example: The adjective is central to debates about trustworthy science.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词在关于科学可信度的争论中处于中心。

items.example: The noun names the standard a result must meet.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指结果必须达到的标准。

items.example: Biology uses it for the copying phase of a cell.
items.exampleCN: 生物学用它指细胞的复制阶段。

items.example: The suffix marks the doer or the device.
items.exampleCN: 后缀标出执行者或装置。

latinEntries.meaning: to fold back; to repeat; to reply
latinEntries.example: Latin replicare means to fold back, and later to reply.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 replicare 意为折回，后来又指答复。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb plicare (plic-, plicatum; to fold)
latinEntries.example: Latin plicare means to fold, and gives complicate and explicit.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 plicare 意为折叠，并给出 complicate 与 explicit。

latinEntries.example: Latin re- appears in reducere, to lead back.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 re- 见于 reducere（引回）。

derivatives.zh: 复制；重复实验；自我复制

definition_zh: 机械的；与机器或力学有关的；不加思考的、机械式的
definition_en: relating to machines or to mechanics; also done by habit without thought
core_image: 一组齿轮咬合着转动，其中一枚缺了齿，仍在原处空转，发出规律的咔嗒声
scene: 打开机壳后，一排齿轮仍在咬合转动，其中一枚缺了齿，却还在原处空转。 The lift stopped because a mechanical fault jammed the door, not because of the power cut.
sceneCN: 这里 mechanical 指与机器部件有关的（第 2 个义项：机器部件方面的）；句意：电梯停下是因为机械故障卡住了门，而不是因为停电；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 机械的；力学的；机械式的
机械部件（罕用，复数形式指机械结构）

senses.title: Relating to machines
senses.definition: concerning machines or their parts rather than human or electronic action
senses.definitionCN: 涉及机器或其部件，而非人或电子动作
senses.example: A mechanical clock needs winding once a day.
senses.exampleCN: 机械钟每天要上一次发条。
senses.why: the adjective was built on the Greek word for a device, so its first job is to mark things of that kind.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词建在希腊语「装置」一词上，因此首要作用是标记同类事物。

senses.title: Of a machine's working parts
senses.definition: describing a fault or action that belongs to moving parts, not to power or software
senses.definitionCN: 描述属于运动部件的故障或动作，而非电力或软件
senses.example: The mechanic found a mechanical cause for the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 技工找到了噪声的机械原因。
senses.why: when a system has layers, the adjective isolates the layer of gears, bearings and seals.
senses.whyCN: 当系统分层时，这个形容词专门标出齿轮、轴承与密封件那一层。

senses.title: Belonging to mechanics as a science
senses.definition: concerning the study of forces and motion rather than chemistry or electricity
senses.definitionCN: 涉及力与运动的研究，而非化学或电学
senses.example: The paper sits on the boundary between mechanical and electrical effects.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇论文处在力学效应与电学效应的交界上。
senses.why: the same Greek root names a branch of physics, and the adjective follows it into the classroom.
senses.whyCN: 同一个希腊词根也命名物理学的一个分支，形容词便随之进入课堂。

senses.title: Automatic, without thought
senses.definition: done by habit or rule with no attention behind it
senses.definitionCN: 凭习惯或规则完成，背后没有留意
senses.example: His apology sounded mechanical and convinced no one.
senses.exampleCN: 他的道歉听起来很机械，谁也没被说服。
senses.why: a machine repeats without judging, and human behaviour that repeats without judging borrows the word.
senses.whyCN: 机器重复而不判断，人不判断地重复行为时便借用这个词。

senses.title: Barely varying, routine
senses.titleCN: 几乎不变的、例行公事的
senses.definition: describing a process that repeats identically with no adjustment
senses.definitionCN: 描述一模一样重复、毫无调整的过程
senses.example: The grading was mechanical: same comments, different names.
senses.exampleCN: 那次评分很机械：评语都一样，只是名字不同。
senses.why: repetition without variation is the visible signature of a machine at work.
senses.whyCN: 毫无变化的重复，是机器运转时最显眼的特征。

senses.title: Describing a physical breakdown
senses.definition: used of a failure caused by wear, jam or breakage of parts
senses.definitionCN: 用于因磨损、卡死或断裂造成的失效
senses.example: Mechanical damage is cheaper to prevent than to repair.
senses.exampleCN: 机械损伤预防起来比修理便宜。
senses.why: engineers divide failures by cause, and this adjective labels the cause that lives in the hardware.
senses.whyCN: 工程师按原因给故障分类，这个形容词标记住在硬件里的那一类。

senses.title: Of mechanical advantage
senses.definition: concerning the ratio by which a tool multiplies force
senses.definitionCN: 涉及工具放大力量的比值
senses.example: A lever gives mechanical gain at the cost of distance.
senses.exampleCN: 杠杆以距离为代价换取机械上的增益。
senses.why: the science of mechanics measures how tools multiply force, and that measure carries the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 力学测量工具如何放大力量，这一测量便带着这个形容词。

senses.title: Of reproduction by machine
senses.definition: describing copies made by a device rather than by hand
senses.definitionCN: 描述由装置而非手工做出的复制
senses.example: Mechanical copies of the print are worth far less than the original.
senses.exampleCN: 那幅版画的机械复制品比原作便宜得多。
senses.why: the age of printed multiples made the word a standard label for copies a machine produces.
senses.whyCN: 印刷复制品的时代让这个词成了机器所产副本的标准标签。

senses.title: Of a device's touch and feel
senses.definition: describing switches or keys that act through physical parts
senses.definitionCN: 描述通过实体部件动作的开关或按键
senses.example: She still prefers a mechanical switch for typing.
senses.exampleCN: 打字时她仍偏爱机械开关。
senses.why: users distinguish a real moving part from a touch surface, and the old adjective draws the line.
senses.whyCN: 用户要区分真正的运动部件与触摸表面，旧形容词正好划出这条线。

senses.title: Drawn with instruments
senses.definition: describing technical drawing done with rulers and compasses rather than freehand
senses.definitionCN: 描述用直尺与圆规而非徒手完成的技术制图
senses.example: The old course began with mechanical drawing before design.
senses.exampleCN: 那门旧课程先教机械制图，再教设计。
senses.why: before printing, precision came from instruments, and drawing by instrument took the adjective's name.
senses.whyCN: 在印刷之前，精确来自仪器，用仪器绘图便取了这个形容词的名字。

intro.en: Mechanical comes from Greek mekhane, a device or means, through Latin mechanicus. The adjective first meant belonging to machines and later came to mean unthinking.
intro.cn: mechanical 来自希腊语 mekhane「装置、手段」，经拉丁语 mechanicus 而来。形容词最初指「属于机器的」，后来引申为「不加思考的」。

items.en: Greek mekhane meant a machine, a device or a means of doing something, and mekhos meant a means or expedient.
items.cn: 希腊语 mekhane 指机器、装置或做事的手段，mekhos 指手段或办法。

items.en: The adjective mekhanikos described what belongs to devices or to inventive skill.
items.cn: 形容词 mekhanikos 描述属于装置或属于巧思技艺的事物。

items.en: Latin mechanicus kept the Greek sense and was used of mechanical arts and of engineers.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mechanicus 保留希腊含义，用于机械技艺与工程人员。

items.en: English mechanical first meant of machines and of the science of mechanics, with no hint of dullness.
items.cn: 英语 mechanical 最初指机器与力学，还没有「呆板」的暗示。

items.en: Newtonian mechanics made the adjective the standard label for force and motion, and the noun mechanics followed.
items.cn: 牛顿力学让这个形容词成为力与运动的标准标签，名词 mechanics 随后出现。

items.en: Industry and bureaucracy made repetition visible, and the adjective acquired its modern meaning of acting without thought.
items.cn: 工业与官僚制度让重复变得显眼，这个形容词于是获得「不假思索」的现代含义。

note.en: The first group is the same machine root in other shapes; the second group is the neighbouring words for automatic and machine-made.
note.cn: 第一组是同一「机器」词根的其他形式；第二组是「自动」与「机器制造」的相邻说法。

entries.definition: One who repairs machines; the adjective describes what belongs to machines.
entries.definitionCN: 指修理机器的人；形容词描述属于机器的事物。

entries.definition: The study of forces and motion; the adjective's third sense points to it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究力与运动的学问；形容词的第三个义项指向它。

entries.definition: The assembly of parts that produces an action; the adjective describes such parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生某个动作的部件组合；形容词描述这类部件。

entries.definition: In a machine-like or unthinking way; it tells how something is done.
entries.definitionCN: 以机器般或不假思索的方式；它说明做事的方式。

entries.definition: Working by itself once set going; mechanical stresses the parts, automatic stresses the lack of a hand.
entries.definitionCN: 一旦启动便自行工作；mechanical 强调部件，automatic 强调不需人手。

entries.definition: Done with the hands; it is the direct opposite of mechanical action.
entries.definitionCN: 用手完成的；是机械动作的直接对立面。

entries.definition: Regular and unvarying; routine describes the pattern, mechanical describes the absence of thought.
entries.definitionCN: 规律而少变化；routine 描述模式，mechanical 描述缺少思考。

entries.definition: Stiff and emotionless in manner; a modern synonym for the figurative sense of mechanical.
entries.definitionCN: 举止僵硬而无感情；是 mechanical 比喻义的现代同义说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real Greek root and the real technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实希腊词根与真实技术搭配。

normal.en: Mekhane is a device, so mechanical means device-like before it means unthinking.
normal.cn: mekhane 是装置，所以 mechanical 先表示「像装置的」，再表示「不假思索的」。

normal.en: The family is regular: mechanic, mechanics, mechanism, mechanically.
normal.cn: 词族很整齐：mechanic、mechanics、mechanism、mechanically。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: mechanical failure, mechanical advantage, mechanical repetition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分开义项：机械故障、机械效益、机械的重复。

normal.en: The adverb ends in -ly, and the comparison uses more and most.
normal.cn: 副词以 -ly 结尾，比较级用 more 与 most。

normal.en: It contrasts with manual, which is the hand against the gear.
normal.cn: 它与 manual 相对：一只手对着一个齿轮。

abstract.en: Picture a gear with one tooth missing, still turning because nothing has told it to stop.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚缺了齿的齿轮还在转，因为没人告诉它该停。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that apologises on a schedule, never looking up.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按时间表道歉，从不抬头。

abstract.en: Picture a drawing so straight that the ruler is still visible in the ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一张画得极直的图，墨迹里还看得见尺子。

examples.en: Mechanical wear, not bad code, caused the shutdown.
examples.cn: 造成停机的是机械磨损，而不是糟糕的代码。

examples.en: His replies were polite but entirely mechanical.
examples.cn: 他的回答礼貌，却完全是机械式的。

examples.en: Mechanical drawings from that era still guide the repair shop.
examples.cn: 那个年代的机械制图至今仍指导着修理车间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米（me）卡（cha）你扣（ni-cal）」——米粒卡住你扣动的地方，正是机械出了毛病

root: 希腊 mekhane「装置、手段」→ mekhanikos「装置的」→ 拉丁 mechanicus → 英语 mechanical；力学义随牛顿力学固定，比喻义「不假思索」起于近代工业与官僚重复。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses move from machines to their working parts, the science of mechanics, unthinking habit, routine, breakdown, force ratios, machine copies, the feel of a switch and instrument drawing.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项从机器出发，经过工作部件、力学、不假思索、例行重复、损坏、力比、机器复制、开关手感，最后到仪器制图。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of meshing gears, one tooth missing, still turning and clicking in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排咬合的齿轮，其中一枚缺了齿，仍在原处转动并咔嗒作响。

branches.en: MACHINE AND PARTS: things of that kind, and specifically the moving layer inside a system.
branches.cn: 机器与部件：同类事物，以及系统中运动的那一层。

branches.en: SCIENCE OF FORCE: mechanics as a subject, and the measured gain a tool gives.
branches.cn: 力的科学：作为学科的力学，以及工具提供的可测增益。

branches.en: AUTOMATISM: acting without attention, and repeating without variation.
branches.cn: 自动性：不留神地行动，以及毫无变化地重复。

branches.en: HARDWARE IN THE WORLD: physical breakdown, and the feel of a real moving switch.
branches.cn: 现实中的硬件：实体损坏，以及真实运动开关的手感。

branches.en: MADE BY INSTRUMENT: copies produced by a machine, and drawings produced by a ruler.
branches.cn: 由器械造成：机器生产的复制品，以及用尺规画出的图纸。

intro.en: Mechanical is a Greek adjective ending on a Greek noun; English later added -ly for the adverb and -s for the science noun.
intro.cn: mechanical 是希腊名词加希腊形容词词尾；英语后来又加 -ly 成副词、加 -s 成学科名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin mechanicus is the borrowing that carried the Greek adjective into European languages; the ending -ical reached English through French forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mechanicus 是把希腊形容词带入欧洲语言的借词；词尾 -ical 经法语形式进入英语。

items.example: The noun is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个词族的源头。

items.example: The adjective supplies the ending that English kept.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供英语所保留的词尾。

items.example: The ending marks an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记关系形容词。

items.example: The ending turns the adjective's field into a science.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把形容词所指领域变成一门学问。

items.example: The ending builds the word for an assembly of parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成「部件组合」的名称。

items.example: The adverb describes the manner of action.
items.exampleCN: 副词描述动作的方式。

items.example: Latin used the adjective as a name for a worker.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个形容词用作工人的名称。

items.example: The Latin word for hand is the base of the direct opposite.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语「手」是它的直接对立词的词基。

latinEntries.structure: mechanicus, mechanica, mechanicum (adj., first and second declension, from Greek)

definition_zh: 礁；暗礁；矿脉；（航海）缩帆
definition_en: a ridge of rock, sand or coral near the surface of the sea, a vein of ore in rock, or to shorten a sail
core_image: 海面下一道浅色的脊，浪在它上面碎成一条白线
scene: 帆船驶近浅水区，船长看见船首方向有一道浅色的脊，浪在它上面碎成一条白线。 The captain saw a pale reef breaking the swell ahead of the bow.
sceneCN: 这里 reef 指「接近水面、使浪破碎的岩脊或珊瑚脊」（第 1 个义项：海面下的礁脊）；句意为船长看见船首前方有一道浅色的礁脊正在把涌浪打碎。

pos.zh: 礁；暗礁；礁脉；矿脉
缩（帆）；收帆

senses.title: A ridge of rock near the surface
senses.definition: a line of rock, sand or coral lying close enough to the surface to break waves
senses.definitionCN: 接近水面、足以使波浪破碎的一道岩石、沙或珊瑚脊
senses.example: The captain saw a pale reef breaking the swell.
senses.exampleCN: 船长看见一道浅色的礁脊把涌浪打碎。
senses.why: The core sense is a shape, not a material: whatever lies near enough to the surface to disturb the water is a reef.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是形状而非材料：任何接近水面、足以扰动水流的物体都算 reef。

senses.title: A coral-built reef
senses.definition: a reef whose frame was raised by coral colonies in warm shallow seas
senses.definitionCN: 在温暖浅海中由珊瑚群体抬升出的礁体
senses.example: The reef grew slowly as the coral colonies stacked their skeletons.
senses.exampleCN: 随着珊瑚群体堆积骨骼，这道礁慢慢长高。
senses.why: Coral is the most famous reef builder, so in ordinary use reef often implies coral even when the word does not say so.
senses.whyCN: 珊瑚是最著名的造礁者，因此日常用法中 reef 常暗指珊瑚，尽管词面并未说明。

senses.title: A hazard shown on charts
senses.titleCN: 海图上标出的航行障碍
senses.definition: a shallow reef that endangers ships and is therefore marked on nautical charts
senses.definitionCN: 危及船只、因此在海图上标出的浅礁
senses.example: The reef lies exactly where the old chart shows no depth.
senses.exampleCN: 这道暗礁正好位于旧海图没有标注深度的位置。
senses.why: Navigation cares about depth, so reef becomes a warning category rather than a geological one.
senses.whyCN: 航海关心的是深度，因此 reef 成了警告类别，而非地质类别。

senses.title: A vein of ore in rock
senses.definition: a gold-bearing or mineral-bearing vein running through rock, especially in mining districts
senses.definitionCN: 贯穿岩石的含金或含矿脉体，尤见于采矿区
senses.example: Miners followed the gold reef deep into the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工沿着含金矿脉深入山体。
senses.why: Mining borrowed the image of a long ridge and applied it underground, where the ore also runs in a line.
senses.whyCN: 采矿借用了「长脊」的形象用于地下，因为矿体也呈线状延伸。

senses.title: To shorten a sail
senses.definition: to reduce the area of a sail by folding or tying part of it down
senses.definitionCN: 通过折叠或系扎帆的一部分来减小受风面积
senses.example: The crew reefed the mainsail as the wind rose.
senses.exampleCN: 风起时船员缩了主帆。
senses.why: The verb is a separate nautical borrowing, probably from Dutch; it shares spelling with the rock but not the same origin path.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是另一条航海借词线，可能来自荷兰语；它与岩石义拼写相同，但来源路径不同。

senses.title: The reef knot
senses.definition: a flat knot used to tie two ends of a line, traditionally used when reefing sails
senses.definitionCN: 用来连接两段绳端的扁平结，传统上用于缩帆
senses.example: He finished with a reef knot that would not slip under load.
senses.exampleCN: 他最后打了一个受力也不滑的平结。
senses.why: The knot is named for the sail-reefing job it was used for, so here reef refers to the sailor's action, not the rock.
senses.whyCN: 这种结因其缩帆用途得名，因此这里的 reef 指水手的动作，而非岩石。

senses.title: A barrier, figuratively
senses.definition: an unseen obstacle that suddenly blocks progress
senses.definitionCN: 突然阻挡进展的隐蔽障碍
senses.example: The talks hit a reef of unresolved property claims.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈撞上了未解决的产权主张这块暗礁。
senses.why: A reef is hidden just under the surface and strikes without warning, which is exactly the figurative point.
senses.whyCN: 暗礁藏在水面之下、毫无预警地撞上来，这正是比喻的要害。

senses.title: A surfing wave over rock
senses.definition: a wave that breaks over a shallow rock or coral bottom, producing a steep, fast ride
senses.definitionCN: 在浅岩或珊瑚底上破碎、形成陡而快的浪
senses.example: Surfers prefer the reef because the wave holds its shape.
senses.exampleCN: 冲浪者偏爱这处礁石浪，因为浪形保持得久。
senses.why: Surfing culture names a spot by its bottom, so reef came to mean a particular kind of breaking wave.
senses.whyCN: 冲浪文化用海底类型给浪点命名，于是 reef 也指一种特定的破碎浪。

intro.en: Reef is a Scandinavian borrowing for a sea ridge; the sailing verb is a separate nautical loan, and the mining sense grew from the same ridge image. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: reef 是来自斯堪的纳维亚语、表示海中脊的借词；缩帆动词是另一条航海借词线，采矿义则由同一「脊」的形象发展而来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Rif meant 'rib' and also 'ridge at sea'. Whether the sea sense grew out of the body-part word or from a verb meaning 'to tear' is debated, so the link is probable rather than proven.
items.cn: rif 既指「肋骨」，也指「海中的脊」。海义是由身体部位词发展而来，还是来自某个意为「撕裂」的动词，尚有争论，因此这种联系只是很可能，而非已证。

items.en: The noun enters English in the sixteenth century, first in sailing and charting accounts of northern waters.
items.cn: 这个名词在 16 世纪进入英语，最初见于北方海域的航行与测深记述。

items.en: The verb 'to reef a sail' appears in the seventeenth century and is usually taken as a separate borrowing, probably from Dutch reven; the shared spelling is accidental.
items.cn: 「缩帆」动词出现于 17 世纪，一般认为是另一条借词线，可能来自荷兰语 reven；拼写相同属偶然。

items.en: In the nineteenth century gold fields from Australia to South Africa called a mineral-bearing vein a reef, extending the ridge image underground.
items.cn: 19 世纪，从澳大利亚到南非的金矿都把含矿脉称作 reef，把「脊」的形象延伸到地下。

items.en: Coral reef as a fixed compound spread in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries with Pacific exploration and Darwin's classification.
items.cn: coral reef 作为固定复合词，随太平洋探险与达尔文分类在 18、19 世纪传播开来。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the relation of rif to 'rib' and to 'tear' is unsettled, and the Dutch origin of the sailing verb is a likely reconstruction rather than a documented fact.
