items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：rif 与「肋骨」「撕裂」的关系没有定论，缩帆动词的荷兰语来源也只是较可信的推测，并非有文献确证的事实。

note.en: Group one holds near-identical spellings with unrelated meanings; group two holds shallow-water and shoreline features that are often used as if interchangeable with reef.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写极近而意义无关的词；第二组是常被当作 reef 同义词使用的浅水与岸线地貌词。

entries.definition: A short repeated phrase in music; it is a different word with no path to the sea ridge.
entries.definitionCN: 音乐中反复演奏的短句；这是另一个词，与海中脊无关。

entries.definition: A crack or tear, from a verb meaning to split; it is not reef, and it describes a gap rather than a rise.
entries.definitionCN: 裂缝或撕裂，来自意为「裂开」的动词；它不是 reef，描述的是凹陷而非隆起。

entries.definition: Old Norse rif meant both rib and sea ridge, so rib may be a distant relative rather than a false friend.
entries.definitionCN: 古诺斯语 rif 既指肋骨也指海中脊，因此 rib 可能是远亲，而非纯然的假朋友。

entries.definition: A nautical word for a sailor or a short jacket, tied historically to reefing sails; it is not a reef itself.
entries.definitionCN: 航海词，指水手或短外套，历史上与缩帆有关；它本身不是礁。

entries.definition: A shallow bank of sand or mud that hazards navigation; it is defined by depth, not by coral or rock.
entries.definitionCN: 危及航行的浅沙洲或泥滩；它以深度定义，而非以珊瑚或岩石定义。

entries.definition: A ridge of sand built by currents, often exposed at low tide; unlike a reef it is loose sediment, not rock or coral.
entries.definitionCN: 由水流堆成的沙脊，低潮时常露出；与礁不同，它是松散沉积物，不是岩石或珊瑚。

entries.definition: A ring-shaped coral reef enclosing a lagoon; an atoll is a kind of reef, so the words are related by type.
entries.definitionCN: 围出潟湖的环状珊瑚礁；环礁是礁的一种，两词是类型关系。

entries.definition: A low sandy island on a reef; it is land, while the reef is the submerged structure that supports it.
entries.definitionCN: 礁上的低矮沙岛；它是陆地，而礁是支撑它的水下结构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Reef is a shape word first: a ridge near the surface that makes waves break.
normal.cn: reef 首先是形状词：接近水面、使浪破碎的一道脊。

normal.en: Coral reef, barrier reef, reef flat and reef crest all build on the same ridge image.
normal.cn: coral reef、barrier reef、reef flat、reef crest 都建立在同一个「脊」的形象上。

normal.en: Reef the sails and reef knot belong to the sailor's reef, not to the rock.
normal.cn: reef the sails 与 reef knot 属于水手的 reef 义，与岩石义不同。

normal.en: Gold reef extends the ridge image into mining: a line of ore in rock.
normal.cn: gold reef 把脊的形象延伸到采矿：岩层中呈线状的矿体。

normal.en: Reef as a hazard is hidden just below the surface, which is why it became a metaphor for unseen trouble.
normal.cn: 作为障碍的 reef 藏在水面之下，因此成了「看不见的麻烦」的比喻。

abstract.en: Picture a white line of foam where the sea suddenly shallows.
abstract.cn: 想象海水突然变浅处那条白色的泡沫线。

abstract.en: Picture a line of gold running through dark rock like a ridge under water.
abstract.cn: 想象一条金线穿过暗色岩石，像水下的脊。

abstract.en: Picture a boat talking to the sea by folding its sail.
abstract.cn: 想象一条船通过折叠帆来与海对话。

examples.en: The reef lies a metre below the surface at low tide.
examples.cn: 低潮时这道礁位于水面下一米。

examples.en: They reefed the sails before the squall reached the boat.
examples.cn: 在飑线到达船之前，他们缩了帆。

examples.en: The mine worked a narrow reef of gold-bearing quartz.
examples.cn: 这座矿开采一条狭窄的含金石英脉。

dict_mnemonic.text: reef 读起来像「锐夫」——水下的脊很「锐」，把浪割成白线；记「暗礁」先想那条白线

root: 古诺斯语 rif「海中的脊」，与「肋骨」同形；其与「撕裂」的联系属推测；缩帆义另经荷兰语航海词传入，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shape through different worlds: the rock under the wave, the coral that builds it, the chart that warns of it, the ore vein underground, the sail shortened, the knot tied, the obstacle unseen, and the wave that surfers seek.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一个形状穿过不同世界：浪下的岩脊、造它的珊瑚、标出它的海图、地下的矿脉、缩起的帆、系好的结、看不见的障碍，以及冲浪者追逐的浪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pale ridge just under the water, with a white line of foam above it.
core.cn: 核心意象：水面下不远处一道浅色的脊，上方是一条白色泡沫线。

branches.en: RIDGE AND BUILDER: a shape in the sea, made most famously by coral.
branches.cn: 脊与建造者：海中的一个形状，最著名的制造者是珊瑚。

branches.en: BREAKING WATER: the same shallow top warns sailors and attracts surfers.
branches.cn: 碎浪：同一个浅顶既警告水手，也吸引冲浪者。

branches.en: UNDERGROUND RIDGE: mining moves the line of rock beneath the surface.
branches.cn: 地下之脊：采矿把这条岩石线移到地表之下。

branches.en: SAILOR'S REEF: a separate nautical word for shortening sail and the knot used to do it.
branches.cn: 水手的 reef：另一条航海词义，指缩帆以及缩帆所用的结。

branches.en: HIDDEN OBSTACLE: what is just under the surface strikes without warning.
branches.cn: 隐蔽障碍：藏在水面下的东西毫无预警地撞上来。

intro.en: Reef is a bare noun with no prefix; its family grows by plural, verb endings and compounding.
intro.cn: reef 是没有前缀的单纯名词；其词族靠复数、动词词尾与复合构成。

latinIntro.en: Reef has no Latin source; it is Scandinavian. Latin-based sea words such as coral, marine and littoral are separate borrowings.
latinIntro.cn: reef 没有拉丁来源，属斯堪的纳维亚语；coral、marine、littoral 等拉丁系海词是另外的借词。

items.example: The noun names the ridge itself.
items.exampleCN: 名词指脊本身。

items.example: The strait is full of reefs.
items.exampleCN: 这条海峡布满暗礁。

items.example: They sailed on with reefed sails.
items.exampleCN: 他们缩着帆继续航行。

items.meaning: the act of shortening a sail
items.example: Reefing took only a minute.
items.exampleCN: 缩帆只用了一分钟。

items.example: The reefy channel needs a local pilot.
items.exampleCN: 这条多礁水道需要本地引航员。

items.meaning: a flat knot used in reefing
items.example: Tie the bundle with a reef knot.
items.exampleCN: 用平结把包裹捆好。

items.meaning: the shallow top of a reef

definition_zh: 猎物；受害者；（prey on）捕食、剥削
definition_en: an animal that is hunted and eaten, a person or thing that is exploited, or the act of hunting and feeding on something

scene: 这里指「猎物」。 The herd bunched together at the water hole, easy prey for a patient hunter.
sceneCN: 这里 prey 指「猎物」（第 1 个义项：被掠食者捕杀的对象）；兽群在水坑边挤成一团，成了耐心猎手的现成猎物。图中可辨识物件：羚羊、水坑、狮子、草丛。

捕食；掠夺（通常用于 prey on / prey upon，不单独使用）

senses.title: The hunted animal
senses.titleCN: 猎物：被其他动物捕杀取食的动物
senses.definition: an animal that is hunted and killed by a predator for food
senses.definitionCN: 指被捕食者猎杀取食的动物
senses.example: The hare is the main prey of the mountain fox.
senses.exampleCN: 野兔是山地狐狸的主要猎物。
senses.why: The noun names the losing side of the hunt, defined relative to a predator rather than by species.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名捕猎中失败的一方，它相对捕食者而定义，而不是按物种定义。

senses.title: A person who is targeted
senses.titleCN: 受害者：被强者盯上的个人
senses.definition: a person who is exploited, deceived or harmed by a stronger party
senses.definitionCN: 指被强势方剥削、欺骗或伤害的人
senses.example: Elderly savers were the prey of the fake investment scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 老年储蓄者是这起虚假投资计划的受害者。
senses.why: The metaphor casts exploitation as predation: the victim is selected, isolated and consumed.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把剥削视为捕猎：受害者被挑选、被孤立、被消耗。

senses.title: Bird of prey
senses.titleCN: 猛禽：以捕猎为生的鸟类
senses.definition: a fixed phrase for a hunting bird such as a hawk, eagle or owl
senses.definitionCN: 指鹰、雕、鸮等以捕猎为生的鸟类的固定说法
senses.example: A bird of prey circled the cliff and then dropped toward the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 一只猛禽绕崖盘旋，随后朝谷底俯冲。
senses.why: The phrase freezes prey into a classifier: the bird is named by what it does to others, not by its own taxonomy.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把 prey 固化为分类词：这类鸟按它对别人做什么来命名，而不是按自身分类。

senses.title: Prey on: to hunt
senses.definition: as a verb with on or upon, to hunt and feed on another animal
senses.definitionCN: 作动词并与 on 或 upon 连用，指猎取并取食另一种动物
senses.example: Owls prey on mice and voles after dark.
senses.exampleCN: 猫头鹰天黑后捕食家鼠与田鼠。
senses.why: The verb keeps the old noun inside it: to prey is to act as the party that takes prey.
senses.whyCN: 动词内部保留了旧名词：to prey 就是扮演取走猎物的那一方。

senses.title: Prey on: to exploit
senses.definition: as a verb with on, to exploit or persistently harm vulnerable people or their fears
senses.definitionCN: 作动词并与 on 连用，指剥削或持续伤害弱势者及其恐惧
senses.example: Loan sharks prey on families who cannot get a bank loan.
senses.exampleCN: 高利贷者剥削那些无法从银行获得贷款的家庭。
senses.why: The verb extends from eating to exploiting because both involve a stronger party living off a weaker one.
senses.whyCN: 动词从取食扩展到剥削，因为两者都是强者靠弱者过活。

senses.title: Fall prey to
senses.definition: an idiom meaning to be caught, harmed or deceived by something
senses.definitionCN: 习语，意为被某物抓住、伤害或欺骗
senses.example: Small shops fell prey to the new online discounters.
senses.exampleCN: 小店铺成了新式网络折扣商的牺牲品。
senses.why: The idiom turns the noun into an event: the victim does not merely become prey but falls into it, as into a trap.
senses.whyCN: 这个习语把名词变成事件：受害者不只是成为猎物，而是像落进陷阱一样陷进去。

senses.title: Prey base
senses.titleCN: 猎物基础：可供捕食的猎物总量
senses.definition: in ecology, the total supply of prey available to support a predator population
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中指可供养捕食者种群的猎物总供应量
senses.example: The decline in the prey base thinned the eagle population.
senses.exampleCN: 猎物基础的减少使雕的种群变稀。
senses.why: Management treats prey as a resource stock, so the noun becomes a measurable base rather than a single animal.
senses.whyCN: 管理把猎物视为资源存量，于是这个名词变成可测量的基础，而不是单只动物。

senses.title: Booty, archaic sense
senses.definition: an archaic or literary sense of plunder taken in war or raid
senses.definitionCN: 古旧或书面义，指战争或劫掠中夺得的财物
senses.example: The old poem calls the captured cattle the prey of the raiders.
senses.exampleCN: 那首古诗把被夺走的牛群称作劫掠者的战利品。
senses.why: This is the original Latin sense of praeda, from which the animal sense later narrowed in English.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语 praeda 的原义，动物义是英语后来从中收窄出来的。

intro.en: Prey comes from Old French preie, from Latin praeda 'booty'. French dropped the d, so prey, predator and predation are doublets of one Latin root.
intro.cn: prey 出自古法语 preie，再往上为拉丁语 praeda「战利品」。法语丢掉了 d，因此 prey、predator 与 predation 是同一拉丁词根的双重借词。

items.en: Praeda meant booty taken in war or hunting, and it could already mean the animal seized by a hunter.
items.cn: praeda 指战争或狩猎中夺得的战利品，也已可指猎手捕获的动物。

items.en: Old French preie carried the word north and lost the d between vowels, giving the shape English borrowed.
items.cn: 古法语 preie 把这个词带到北方，并在元音之间丢掉 d，形成英语借入时的形状。

items.en: English prey appears in the thirteenth century. The exact first citation is uncertain, and the spelling settled later.
items.cn: 英语 prey 在 13 世纪出现；确切首见书证存疑，拼写也是后来才固定。

items.en: Predator and predation were borrowed later directly from Latin, so they keep the d that French had dropped. The three words are doublets, not separate roots.
items.cn: predator 与 predation 后来直接从拉丁语借入，因此保留了法语丢掉的 d。这三个词是同一词根的双重借词，并非不同词根。

items.en: The verb prey on developed from the noun in English, first in the hunting sense and later in the sense of exploiting people.
items.cn: 动词短语 prey on 在英语中由名词发展而来，先取狩猎义，后扩展为剥削人。

note.en: The look-alike group contains a true homophone and two same-root relatives; the near-meaning group separates hunted animals, victims and game.
note.cn: 形近组含一个真正的同音词和两个同根词；近义组区分被猎动物、受害者与猎物。

entries.definition: Means to address a deity or to ask earnestly. It sounds identical to prey but comes from Latin precari 'to entreat', a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 意为向神祈祷或恳求。它与 prey 发音相同，却出自拉丁语 precari「恳求」，是不同词根。

entries.definition: The party that hunts. It is the same Latin root with the d restored, and it is the opposite role to prey.
entries.definitionCN: 指狩猎的一方。它是同一拉丁词根、恢复了 d 的形式，角色与 prey 相反。

entries.definition: The act of killing and eating. Prey is what is taken; predation is the taking.
entries.definitionCN: 指杀死并取食的行为。prey 是被取走之物，predation 是取走的行为。

entries.definition: An animal being hunted, often in hunting and literary contexts. It stresses pursuit and is rarely used for plants or microbes.
entries.definitionCN: 指被追猎的动物，多见于狩猎与文学语境，强调追捕，很少用于植物或微生物。

entries.definition: A person or animal harmed by an event or crime. The figurative sense of prey overlaps with it, but victim carries no hunting image.
entries.definitionCN: 指因事件或犯罪受害的人或动物。prey 的比喻义与之重叠，但 victim 不含捕猎意象。

entries.definition: Wild animals hunted for food or sport. Game is a category under hunting law; prey is the ecological role.
entries.definitionCN: 指为食用或运动而猎捕的野生动物。game 是狩猎法中的类别；prey 是生态角色。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: Prey lost the d that predator kept, so the two forms look different but share praeda.
normal.cn: prey 丢了 d，predator 保留了 d，两个形式不同却共享 praeda。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: fall prey to, easy prey, bird of prey, prey on.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：成为牺牲品、容易得手的猎物、猛禽、捕食。

normal.en: Pray is a homophone but not a relative: entreaty, not booty.
normal.cn: pray 是同音词却不是同族词：意为恳求，而非战利品。

normal.en: The ecological pair is predator and prey, and the act between them is predation.
normal.cn: 生态学的一对是捕食者与猎物，两者之间的行为叫捕食。

normal.en: The verb needs on: birds prey on mice, lenders prey on the desperate.
normal.cn: 动词必须带 on：鸟捕食老鼠，放贷者剥削走投无路者。

abstract.en: Picture an antelope lifting its head at the water hole while the grass behind it moves.
abstract.cn: 想象羚羊在水坑边抬头，身后的草丛却在动。

abstract.en: Picture a pensioner signing a form that promises a guaranteed return.
abstract.cn: 想象一位退休老人签下一份承诺保底收益的表格。

abstract.en: Picture an old poem in which cattle are dragged away as booty.
abstract.cn: 想象一首古诗里，牛群被当作战利品拖走。

examples.cn: 鹿先僵住，随后狂奔，但猎物早已被选定。

examples.en: Small firms often fall prey to larger rivals' pricing tactics.
examples.cn: 小企业常常成为大对手定价策略的牺牲品。

examples.en: The prey base in the valley has shrunk since the wetlands were drained.
examples.cn: 湿地被排干后，谷地的猎物基础缩小了。

dict_mnemonic.text: prey 与 pray 同音：猎物在逃命时也在「祈祷」→ prey 猎物

root: 拉丁 praeda「战利品、猎物」→ 古法语 preie（丢掉 d）→ 英语 prey；predator、predation 为同一词根的另一路借词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from one Latin word for booty and split into the hunted animal, the exploited person, the hunting verb and the ecological stock.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从拉丁语「战利品」出发，分化为被猎动物、被剥削者、捕食动词与生态存量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an antelope alert at the water hole, with movement in the grass behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：水坑边警觉的羚羊，身后草丛有动静。

branches.en: RAPTORS AND BOOTY: the bird of prey and the old plunder sense are two layers of the same Latin word.
branches.cn: 猛禽与战利品：猛禽义与古老的劫掠义是同一个拉丁词的两层。

branches.en: EXPLOITATION: the verb harms the weak, and the idiom turns it into an event.
branches.cn: 剥削：动词施加伤害，习语则把它变成一次遭遇。

branches.en: THE VERB: prey on turns the noun into an action that requires a target.
branches.cn: 动词：prey on 把名词变成必须有目标的行为。

branches.en: MANAGEMENT: prey becomes a measurable stock that supports predators.
branches.cn: 管理：猎物变成可计量、供养捕食者的存量。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: hunting supplies the vocabulary for every one-sided harm.
branches.cn: 比喻：捕猎为一切单向伤害提供了词汇。

intro.en: Prey is a short word with a long history: the Latin root is hidden by a French sound change.
intro.cn: prey 是个短词却有长历史：拉丁词根被一次法语语音变化遮住了。

latinIntro.en: Praeda is the root; French dropped the d; the same root returns with the d intact in predator, predation and predatory.
latinIntro.cn: praeda 是词根；法语丢掉了 d；同一词根在 predator、predation、predatory 中带着 d 完整返回。

definition_zh: 植食性的；以植物为食的
definition_en: describing an animal whose diet consists mainly of plants, or a structure adapted to eating plant material
core_image: 一排宽大的臼齿在咀嚼干草，齿面被磨成水平的磨盘
scene: 这里指「植食性的」。 The herbivorous dinosaurs had broad grinding teeth suited to ferns and cycads.
sceneCN: 这里 herbivorous 指「植食性的」（第 1 个义项：以植物为主要食物）；这些植食性恐龙有宽阔的研磨齿，适合吃蕨类与苏铁。图中可辨识物件：臼齿、干草、蕨叶、苏铁。

pos.zh: 植食性的；以植物为食的（比较级 more herbivorous，最高级 most herbivorous）

collocations.zh: 严格植食的；完全不吃动物性食物

senses.title: Plant-eating by diet
senses.titleCN: 植食性：食谱以植物为主
senses.definition: describing an animal whose food is mainly plant material
senses.definitionCN: 描述以植物材料为主要食物的动物
senses.example: Most large mammals on the plain are herbivorous.
senses.exampleCN: 平原上的大型哺乳动物大多是植食性的。
senses.why: The adjective attaches the diet class to a particular animal, so it answers what kind of eater this species is.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把食性类别挂到具体动物上，用来回答这个物种属于哪类取食者。

senses.title: Teeth built for plants
senses.titleCN: 齿型适应：宽平的研磨面
senses.definition: describing dental or jaw anatomy adapted to grinding tough plant fibres rather than shearing flesh
senses.definitionCN: 描述适应研磨坚韧植物纤维而非切割肉类的牙齿或颌部结构
senses.example: The herbivorous jaw is deep and the molars are flat.
senses.exampleCN: 植食性的颌部厚实，臼齿扁平。
senses.why: Anatomy carries the diet: flat grinding surfaces are the physical signature of a plant eater.
senses.whyCN: 解剖结构携带着食性信息：平坦的研磨面就是植食者的物理签名。

senses.title: Gut adapted to fibre
senses.titleCN: 消化道适应：长肠与发酵腔
senses.definition: describing a digestive tract that is long or chambered enough for microbes to break down cellulose
senses.definitionCN: 描述足够长或具有发酵腔、可供微生物分解纤维素的消化道
senses.example: Herbivorous mammals have a caecum or rumen for fermentation.
senses.exampleCN: 植食性哺乳动物有盲肠或瘤胃用于发酵。
senses.why: Cellulose resists ordinary digestion, so the adjective also marks an animal that houses microbes.
senses.whyCN: 纤维素难以普通消化，因此这个形容词也标出体内养着微生物的动物。

senses.title: Herbivorous insects
senses.titleCN: 植食性昆虫：把植物当全部食物
senses.definition: describing insects that feed on leaves, sap, wood, seeds or nectar
senses.definitionCN: 描述取食叶片、汁液、木材、种子或花蜜的昆虫
senses.example: Herbivorous beetles account for much of the damage in the plantation.
senses.exampleCN: 植食性甲虫造成了种植园里的大部分损害。
senses.why: Most animal species are insects, and most of them are plant eaters, so this is the largest herbivorous group on land.
senses.whyCN: 动物物种以昆虫为主，而昆虫大多吃植物，因此这是陆地上最大的植食类群。

senses.title: Strictly herbivorous
senses.titleCN: 严格植食：完全不吃动物性食物
senses.definition: describing a diet with no animal material at all, as opposed to occasional omnivory
senses.definitionCN: 描述完全不含动物性食物的食性，与偶尔杂食相对
senses.example: The species is strictly herbivorous and will not take carrion.
senses.exampleCN: 该物种严格植食，不会取食腐肉。
senses.why: The adverb matters because many herbivores occasionally eat insects, which blurs the boundary with omnivory.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词很重要，因为许多植食动物偶尔吃昆虫，从而模糊了与杂食的边界。

senses.title: Herbivorous dinosaurs
senses.titleCN: 植食恐龙：古生物中的取食类群
senses.definition: describing extinct reptiles identified as plant eaters from teeth, gut contents or coprolites
senses.definitionCN: 描述依据牙齿、胃内容物或粪化石判定为植食的已灭绝爬行动物
senses.example: Herbivorous dinosaurs ranged from low browsers to high-reaching sauropods.
senses.exampleCN: 植食恐龙从低处啃食者一直分布到高处的蜥脚类。
senses.why: Palaeontology uses the adjective for fossil taxa whose diet must be inferred rather than observed.
senses.whyCN: 古生物学把这个形容词用于食性只能推断、无法直接观察的化石类群。

senses.title: Marine plant eaters
senses.titleCN: 海洋植食：吃海草与藻类
senses.definition: describing aquatic animals that graze seagrass, macroalgae or epilithic algae
senses.definitionCN: 描述啃食海草、大型藻类或附着藻类的水生动物
senses.example: Herbivorous fish keep the reef free of smothering algae.
senses.exampleCN: 植食性鱼类让礁体免于被藻类覆盖。
senses.why: Reef health depends on these grazers, so the adjective becomes a management label.
senses.whyCN: 礁体健康依赖这些啃食者，因此这个形容词也成了管理标签。

senses.title: Figurative and dietary use
senses.titleCN: 比喻与饮食用法：温和或素食
senses.definition: used informally of a person's plant-based diet, or humorously of a mild, non-aggressive temperament
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指个人的植物性饮食，或戏谑地指温和、不具攻击性的性情
senses.example: He describes himself as herbivorous but still eats fish.
senses.exampleCN: 他自称植食，不过仍吃鱼。
senses.why: The adjective softens a dietary choice into a temperament metaphor, which is why it appears in casual writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把饮食选择软化成一种性情比喻，因此常见于随笔。

intro.en: Herbivorous is the Latin adjective herbivorus, built from herba 'grass' and vorare 'devour', and it predates the English noun herbivore.
intro.cn: herbivorous 是拉丁形容词 herbivorus，由 herba「草」与 vorare「吞食」构成，其出现早于英语名词 herbivore。

items.en: Herba covered grass and green plants generally, not only culinary herbs.
items.cn: herba 泛指草与绿色植物，不只是烹饪用的香草。

items.en: Vorare meant to swallow or devour, and the adjective -vorus 'eating' was used in compounds such as carnivorus.
items.cn: vorare 意为吞咽、吞食，形容词成分 -vorus「吃……的」用于 carnivorus 这类复合词。

items.en: Herbivorus belongs to modern scientific Latin, where diet adjectives were formed freely from Latin roots. Its exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: herbivorus 属近代科学拉丁语，这类食性形容词可由拉丁词根自由构成；确切首用存疑。

items.en: English adopted herbivorous in the nineteenth century alongside the noun. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在 19 世纪与名词同时期采用 herbivorous；确切首见书证存疑。

items.en: The same pattern produced carnivorous, omnivorous, insectivorous and frugivorous, so the ending -ivorous became a productive classifier.
items.cn: 同一模式造出 carnivorous、omnivorous、insectivorous、frugivorous，词尾 -ivorous 因而成为能产的分类成分。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vorous ending; the near-meaning group separates plant eating from related but narrower labels.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -vorous 结尾；近义组把植食与更窄的相关标签区分开。

entries.definition: The animal itself. It cannot modify another noun, so a plant-eating dinosaur is a herbivorous dinosaur, not a herbivore dinosaur.
entries.definitionCN: 指动物本身。它不能修饰其他名词，因此应说 herbivorous dinosaur，而不是 herbivore dinosaur。

entries.definition: Describes a flesh diet. The stem caro- 'flesh' is the only difference, and the two adjectives mark opposite diets.
entries.definitionCN: 描述食肉。词干 caro-「肉」是唯一差别，两个形容词标示相反的食性。

entries.definition: Describes a mixed diet of plants and animals. The stem omni- 'all' widens the diet beyond herbivorous.
entries.definitionCN: 描述植物与动物混合的食性。词干 omni-「全部」把食性拓宽到植食之外。

entries.definition: Describes a diet of leaves specifically. It is narrower than herbivorous, which also covers grass, fruit and seeds.
entries.definitionCN: 描述专食树叶的食性。它比 herbivorous 更窄，后者还包括草、果实与种子。

entries.definition: Describes a diet of grasses and cereals. It is a rare technical term, narrower than herbivorous.
entries.definitionCN: 描述以禾草与谷物为食。它是罕见的技术词，比 herbivorous 更窄。

entries.definition: A transparent compound meaning the same as herbivorous but without the scientific register.
entries.definitionCN: 透明的复合词，含义与 herbivorous 相同，但不带科学语域。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实后缀、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: herba 'grass' + -vorous 'eating': eating grass and plants.
normal.cn: herba「草」+ -vorous「吃……的」：吃草与植物。

normal.en: Swap the stem to change the diet: herbi-, carni-, omni-, insecti-, frugi-.
normal.cn: 换词干就换食性：herbi-、carni-、omni-、insecti-、frugi-。

normal.en: Typical phrases: herbivorous animal, herbivorous dinosaur, herbivorous insect, strictly herbivorous.
normal.cn: 典型搭配：植食动物、植食性恐龙、植食性昆虫、严格植食。

normal.en: Flat molars and a fermentation chamber are the anatomical tells of this adjective.
normal.cn: 扁平臼齿与发酵腔是这个形容词的解剖学线索。

normal.en: The noun is herbivore and the process is herbivory; keep the three forms apart.
normal.cn: 名词是 herbivore，过程是 herbivory；三种形式要分清。

abstract.en: Picture molars grinding dry grass into a flat paste.
abstract.cn: 想象臼齿把干草磨成扁平的糊。

abstract.en: Picture a caterpillar stripping a leaf down to its veins.
abstract.cn: 想象毛虫把一片叶子啃到只剩叶脉。

abstract.en: Picture a fish scraping algae off coral so the coral can still see light.
abstract.cn: 想象一条鱼把藻类从珊瑚上刮掉，让珊瑚仍能见到光。

examples.en: The fossil's flat molars mark it as herbivorous.
examples.cn: 这块化石的扁平臼齿表明它是植食性的。

examples.en: Herbivorous insects remove a large share of the canopy each summer.
examples.cn: 每年夏天，植食性昆虫带走大量树冠叶片。

examples.en: The lake's herbivorous fish keep the water clear of algae.
examples.cn: 湖中的植食性鱼类让水体免于藻类覆盖。

dict_mnemonic.text: herbivore（食草动物）+ ous（……的）→ 食草的 → herbivorous 植食性的

root: 拉丁 herba「草」+ vorare「吞食」→ 科学拉丁语 herbivorus「吃植物的」→ 英语 herbivorous。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply one adjective to diet, teeth, gut, insects, strictness, fossils, reefs and casual talk.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个形容词用于食性、牙齿、消化道、昆虫、严格程度、化石、礁体与口语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: flat molars grinding dry grass into paste.
core.cn: 核心意象：扁平臼齿把干草磨成糊。

branches.en: DIET: the base sense says the food is plant material.
branches.cn: 食性：基本义说食物是植物材料。

branches.en: ANATOMY: teeth and gut carry the diet in bone and tissue.
branches.cn: 解剖：牙齿与消化道把食性写进骨骼与组织。

branches.en: SCOPE: insects dominate the class, and strictness separates it from omnivory.
branches.cn: 范围：昆虫在这一类中占主导，严格程度则把它与杂食分开。

branches.en: APPLIED FIELDS: palaeontology infers it from fossils, reef management relies on it.
branches.cn: 应用领域：古生物学从化石推断它，礁体管理依赖它。

branches.en: DRIFT: the adjective becomes a gentle metaphor for diet and temperament.
branches.cn: 漂移：这个形容词成为饮食与性情的温和比喻。

intro.en: Herbivorous is a Latin adjective whose ending -vorous is a productive classifier in zoology.
intro.cn: herbivorous 是拉丁形容词，其结尾 -vorous 在动物学中是能产的分类成分。

latinIntro.en: Herba is the plant, vorare the eating, and -vorus the adjectival form of the eating verb.
latinIntro.cn: herba 是植物，vorare 是吃，-vorus 是吃的动词的形容词形式。

items.example: The lizard is entirely herbivorous.
items.exampleCN: 这种蜥蜴完全植食。

items.example: Each herbivore has its preferred grass.
items.exampleCN: 每种植食动物都有偏好的草。

items.example: Herbivory varies with leaf toughness.

items.example: Carnivorous plants trap insects.
items.exampleCN: 食肉植物会捕获昆虫。

items.example: Omnivorous birds take grain and grubs.
items.exampleCN: 杂食鸟类既吃谷物也吃幼虫。

items.example: Insectivorous bats hunt after dusk.
items.exampleCN: 食虫蝙蝠入夜后捕食。

items.example: Frugivorous birds spread the seeds.
items.exampleCN: 食果鸟类传播种子。

items.meaning: a plant valued for food or medicine
items.meaningCN: 用于食物或药物的植物
items.example: The herb grows in damp shade.
items.exampleCN: 这种草本长在潮湿的荫处。

items.example: The larvae are voracious.
items.exampleCN: 这些幼虫非常贪食。

definition_en: to force something out with a sudden push; to make a person leave a place
core_image: 驾驶舱红灯闪起，飞行员双手拉下座椅上方的拉环，座舱盖先飞出去，座椅带着人向上冲出；光驱托盘「咔」一声弹出一半；旧弹壳从枪膛侧面抛出一道弧线

senses.title: To throw out
senses.definition: to force something out with a sudden push
senses.definitionCN: （动词）用突然的推力把东西弄出去
senses.example: Press the small key and the drive will eject the disc halfway.
senses.exampleCN: 按下那个小键，光驱就会把光盘弹出一半。
senses.why: A drive tray pushed half open with a disc resting on its lip.
senses.whyCN: 光驱托盘被推出一半，一张光盘搁在托盘边上。

senses.title: To expel a person
senses.definition: to force a person to leave a place or a group
senses.definitionCN: （动词）强迫某人离开某地或某团体
senses.example: The stewards moved in to eject the man who had climbed onto the pitch.
senses.exampleCN: 安保人员上前把那个爬进球场的男子赶了出去。

senses.title: To escape from a cockpit
senses.definition: to leave an aircraft by means of an explosive seat
senses.definitionCN: （动词）借助爆炸座椅离开飞机
senses.example: The pilot had to eject before the aircraft hit the ridge.

senses.why: A red warning light in a cockpit with two hands pulling a loop above the seat.
senses.whyCN: 驾驶舱里红色警示灯亮着，双手正拉下座椅上方的拉环。

intro.en: Eject is Latin ejectus, thrown out, from ejicere, which joins ex- meaning out to jacere meaning to throw; the same ject- root gives reject, inject and project.
intro.cn: eject 就是拉丁语 ejectus（被扔出的），来自 ejicere，它把 ex-（向外）与 jacere（投掷）结合；同一个 ject- 词根给出 reject、inject 与 project。

items.en: Latin jacere means to throw.
items.cn: 拉丁语 jacere 意为投掷。

items.en: Adding ex- gives ejicere, to throw out.
items.cn: 加 ex- 构成 ejicere，意为扔出去。

items.en: The participle ejectus means thrown out.
items.cn: 分词 ejectus 意为被扔出的。

items.en: English took eject in the 15C for throwing out or expelling.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪借用 eject，指扔出或驱逐。

items.en: Machines gave eject the sense of pushing a part out automatically.
items.cn: 机器使 eject 有了自动把部件推出来的意思。

items.en: Ejection seats made eject the standard word for escaping a cockpit.
items.cn: 弹射座椅使 eject 成为逃离座舱的标准用词。

note.en: Eject, reject and inject share ject-, the Latin root for throw; the prefix says out, back or in.
note.cn: eject、reject 与 inject 共用 ject-，那是拉丁语「投掷」的词根；前缀说明是向外、向后还是向内。

dict_mnemonic.text: eject ＝ e-（向外，ex- 在 j 前的变体）＋ ject（投掷，拉丁 jacere）＝「往外扔」。ject- 这一家全靠前缀定方向：e-（外）→ eject 弹出／驱逐、ejection 弹出、ejector 弹射器；re-（回）→ reject 扔回去＝拒绝；in-（内）→ inject 打进去＝注射；pro-（前）→ project 往前投＝投射／项目；de-（下）→ deject 使沮丧；ob-（对着）→ object 扔回去反对＝物体／反对。三个常用场景记住就够：机器 eject a disc 弹出光盘，安保 eject a troublemaker 把人赶出去，飞行员 eject 弹射逃生。名词「弹射座椅」是 ejection seat。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）＋ jacere（投掷）→ ejicere → ejectus（被扔出的）→ eject（弹出；驱逐）

definition_en: a large shapeless body of matter, a great quantity of it, or the amount of matter in a body
core_image: 一盆揉好的面团被两只手按下去，整团摊在案板上，越揉越沉
scene: 面粉加水和成一大团，摊在案板上占了半张台面，两只手按下去要费点力。 A mass of dough filled the whole board.
sceneCN: 这里 mass 指没有定形、聚成整体的一大团东西（第 1 个义项：不分形状的团块）；句意：一大团面团占满了整块案板。图中可辨识物件：面团、案板、面粉袋、擀面杖；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A shapeless lump
senses.definition: a body of matter with no clear shape, often formed by pressing things together
senses.definitionCN: 没有明确形状的一团物质，常由挤压而成
senses.example: A mass of dough filled the whole board.
senses.exampleCN: 一大团面团占满了整块案板。
senses.why: Latin massa meant a lump of dough or metal, so the shapeless lump is the root picture of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 massa 指面团或金属的一团，因此「无定形的一团」是这个词的根源画面。

senses.title: A very large quantity
senses.definition: a great number or amount of things taken together
senses.definitionCN: 许多事物合在一起所形成的大数量
senses.example: A mass of evidence supports the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 大量证据支持这一主张。
senses.why: a lump is many small pieces pressed into one, so the word naturally shifted from one lump to a heap of things.
senses.whyCN: 一团是许多小块压在一起，于是这个词自然从「一团」滑到「一堆」。

senses.title: Quantity of matter in physics
senses.definition: the quantity of matter in a body, measured by its resistance to acceleration
senses.definitionCN: 物体所含物质的量，以其抵抗加速度的程度来量度
senses.example: Mass is not the same as weight, though scales blur the two.
senses.exampleCN: 质量与重量并不相同，尽管秤常把两者混在一起。
senses.why: physicists needed a word for how much stuff a body contains, and the lump word was the obvious choice.
senses.whyCN: 物理学家需要指称一个物体含有多少实体，那团东西的词自然是首选。

senses.title: The common people
senses.definition: the ordinary people of a society, considered as one body
senses.definitionCN: 社会中的普通人，被当作一个整体来看
senses.example: The reform was popular with the masses but not with the owners.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革受大众欢迎，却不受业主欢迎。
senses.why: crowds pressed together in a square look like one lump, and politics named that lump the masses.
senses.whyCN: 广场上挤在一起的人群看上去就是一团，政治语言把这团叫作「大众」。

senses.title: The religious service
senses.definition: the central service of the Roman Catholic Church, especially one said for the dead
senses.definitionCN: 罗马天主教会的主要礼仪，尤指为亡者举行的那一场
senses.example: They attended early Mass on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们星期天参加了清早的弥撒。
senses.why: this sense comes from Latin missa 'dismissal', a different source from massa, and must never be merged with the lump word.
senses.whyCN: 这一义出自拉丁 missa「遣散」，与 massa 不同源，绝不能与「团块」那个词混为一谈。

senses.title: To gather in a crowd
senses.definition: to come together in large numbers, as troops or protesters do
senses.definitionCN: 以大量人数聚拢，如军队或抗议者
senses.example: Troops massed along the border overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 部队一夜之间集结在边境一带。
senses.why: if a mass is many units pressed into one body, then to mass is the act of pressing them together.
senses.whyCN: 既然 mass 是许多单位压成一个整体，那么动词 mass 就是把它们压到一起的动作。

senses.title: Large-scale, for everyone
senses.definition: produced or done on a large scale and aimed at ordinary people
senses.definitionCN: 以大规模制作或进行、面向普通人的
senses.example: Mass production brought the clock within reach of clerks.
senses.exampleCN: 大批量生产让职员也买得起钟表。
senses.why: the adjective turns the lump into a scale word: one lump, then one industry serving a whole market.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把「一团」变成尺度词：先是一团，再是整个服务一方市场的产业。

senses.title: The bulk or greater part
senses.definition: the greater part of something, considered as one undifferentiated body
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的较大部分，被看作一个未加区分的整体
senses.example: The mass of the population lives along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 人口的大部分住在沿海一带。
senses.why: a lump is undivided, so the word also covers the majority when nobody bothers to split it up.
senses.whyCN: 一团是不加分割的，因此当没人去细分时，这个词也指「大多数」。

intro.en: Mass in the sense of a lump comes from Latin massa, generally thought to come from Greek maza 'barley cake'. The church sense comes from Latin missa 'dismissal' and is a separate word.
intro.cn: 「团块」义的 mass 来自拉丁 massa，一般认为源自希腊 maza「大麦饼」；弥撒义来自拉丁 missa「遣散」，是另一个词。

items.en: Maza meant a barley cake or a lump of kneaded dough, and it is generally thought to be the older source behind Latin massa.
items.cn: maza 指大麦饼或揉成团的面，一般认为它是拉丁 massa 更早的来源。

items.en: Massa meant a lump, a mass of metal or dough; the further link to Greek maza is a common view rather than a documented chain.
items.cn: massa 指一团、一块金属或面团；它与希腊 maza 的联系是常见看法，而非有文献可查的链条。

items.en: Missa meant 'dismissal' and became the name of the church service; it has nothing to do with massa and must be kept apart.
items.cn: missa 意为「遣散」，后来成为礼拜仪式的名称；它与 massa 毫无关系，必须分开。

items.en: Both words entered English in the Middle Ages, the lump word through French and the church word through the liturgy.
items.cn: 两个词都在中世纪进入英语：团块义经法语而来，礼仪义经教会用语而来。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the lump word was narrowed by physics to the measurable quantity of matter in a body.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，物理学把「团块」词收窄为物体中可量度的物质的量。

items.en: The first dates for the political and industrial senses are approximate; both words are well attested from the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 政治义与工业义的最早年代为约数；两个词在中世纪都已有充分书证。

note.en: The first group holds forms built on massa plus two near-forms, one of which is famously a different word; the second group holds quantity words.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 massa 的词形，另加一个形近但著名地属于另一个词的词；第二组是表示数量的词。

entries.definition: Built on mass with an adjective suffix, meaning 'huge and solid'; it describes the lump rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 在 mass 上加形容词后缀构成，意为「巨大而结实的」；它描述那团东西而不命名它。

entries.definition: A compact group of mountains, from French massif and the same massa stock; it is a shaped lump of rock.
entries.definitionCN: 指紧凑的一群山，出自法语 massif 与同一 massa 词源；它是被塑造过的一团岩石。

entries.definition: From French amasser, built on masse; to heap things into one lump, usually wealth or evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 出自法语 amasser，由 masse 构成；把东西堆成一团，通常指财富或证据。

entries.definition: The volume or the greater part of something; mass stresses the stuff, bulk stresses the size it takes up.
entries.definitionCN: 指体积或较大部分；mass 强调那团实体，bulk 强调它占的空间。

entries.definition: A pile of separate things stacked up; a mass can be one continuous body, a heap is always many pieces.
entries.definitionCN: 分开的东西堆成一摞；mass 可以是一个连续的整体，heap 永远是许多件。

entries.definition: A large number of people gathered together; the phrase for the masses is a political body, not a crowd in a street.
entries.definitionCN: 聚在一起的一大群人；「大众」是政治意义上的整体，不是街上的一群人。

entries.definition: The force of gravity on a body; mass is how much matter it holds, weight is how hard gravity pulls it.
entries.definitionCN: 重力对物体施加的力；mass 是所含物质的量，weight 是重力拉它的力度。

entries.definition: More than half of a counted group; the bulk phrase means an unsplit body, not a tally.
entries.definitionCN: 被计数群体中过半的部分；而「人口的大部分」是不加细分的整体，不是点数结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin source, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁来源、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin massa was a lump of dough, so mass begins as a shapeless lump.
normal.cn: 拉丁 massa 是一团面，因此 mass 最初就是无定形的一团。

normal.en: The family runs mass, massive, massively, massless and biomass.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mass、massive、massively、massless 与 biomass。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale sense: mass media, mass production, mass market.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出规模义：大众传媒、大批量生产、大众市场。

normal.en: Physics pairs mass with weight, and the two are not interchangeable.
normal.cn: 物理把 mass 与 weight 配对，二者不能互换。

normal.en: Remember that Mass the service comes from Latin missa, not from massa.
normal.cn: 要记住弥撒义的 Mass 出自拉丁 missa，而非 massa。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd in a square pressing into one single dark shape from above.
abstract.cn: 从高处看，广场上的人群挤成一个黑色整体。

abstract.en: Picture a snowball rolling downhill and growing heavier with every turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一个雪球滚下山坡，每转一圈就更沉一些。

abstract.en: Picture a baker's hands pushing a whole table of dough into one lump.
abstract.cn: 想象面包师把整张台面的面按成一团。

examples.en: The nebula contains a mass of gas several times that of the sun.
examples.cn: 这团星云所含气体的质量是太阳的若干倍。

examples.en: Mass tourism has changed the old harbour beyond recognition.
examples.cn: 大众旅游把这个老港口改变得面目全非。

examples.en: Protesters massed outside the hall before the vote.
examples.cn: 表决之前，抗议者在大厅外集结。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马死」——一大群马挤成一团，马死了也堆成一大堆 → 团块、大量

root: 希腊 maza「大麦饼、面团」→ 拉丁 massa「一团、一块」→ 法语 masse → 英语 mass「团块、大量」；物理学再收窄为「质量」；弥撒义的 Mass 另出拉丁 missa「遣散」，与此无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all begin with one lump: dough on a board, a heap of evidence, a measured quantity in physics, a crowd pressed into one body, the bulk of a population, the act of pressing a crowd together, an industry serving everyone, and an unsplit majority.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一团东西出发：案板上的面团、一堆证据、物理里可量度的量、挤成一个整体的人群、人口的大部分、把人挤到一起的动作、服务所有人的产业，以及不加细分的多数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lump of dough pressed flat across a whole board.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团面被按平，摊满整块案板。

branches.en: THE LUMP AND THE HEAP: one continuous body first, then many pieces pressed into a great quantity.
branches.cn: 一团与一堆：先是连续的一体，再是许多件压成大数量。

branches.en: THE MEASURED LUMP: physics turns the lump into a number that resists acceleration.
branches.cn: 可量度的团：物理学把这团东西变成一个抵抗加速度的数。

branches.en: PEOPLE AS ONE BODY: a crowd pressed together becomes the masses, and an unsplit bulk becomes the majority.
branches.cn: 被当作一体的民众：挤在一起的人群成为大众，未加细分的整体成为多数。

branches.en: THE OTHER WORD: the church service sounds the same but descends from missa, a root of its own.
branches.cn: 另一个词：宗教礼仪读音相同，却出自 missa，自有一个词根。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE SCALE: pressing things together, and an industry that serves a whole market.
branches.cn: 动作与尺度：把东西压到一起，以及服务整个市场的产业。

intro.en: Mass is a Latin noun of a lump, with a small English family built on it; the church word Mass is a separate stock and is marked as such.
intro.cn: mass 是拉丁语里表示「一团」的名词，英语在其上长出一个不大的词族；弥撒义的 Mass 另有来源，下面单独标出。

latinIntro.en: Latin massa gives mass, massive, massif and amass through French; missa is a different Latin noun and gives only the church sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 massa 经法语给出 mass、massive、massif 与 amass；missa 是另一个拉丁名词，只给出礼仪义。

items.meaning: lump; mass of metal or dough
items.meaningCN: 一团；金属或面团的一块
items.example: The root supplies the picture of a shapeless lump.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「无定形一团」的画面。

items.example: One word covers the lump, the heap and the measured quantity.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词兼指团块、堆与可量度的量。

items.example: A massive wall is one great lump of stone.
items.exampleCN: 一堵厚墙就是一大团石头。

items.example: The massif rises as one block from the plain.
items.exampleCN: 那片山地从平原上整块隆起。

items.example: To amass is to press many things into one heap.
items.exampleCN: amass 就是把许多东西压成一堆。

items.meaning: the total living matter in an area
items.meaningCN: 某一区域内的生物总量
items.example: The prefix narrows the lump to living stuff.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把这团东西限定为活物。

items.example: The compound turns the lump into a sales scale.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把「一团」变成销售的尺度。

items.structure: Latin noun, first declension, separate source
items.example: This root is not related to massa in any way.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根与 massa 没有任何关系。

definition_zh: 谷类作物；谷物；（英式）谷物早餐
definition_en: a grass grown for its edible grain, the grain itself, or a breakfast food made from such grain
core_image: 早餐桌上的一碗燕麦片，旁边放着麦穗与一袋面粉，三样东西都来自同一种草
scene: 厨房台面上摆着一碗泡了牛奶的燕麦片，旁边是一束干麦穗和一袋面粉。 Cereal crops cover more land than any other food group.
sceneCN: 这里指「谷类作物」（第 1 个义项：作为作物类别）；句意为谷类作物占用的土地超过任何其他食物类别。

pos.zh: 谷类作物；谷物；（英式）谷物早餐
谷物的；用谷物制成的

derivatives.zh: cereal + grain（组合成分）→ 谷物籽粒（语义偏移：从作物类别缩小到籽粒本身）
cereal + crop（组合成分）→ 谷类作物（语义偏移：强调田间栽培对象）
cereal + bar（组合成分）→ 谷物棒（语义偏移：转为便携食品）
breakfast（早餐）+ cereal → 谷物早餐（语义偏移：专指早餐碗里的加工谷物）
cereal + box（组合成分）→ 谷物包装盒
cereal + bowl（组合成分）→ 谷物碗

senses.title: A grass grown for grain
senses.titleCN: 为收籽粒而种植的禾草
senses.definition: any grass cultivated mainly for its edible starchy grain, such as wheat, rice or maize
senses.definitionCN: 主要为可食淀粉籽粒而栽培的任何禾草，如小麦、稻或玉米
senses.example: Wheat is the cereal best suited to this cold plateau.
senses.exampleCN: 小麦是最适合这块寒冷高原的谷类作物。
senses.why: The word names the plant category, and the botanical link is that all of them are grasses.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名植物类别，其植物学联系在于它们都是禾草。

senses.title: Cereal grain as a mass
senses.definition: the grain of such plants considered as a food or trade commodity
senses.definitionCN: 这类植物的籽粒，作为食品或贸易商品来看
senses.example: Cereal is shipped in bulk from the lake port.
senses.exampleCN: 谷物从这个湖港以散装方式运出。
senses.why: The plant and its product are named by one word because the grain is the reason the plant is grown.
senses.whyCN: 植物与产物用同一个词命名，因为籽粒正是种植它的理由。

senses.title: A breakfast food from grain
senses.definition: a processed breakfast food made from toasted or flaked cereal grains, countable in British usage
senses.definitionCN: 由烘烤或压片的谷物制成的加工早餐食品，英式用法可数
senses.example: The shelf holds six kinds of cereal.
senses.exampleCN: 货架上摆着六种谷物早餐。
senses.why: In the twentieth century the product took the name of its raw material, and British usage made it countable.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪时产品沿用了原料之名，英式用法又使它可数。

senses.title: A bowl of cereal
senses.definition: a serving of breakfast cereal, usually with milk
senses.definitionCN: 一份谷物早餐，通常加牛奶
senses.example: He eats a bowl of cereal standing up.
senses.exampleCN: 他站着吃一碗谷物早餐。
senses.why: A mass noun can be counted through its container, so a bowl becomes the unit of everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 不可数名词可以借容器计数，于是「一碗」成为日常使用的单位。

senses.title: Grain used as animal feed
senses.definition: cereal grain fed to livestock rather than milled for people
senses.definitionCN: 喂给家畜、而非磨给人吃的谷类籽粒
senses.example: Most of the cereal goes to feed, not to flour.
senses.exampleCN: 大部分谷物用作饲料，而非磨成面粉。
senses.why: The same harvest splits by end use, and feed is the largest destination in many regions.
senses.whyCN: 同一批收成按最终用途分流，在许多地区饲料是最大去向。

senses.title: Adjectival: made from grain
senses.definition: describing a product, field or policy connected with cereal grain
senses.definitionCN: 描述与谷物有关的产品、田地或政策
senses.example: Cereal production rose after the irrigation canal opened.
senses.exampleCN: 灌溉渠开通后谷物产量上升。
senses.why: The noun attributively modifies another noun, a common English way of making a category adjective.
senses.whyCN: 名词作定语修饰另一名词，是英语构成类别形容词的常见方式。

senses.title: A crop in a rotation
senses.definition: a cereal crop considered as one stage in a field rotation
senses.definitionCN: 作为田间轮作一个环节的谷类作物
senses.example: The rotation puts cereal after legumes.
senses.exampleCN: 轮作把谷物安排在豆类之后。
senses.why: Agronomy treats the plant as a slot in a sequence, which gives the word a planning sense.
senses.whyCN: 农学把这种植物当作序列中的一格，于是这个词有了规划义。

senses.title: Grain as a traded commodity
senses.definition: cereal grain priced and traded on markets, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 在市场上定价与交易的谷类籽粒，常用复数
senses.example: Cereal prices fell after a record harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 创纪录的收成之后，谷物价格下跌。
senses.why: Trade abstracts the plant into a contract, and the market sense is the most abstract of the eight.
senses.whyCN: 贸易把植物抽象成合约，市场义是八义中最抽象的一层。

intro.en: Cereal comes from Latin cerealis, of Ceres, the Roman goddess of grain, through French céréale. The breakfast sense is a twentieth-century development. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cereal 来自拉丁 cerealis「刻瑞斯的」，刻瑞斯是罗马谷物女神，经法语 céréale 进入英语。早餐义是二十世纪的发展。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ceres was the Roman goddess of grain and harvest, and her name stands at the head of the whole family.
items.cn: 刻瑞斯是罗马的谷物与丰收女神，她的名字位于整个词族的顶端。

items.en: Cerealis meant of Ceres or of grain, and the neuter plural cerealia named her festival and the grain offered at it.
items.cn: cerealis 意为刻瑞斯的或谷物的；中性复数 cerealia 指她的节庆与节上献的谷物。

items.en: French céréale carried the adjective and noun into English in the nineteenth century as a botanical and agricultural term.
items.cn: 法语 céréale 在十九世纪把这个形容词与名词带入英语，作为植物学与农学术语。

items.en: English cereal first named the grain plants, then their grain, and only later the processed breakfast product.
items.cn: 英语 cereal 先指谷类植物，再指其籽粒，最后才指加工后的早餐产品。

items.en: The breakfast food sense grew in the early twentieth century with commercial flaked and puffed cereals, and British usage made it countable.
items.cn: 早餐食品义在二十世纪初随商业化的压片与膨化谷物而发展，英式用法又使其可数。

items.en: Source uncertain (goddess's deeper name): the pre-Latin origin of Ceres is reconstructed and debated, so any Indo-European root offered for it is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（女神名的更深词源）：Ceres 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构且有争议，凡为其给出的印欧词根均属假说。

note.en: Group one holds words that sound like cereal or name its source; group two holds words for grain and grain foods.
note.cn: 第一组是读音像 cereal 或指其来源的词；第二组是表示谷物及谷物食品的词。

entries.definition: A story or set arranged in a series, from Latin series; it sounds identical to cereal but shares no origin.
entries.definitionCN: 按序列编排的故事或一组事物，来自拉丁 series；与 cereal 读音相同，但无共同来源。

entries.definition: The Roman goddess of grain whose name gives cereal; the word is a proper noun, not a food.
entries.definitionCN: 罗马谷物女神，其名给出 cereal；这是专有名词，不是食物。

entries.definition: The seed of a cereal plant; cereal alone can name the plant, the grain or the breakfast food.
entries.definitionCN: 谷类植物的籽粒；单说 cereal 可指植物、谷物或早餐食品。

entries.definition: The seed or the harvested mass; cereal is the plant category or the breakfast product.
entries.definitionCN: 种子或收获后的总量；cereal 是植物类别或早餐产品。

entries.definition: In British English it means the chief local cereal, often wheat; in American English it means maize. Cereal avoids that split.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语指当地主要谷物，常为小麦；美式英语指玉米。cereal 可避开这一分歧。

entries.definition: A sweetened mixture of oats, nuts and dried fruit eaten as a breakfast cereal; it is one product, not the category.
entries.definitionCN: 燕麦、坚果与果干加糖混合的早餐谷物食品；它是单一产品，不是类别。

entries.definition: A hot dish of grain boiled in water or milk; cereal is the raw material or the cold packaged product.
entries.definitionCN: 谷物加水或牛奶煮成的热食；cereal 是原料或冷食包装产品。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ceres, the grain goddess, stands behind the word.
normal.cn: 谷物女神刻瑞斯站在这个词的背后。

normal.en: The family runs cereal, cereal grain, cereal crop, breakfast cereal, cereal bar.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cereal、cereal grain、cereal crop、breakfast cereal、cereal bar。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: cereal crops in the field, breakfast cereal in the bowl.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：田里的谷类作物，碗里的谷物早餐。

normal.en: The homophone serial belongs to a different family and means a series.
normal.cn: 同音词 serial 属于另一词族，意为系列。

normal.en: British corn and American corn part company, which is why cereal is the safer category word.
normal.cn: 英式 corn 与美式 corn 分道扬镳，因此 cereal 是更安全的类别词。

abstract.en: Picture a goddess holding one sheaf that becomes a bowl, a bag of flour and a box on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一位女神手持一束麦穗，它变成一只碗、一袋面粉与货架上的一盒产品。

abstract.en: Picture a field that is also a price chart, each row of stalks a line on the market page.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田同时是一张价格图，每一行麦秆都是行情页上的一条线。

abstract.en: Picture a breakfast table where every object can be traced back to one kind of grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一张早餐桌，每样东西都能追到同一种草。

examples.en: Cereal crops need nitrogen at the start of the season.
examples.cn: 谷类作物在生长季开始时需要氮。

examples.en: She poured the milk over her cereal.
examples.cn: 她把牛奶倒在谷物早餐上。

examples.en: Cereal prices are sensitive to weather in exporting regions.
examples.cn: 谷物价格对出口地区的天气很敏感。

dict_mnemonic.text: Ceres（谷物女神）+ -al（……的）→ 女神的谷物 → 谷类作物、谷物，再到碗里的谷物早餐；与同音的 serial（系列）无关。

root: 拉丁 Ceres（罗马谷物女神，属格 Cereris）+ -alis「……的」→ cerealis「谷物的」→ 法语 céréale → 英语 cereal；Ceres 的更深词源属重构且有争议。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one grass: the plant, its grain, the milled product, the bowl, the feed, the adjective, the rotation slot and the market contract.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一种草展开：植物、籽粒、加工产品、碗中之物、饲料、形容词、轮作位置与市场合约。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one kind of grass can become a sheaf, a sack of grain, a bag of flour and a bowl on a breakfast table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一种草可以变成一束麦穗、一袋谷粒、一袋面粉和早餐桌上的一只碗。

branches.en: THE PLANT: the botanical category comes first.
branches.cn: 植物：植物学类别最先出现。

branches.en: THE MASS AND THE MARKET: grain as a bulk food and as a priced contract.
branches.cn: 总量与市场：谷物既是散装食品，也是定价合约。

branches.en: THE BOWL: the processed product and the serving it fills.
branches.cn: 碗：加工产品以及它装满的一份。

branches.en: THE FEED TROUGH: the same harvest diverted to animals.
branches.cn: 饲料槽：同一批收成转向动物。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY LABEL: adjective use and the crop's place in a rotation.
branches.cn: 类别标签：形容词用法与作物在轮作中的位置。

intro.en: Cereal is a Latin adjective turned noun, built from a divine name and a suffix, so its morphology runs through the goddess rather than through a verb.
intro.cn: cereal 是由拉丁形容词转成的名词，由一个神名与后缀构成，因此其构词沿女神名展开，而非沿动词展开。

latinIntro.en: Latin Ceres, genitive Cereris, supplies the stem, and -alis makes the relational adjective cerealis; the neuter plural cerealia named the goddess's festival.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 Ceres（属格 Cereris）提供词干，-alis 构成关系形容词 cerealis；中性复数 cerealia 指女神的节庆。

items.structure: Ceres, Cereris (Latin proper noun, third declension)
items.example: Ceres gave her name to the whole category.
items.exampleCN: 刻瑞斯把名字给了整个类别。

items.example: The suffix builds cerealis from the goddess's name.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由女神名构成 cerealis。

items.example: The adjective described both the goddess and the crop.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词同时描述女神与作物。

items.meaning: a grain plant or its food
items.example: Cereal entered English as a learned term.
items.exampleCN: cereal 作为学术用语进入英语。

items.meaning: the seed of a cereal plant
items.example: The cereal grain is milled into flour.
items.exampleCN: 谷粒被磨成面粉。

items.meaning: a cereal grown in a field
items.example: The cereal crop rotated with beans.
items.exampleCN: 谷类作物与豆类轮作。

items.meaningCN: 加工过的早餐谷物食品
items.example: Breakfast cereal replaced porridge in many homes.
items.exampleCN: 在许多家庭里，谷物早餐取代了粥。

items.example: The cereal bar fits in a coat pocket.
items.exampleCN: 谷物棒能塞进外套口袋。

items.meaning: the packaging of a breakfast cereal
items.example: The cereal box carries the nutrition table.
items.exampleCN: 谷物盒上印着营养表。

definition_zh: 有喙的；尖端弯如鸟喙的；船首作喙形的；果实带喙状残留的；壶嘴作喙形的
definition_en: having a beak, or ending in a hard point shaped like one, as said of birds, fruits, ships and vessels
core_image: 一只鸟的头部侧影：角质喙从额前伸出，向前收成一个坚硬的尖，凡照此形者皆可称之
scene: 标本室里，管理员掀开一层防尘布，露出一排鸟头骨标本。 Each beaked skull in the drawer belonged to a wading bird.
sceneCN: 这里 beaked 是「有喙的」（第 1 个义项：生有鸟喙，喙部形态可辨）；句意：抽屉里每一具带喙的头骨都属于一种涉禽。

pos.zh: 有喙的；喙状的；具喙形部件的（多用于复合形容词与学术描述）

senses.title: Having a Beak
senses.definition: having a beak, especially a beak of a stated kind
senses.definitionCN: 长有鸟喙，尤指喙形可辨的
senses.example: The beaked bird pried open the seed with a single twist.
senses.exampleCN: 那只带喙的鸟一拧就把种子撬开了。
senses.why: the suffix -ed turns a noun into a possessor, so beaked simply means equipped with the beak that the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ed 把名词变成「具有者」，因此 beaked 就是「带着名词所指的那个喙」。

senses.title: Shaped Like a Beak
senses.definition: ending in a narrow, often down-curved point that resembles a beak
senses.definitionCN: 末端收成狭窄、常向下弯的尖，形似鸟喙
senses.example: The handle ends in a beaked hook that catches the rope.
senses.exampleCN: 把手末端是一个喙状的钩，能勾住绳索。
senses.why: once the beak is detached from the bird it becomes a shape, and any tip that curves to a point can borrow it.
senses.whyCN: 喙一旦脱离鸟的身体就变成一个形状，任何弯成尖的末端都可以借用它。

senses.title: With a Beak-Shaped Prow
senses.definition: having a prow built or carved to a sharp beak-like point, as old galleys were
senses.definitionCN: 船首建成或雕成尖锐的喙形，如古代桨帆船
senses.example: The beaked prow of the old galley still shows above the sand.
senses.exampleCN: 旧桨帆船的尖嘴船首仍露在沙面之上。
senses.why: a warship's prow was built as a beak, and the whole vessel was named by that single forward feature.
senses.whyCN: 战船的船首被做成喙形，整条船便由这一个向前的特征得名。

senses.title: Bearing a Beaked Fruit
senses.definition: botanical, of a fruit or nut that keeps a hard, beak-like point at its tip
senses.definitionCN: 植物学术语，指果实或坚果顶端保留坚硬的喙状尖
senses.example: The beaked hazelnut hides its nut inside a long papery sheath.
senses.exampleCN: 喙状榛把坚果藏在一层长长的纸质总苞里。
senses.why: botany keeps the bird's word for a hardened point left on a fruit, because the outline is the same.
senses.whyCN: 植物学沿用了鸟的这个词，指果实上残留的硬尖，因为轮廓完全相同。

senses.title: Of the Beaked Whale Family
senses.definition: used in the fixed name of the whale family whose snout narrows to a beak-like rostrum
senses.definitionCN: 用于喙鲸科的固定名称，这一类鲸的吻部收窄成喙状
senses.example: Beaked whales can hold their breath for more than an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 喙鲸能屏住呼吸一个多小时。
senses.why: taxonomy fixes a common noun into a family label, and the whale is named for its narrow, beak-like snout.
senses.whyCN: 分类学把一个普通名词固定为科名，这种鲸因狭窄如喙的吻部而得名。

senses.title: With a Beak-Formed Spout
senses.definition: describing a jug or vessel whose spout projects and narrows like a beak
senses.definitionCN: 指壶或器皿的嘴向前伸出、收窄如喙
senses.example: The potter shaped a beaked jug for pouring oil.
senses.exampleCN: 陶工做了一把喙形嘴的壶用来倒油。
senses.why: a vessel pours through a narrow projecting mouth, and potters named that mouth after the bird's beak.
senses.whyCN: 器皿经由一个向前伸出的窄口倒出液体，陶工便按鸟喙给这个口命名。

senses.title: Wearing the Beaked Mask
senses.definition: describing a figure wearing the long beak-shaped mask associated with plague doctors
senses.definitionCN: 描述戴着与瘟疫医生相关的长喙状面具的形象
senses.example: The beaked physician in the woodcut carried a cane, not a scalpel.
senses.exampleCN: 版画里那位戴鸟嘴面具的医生拿的是手杖，不是手术刀。
senses.why: the mask actually encloses a beak-shaped chamber for herbs, so the wearer is described by the object on his face.
senses.whyCN: 面具内部本就是一个喙形药草腔，因此戴它的人被脸上那件器物来指称。

senses.title: A Beaked Evolutionary Form
senses.definition: used in morphology for a variant whose beak is enlarged or specialised as an evolved trait
senses.definitionCN: 形态学中描述喙部增大或特化、作为演化性状的变型
senses.example: The beaked morphotype appeared only after the lake lost its open water.
senses.exampleCN: 喙部特化的形态型在湖泊失去开阔水域之后才出现。
senses.why: in morphology the beak is a trait that can appear or disappear, so beaked names a form rather than an individual.
senses.whyCN: 在形态学中喙是一项可出现也可消失的性状，因此 beaked 命名的是一个形态，而非一只个体。

intro.en: Beaked is beak plus the adjectival -ed. Beak comes from Old French bec, from Latin beccus, a word generally taken as a Gaulish loan whose deeper source is uncertain. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: beaked 是 beak 加形容词后缀 -ed。beak 来自古法语 bec，再上溯拉丁 beccus；beccus 一般认为是高卢语借词，更早来源不确定。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin beccus meant 'beak'; it is generally taken to be a Gaulish loanword, and its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁 beccus 意为「喙」；一般认为是高卢语借词，其更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old French bec, recorded from the twelfth century, is the form English borrowed and the direct source of English beak.
items.cn: 古法语 bec 自 12 世纪有记录，是英语借入的形式，也是英语 beak 的直接来源。

items.en: Middle English bek or bec appears in the thirteenth century, first in falconry and hunting descriptions.
items.cn: 中古英语 bek 或 bec 见于 13 世纪，最早出现在鹰猎与狩猎的描述中。

items.en: The past participle ending -ed, from Old English -ed, was used adjectivally with the sense 'provided with', giving beaked 'having a beak'.
items.cn: 过去分词后缀 -ed 来自古英语 -ed，作形容词时表示「具有……的」，于是 beaked 即「长着喙的」。

items.en: Beaked whale and beaked hazelnut fixed the word in zoology and botany, where the beak is a diagnostic feature.
items.cn: beaked whale 与 beaked hazelnut 把该词固定在动物学与植物学中，那里的「喙」是鉴别特征。

items.en: Source uncertain (beccus): the Gaulish loan is a common view rather than a proven fact; the first date of beaked as an adjective is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（beccus）：高卢语借词是通行看法而非已证事实；beaked 作形容词的首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that resemble beaked in form but not in root; group two holds the anatomical words that overlap with it in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近但词根不同的词；第二组是在含义上与之重叠的解剖学术语。

entries.definition: The pointed top of a mountain; its origin is uncertain and it is not connected with beak, despite the near-identical sound.
entries.definitionCN: 山峰的尖顶；来源不确定，尽管读音几乎相同，与 beak 并无同源关系。

entries.definition: A tall drinking cup; it comes through Medieval Latin bicarium from Greek bikos 'a vessel', not from Latin beccus.
entries.definitionCN: 高杯；经中世纪拉丁 bicarium 上溯希腊 bikos「容器」，并非来自拉丁 beccus，属不同词根。

entries.definition: A northern English word for a small stream, from Old Norse bekkr; it shares spelling shape with beak but no ancestry.
entries.definitionCN: 英格兰北部指小溪的词，来自古诺斯 bekkr；与 beak 只有拼写相近，没有共同来源。

entries.definition: The noun that beaked is built on; the adjective adds only the idea of possession.
entries.definitionCN: beaked 所依附的名词；形容词只是在它之上加了「具有」的意思。

entries.definition: The formal zoological and botanical adjective for 'having a beak', built on Latin rostrum 'beak'; beaked is its plainer English twin.
entries.definitionCN: 动物学与植物学中「有喙的」正式形容词，建立在拉丁 rostrum「喙」之上；beaked 是它更朴素的英语对应词。

entries.definition: The beak of a bird, especially a flat or soft one; it names the organ itself, while beaked describes something as possessing or resembling it.
entries.definitionCN: 鸟的嘴，尤指扁平或柔软的喙；它命名器官本身，而 beaked 描述某物具有或形似该器官。

entries.definition: The projecting nose and mouth of an animal; broader and fleshier than a beak, which is hard and keratinous.
entries.definitionCN: 动物突出的鼻口部；比喙更宽、更有肉，而喙是坚硬角质的。

entries.definition: A long tubular organ of the mouth, as in a butterfly or an elephant; it is flexible where a beak is rigid.
entries.definitionCN: 口部细长的管状器官，如蝴蝶或大象的；它柔韧，而喙坚硬。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real zoological and botanical names, and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的动物学与植物学名称以及真实同族词。

normal.en: beak + -ed: a bird equipped with the one hard point it feeds with.
normal.cn: beak + -ed：一只鸟被配上它用来取食的那一个硬尖。

normal.en: The noun travelled Old French bec to Latin beccus, and beccus is probably a Gaulish loan.
normal.cn: 这个名词经古法语 bec 上溯拉丁 beccus，而 beccus 很可能是高卢语借词。

normal.en: Fixed names carry the sense: beaked whale, beaked hazelnut, beaked mask.
normal.cn: 固定名称承载词义：喙鲸、喙状榛、鸟嘴面具。

normal.en: Keep it apart from peak, which looks close but has a different and uncertain history.
normal.cn: 要与 peak 分开，后者外形相近，但来源不同且本身不确定。

normal.en: The family runs beak, beaky, beakless, beak-like, beaked.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 beak、beaky、beakless、beak-like、beaked。

abstract.en: Picture a single hard point growing from a rounded head, then imagine it reappearing on a prow, a nut and a jug.
abstract.cn: 想象一个从圆钝头部长出的硬尖，再想象它依次出现在船首、坚果与壶上。

abstract.en: Picture a ship whose whole identity is one forward beak.
abstract.cn: 想象一条船，它的全部身份就是向前伸出的那一只喙。

abstract.en: Picture a masked figure whose face is a beak filled with herbs.
abstract.cn: 想象一个面具人，他的脸就是一只装满药草的喙。

examples.en: Ornithologists measure the beaked skull to separate the two species.
examples.cn: 鸟类学家测量带喙的头骨以区分这两个物种。

examples.en: A beaked figure stood at the door of the plague house.
examples.cn: 一个戴鸟嘴面具的人站在疫病收容所门口。

examples.en: Each beaked achene ends in a stiff point.
examples.cn: 每一枚具喙瘦果都以一个硬尖收尾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「beak（喙）+ ed」——头上带着一只尖喙 → 有喙的、喙状的

root: 古法语 bec「喙」← 拉丁 beccus；beccus 一般认为是高卢语借词，更早来源不确定，与 peak 无同源关系。英语 beaked = beak + -ed（古英语 -ed，过去分词后缀作形容词）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of beaked all start from one shape: a hard point growing out of a rounded head, which then reappears on prows, fruits, spouts and masks.
sensesIntro.cn: beaked 的八个义项都从一个形状出发：圆钝头部伸出的硬尖，随后再现在船首、果实、壶嘴与面具上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard pointed beak projecting from a rounded head.
core.cn: 核心意象：圆钝头部前端伸出的坚硬尖喙。

branches.en: BIRD BODY: possession of a beak, and the beak as an evolved trait.
branches.cn: 鸟的身体：拥有喙，以及喙作为演化性状。

branches.en: SHAPED END: any object ending in a beak-like point, including a vessel's spout.
branches.cn: 成形的末端：任何收成喙状尖的物体，包括器皿的嘴。

branches.en: SHIP: the prow itself takes the shape of a beak.
branches.cn: 船：船首本身化作喙形。

branches.en: PLANT: a fruit keeps a beak-like remnant at its tip.
branches.cn: 植物：果实顶端保留喙状残留。

branches.en: NAMED FIGURES: a whale family and the masked physician are both named by the beak.
branches.cn: 被命名的形象：鲸类一科与蒙面医生都由喙得名。

intro.en: Beaked can be read as two pieces: a borrowed noun for a bird's mouth, and an adjectival ending meaning 'provided with'.
intro.cn: beaked 可以拆成两段读：一个借来的「鸟嘴」名词，以及表示「具有」的形容词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin beccus is the earliest recoverable form; it is usually explained as a Gaulish loan, so the trail stops there rather than at a Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 beccus 是今可追溯的最早形式；它通常被解释为高卢语借词，因此线索到此为止，而不是停在某个拉丁词根上。

items.meaning: the hard mouth parts of a bird
items.example: The hawk cleaned its beak on the branch.
items.exampleCN: 鹰在树枝上清理自己的喙。

items.structure: beccus (Latin noun, second declension, probably Gaulish loan)
items.example: Beccus is the form behind French bec and English beak.
items.exampleCN: beccus 是法语 bec 与英语 beak 背后的形式。

items.structure: -ed (Old English past participle suffix used adjectivally)
items.example: Beaked means provided with a beak.
items.exampleCN: beaked 意为长有喙的。

items.example: The beaked bird is adapted to cracking shells.
items.exampleCN: 这种带喙的鸟适应了咬碎贝壳。

items.meaning: resembling a beak; having a hooked nose
items.example: He had a beaky profile in the photograph.
items.exampleCN: 照片里他的侧影呈鹰钩鼻状。

items.example: The beakless chick must be fed by hand.
items.exampleCN: 无喙的雏鸟必须人工喂养。

items.meaning: a whale of the family Ziphiidae
items.example: Beaked whales produce clicks too high for human hearing.
items.exampleCN: 喙鲸发出的咔嗒声高到人耳听不见。

items.meaning: a hazel whose nut ends in a beak-like point
items.example: Beaked hazelnut grows along the northern edge of the forest.
items.exampleCN: 喙状榛生长在森林北缘。

items.meaning: the long beak-shaped mask of plague doctors
items.meaningCN: 瘟疫医生所戴的长喙状面具
items.example: Museums still display a beaked mask stuffed with dried herbs.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆仍陈列着一只塞满干药草的鸟嘴面具。

definition_zh: 机器；由部件组成并做功的装置；也指计算机或组织化的运作体系；动词指机械加工
definition_en: a device of connected parts that performs work; also a computer or an organised system, and to cut or shape with a machine tool
core_image: 一台车床夹着一段金属，刀头沿着导轨推进，铁屑卷成一圈圈落下来
scene: 车间的车床夹着一段金属，刀头沿导轨推进，铁屑卷成一圈圈落下。 The machine cut the shaft to within a hair of the required size.
sceneCN: 这里 machine 指由部件组成并做功的装置（第 1 个义项：机器这一装置）；句意：这台机器把轴削到与要求尺寸相差不到一根头发。

pos.zh: 机器；计算机；运作体系
用机床加工；机械切削

senses.title: A device that performs work
senses.definition: an assembly of connected parts that uses power to carry out a task
senses.definitionCN: 由相连部件构成、使用动力完成任务的组合体
senses.example: The machine lifts the load with a single lever.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器只用一个手柄就抬起货物。
senses.why: the Greek noun named any contrivance, so the first sense is the broad one of a built device.
senses.whyCN: 希腊名词原指任何巧妙装置，因此第一个义项就是「人造装置」这一宽泛含义。

senses.title: A computer
senses.definition: the computing hardware that executes stored instructions
senses.definitionCN: 执行已存指令的计算硬件
senses.example: The machine rebooted before the backup finished.
senses.exampleCN: 备份还没完成，机器就重启了。
senses.why: computers became the most common machine in daily life, and speakers shortened the name.
senses.whyCN: 计算机成了日常最常见的机器，说话者就把名称缩短了。

senses.title: A household or workshop appliance
senses.definition: a named device for one task, as in a washing or sewing machine
senses.definitionCN: 为单一任务命名的装置，如洗衣机或缝纫机
senses.example: The sewing machine has outlived three owners.
senses.exampleCN: 那台缝纫机已经比三位主人活得都久。
senses.why: a device is named by its task plus this general word, which is how the compound names spread.
senses.whyCN: 装置以「任务＋这个总称」命名，这类复合名称就是这样扩散的。

senses.title: A machine tool
senses.definition: a powered tool that cuts or shapes metal and other materials
senses.definitionCN: 切削或成型金属等材料的动力工具
senses.example: The new machine holds a tolerance of a hundredth of a millimetre.
senses.exampleCN: 这台新机床能保持百分之一毫米的公差。
senses.why: in a workshop, the general word often means the tool that makes other parts.
senses.whyCN: 在车间里，这个总称常指制造其他零件的工具。

senses.title: To cut or shape by machine
senses.definition: to remove material or form a part with a powered tool
senses.definitionCN: 用动力工具去除材料或成型零件
senses.example: They machined the block in two passes.
senses.exampleCN: 他们分两道工序加工了那块坯料。
senses.why: the noun became a verb the moment the tool's action needed a name.
senses.whyCN: 当工具的动作需要一个名称时，名词就变成了动词。

senses.title: A political organisation
senses.definition: the permanent staff and structure that win elections or hold power
senses.definitionCN: 赢得选举或维持权力的常设人员与结构
senses.example: The party machine decided the candidate before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 政党机器在投票之前就决定了候选人。
senses.why: an organisation that runs without sentiment is described by the most impersonal noun available.
senses.whyCN: 不带感情运转的组织，就用最非人格的名词来描述。

senses.title: An impersonal system of rule
senses.definition: the administrative apparatus of a state or large institution
senses.definitionCN: 国家或大型机构的行政装置
senses.example: The state machine ground down every small request.
senses.exampleCN: 国家机器把每一个小请求都磨掉了。
senses.why: the image of interlocking parts describes bureaucracy better than any abstract word.
senses.whyCN: 「咬合的部件」这一意象，比任何抽象词都更能描述官僚体系。

senses.title: A person who acts automatically
senses.definition: a person treated as incapable of independent thought
senses.definitionCN: 被视为无法独立思考的人
senses.example: They turned him into a machine that answered tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把他变成一台只回答工单的机器。
senses.why: calling a person a machine denies judgement, which is the insult the word carries here.
senses.whyCN: 把人叫作机器就是否认其判断力，这正是这个词在此处的贬义。

senses.title: Automated by computation
senses.definition: used before a noun for processes carried out by computers
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，指由计算机完成的过程
senses.example: Machine translation improved, but it still misses tone.
senses.exampleCN: 机器翻译进步了，却仍抓不住语气。
senses.why: as a modifier, the word marks the shift from human to computed action.
senses.whyCN: 作修饰语时，这个词标记从人工到计算动作的转移。

senses.title: The power unit of a vehicle
senses.definition: the engine and its housing in a boat, train or vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 船、火车或车辆中的发动机及其外壳
senses.example: The fire machine kept its pump running for nine hours.
senses.exampleCN: 消防车的泵持续运转了九个小时。
senses.why: early industrial English called a powered vehicle a machine, and the usage survives in a few names.
senses.whyCN: 早期工业英语把动力车辆叫作 machine，这种用法在少数名称里留存下来。

intro.en: Machine came from Greek mekhane through Latin machina and French. It meant any contrivance long before it meant a powered device, and its computing and organisational senses are later extensions.
intro.cn: machine 经拉丁语 machina 与法语来自希腊语 mekhane。它很久以前指任何巧妙装置，之后才指动力装置；计算机义与组织义是更晚的延伸。

items.en: Greek mekhane named a device, especially a stage crane or a siege engine, and also a means or expedient.
items.cn: 希腊语 mekhane 指装置，尤指舞台吊机或攻城器械，也指手段与办法。

items.en: Latin machina meant a structure, scaffold or engine, and the phrase deus ex machina came from the stage crane.
items.cn: 拉丁语 machina 指结构、脚手架或器械，短语 deus ex machina 就来自舞台吊机。

items.en: French machine entered English in the seventeenth century and covered any constructed device, not only powered ones.
items.cn: 法语 machine 在十七世纪进入英语，指任何建造出来的装置，而不只是动力装置。

items.en: Steam and factory work narrowed machine toward devices with moving parts driven by power.
items.cn: 蒸汽与工厂作业把 machine 收窄为由动力驱动、带运动部件的装置。

items.en: The twentieth century added the computer and the party machine, both built on the image of parts working together.
items.cn: 二十世纪加上计算机与政党机器两义，二者都建立在「部件协同运转」的意象上。

items.en: Machining arose in workshops as the verb for what a machine tool does to metal.
items.cn: machining 在车间里产生，指机床对金属所做的加工。

note.en: The first group is the machine family in other shapes; the second group is the neighbouring words for devices and systems.
note.cn: 第一组是 machine 词族的其他形态；第二组是装置与体系的相邻说法。

entries.definition: Machines as a mass; one machine is countable, machinery is not.
entries.definitionCN: 指机器的整体；一台机器可数，machinery 不可数。

entries.definition: A person who operates or makes machines; the noun names the equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 指操作或制造机器的人；名词指设备。

entries.definition: A person who repairs machines; a machine is the thing repaired.
entries.definitionCN: 指修理机器的人；machine 是被修的东西。

entries.definition: The set of parts that produces a motion; a machine contains one or more mechanisms.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生运动的那组部件；一台机器包含一个或多个机构。

entries.definition: Any constructed thing made for a purpose, often small; a machine usually has moving parts and power.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的造的任何东西，常指小型；machine 通常有运动部件与动力。

entries.definition: A machine that converts energy into motion; it is a part of many machines.
entries.definitionCN: 把能量转成运动的机器；它是许多机器的一个部件。

entries.definition: An implement a person holds and guides; a machine supplies its own motion.
entries.definitionCN: 由人握持与引导的器具；machine 自己提供运动。

entries.definition: A set of equipment working as one, often for an experiment or an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体工作的一整套设备，常用于实验或机构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real Greek source and the real noun-verb pair.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实希腊语来源与真实名词动词成对关系。

normal.en: Mekhane meant a stage crane, so a machine is first a thing that lifts and moves.
normal.cn: mekhane 原指舞台吊机，所以 machine 首先是能吊起与移动东西的装置。

normal.en: The verb forms are regular: machines, machined, machined, machining.
normal.cn: 动词形式规则：machines、machined、machined、machining。

normal.en: Task names build on it: washing machine, sewing machine, machine tool.
normal.cn: 任务名称在它之上构成：洗衣机、缝纫机、机床。

normal.en: The computing sense is simply the shortened name of the most common machine.
normal.cn: 计算机义不过是「最常用机器」的简称。

normal.en: Two objects split the verb: machine a part, machine a surface.
normal.cn: 两类宾语分开动词：加工一个零件，加工一个表面。

abstract.en: Picture a crane on a stage lowering a god who is only a painted board.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台上的吊机放下一个神，而那神不过是一块画板。

abstract.en: Picture a lathe turning a shaft until the metal is exactly the size of an idea.
abstract.cn: 想象车床削一根轴，直到金属恰好等于一个想法的尺寸。

abstract.en: Picture an office where every request disappears into a slot and comes out stamped.
abstract.cn: 想象一间办公室，每个请求都落进一个槽口，再盖着章出来。

examples.en: The machine does the lifting, but a person still chooses where.
examples.cn: 机器负责起吊，但选择吊到哪里仍由人决定。

examples.en: They machined the replacement part overnight.
examples.cn: 他们连夜加工了那只替换零件。

examples.en: The party machine had chosen the nominee months earlier.
examples.cn: 政党机器几个月前就已定下候选人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马（ma）身（chine）」——马拉着的一副身架，就是最早干活的机器

root: 希腊 mekhane「装置、舞台吊机」→ 拉丁 machina「结构、器械」→ 法语 machine → 英语 machine；先泛指装置，工业时代收窄为动力装置，二十世纪扩展出计算机与组织体系义，动词指机床加工。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses run from the general device to the computer, the appliance, the machine tool, the verb, the party machine, the state apparatus, the dehumanised person, computed processes and the vehicle's power unit.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项从泛指的装置出发，经过计算机、家用器具、机床、动词用法、政党机器、国家机器、被机械化的人、计算化流程，最后到车辆动力机组。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lathe holding a metal shaft while a cutter advances and curls off chips.
core.cn: 核心意象：车床夹着一段金属轴，刀头推进，铁屑卷曲落下。

branches.en: DEVICES: any working assembly, and the named appliance built on that pattern.
branches.cn: 装置：任何做功的组合体，以及按此模式命名的器具。

branches.en: COMPUTATION: the computer itself, and processes carried out by computed action.
branches.cn: 计算：计算机本身，以及由计算动作完成的过程。

branches.en: TOOL AND ACTION: the machine tool, and the verb for what it does to metal.
branches.cn: 工具与动作：机床，以及它对金属所做加工的动词。

branches.en: ORGANISED POWER: the party machine, and the administrative apparatus of a state.
branches.cn: 组织化的权力：政党机器，以及国家的行政装置。

branches.en: THE MECHANICAL FIGURE: a person reduced to a machine, and a vehicle's engine unit.
branches.cn: 机械化的形象：被降为机器的人，以及车辆的动力机组。

intro.en: Machine is a borrowed noun with no living affix; its family adds -ery, -ist, -ing and compound forms.
intro.cn: machine 是借入名词，本身没有能产的词缀；其词族另加 -ery、-ist、-ing 与复合形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin machina is the direct source of the French and English forms; the Greek noun mekhane stands behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 machina 是法语与英语形式的直接来源，其背后是希腊名词 mekhane。

senses.title: Replace the voices

senses.title: Hand out a name

intro.en: Dub began as a blow: the sword tap that made a knight. From striking it moved to naming, then to laying a new voice over a film, and finally to a Jamaican remix that strips a track down to drum and bass.
intro.cn: dub 起初是一击：使人成为爵士的那下剑拍。从「击打」它转到「起名」，再到给影片铺上新的声音，最后变成把曲子剥到只剩鼓与贝斯的牙买加混音。

items.en: Old French adober means to equip a man with arms.
items.cn: 古法语 adober 意为给人装备武器。

items.en: English dub is used for the sword touch that makes a man a knight.

items.en: The verb is extended to giving a person or thing a new name.

items.en: Dub is applied to replacing the spoken track of a film.
items.cn: dub 被用于替换影片的对白声轨。

items.en: Dub names a Jamaican remix style built on drum, bass and echo.
items.cn: dub 指称一种以鼓、贝斯与回声构成的牙买加混音风格。

note.en: Dub shares its short blunt shape with dab and cub, while its neighbours name the three things it does: supplying a voice, giving a name and granting a title.

dict_mnemonic.text: dub 的源头是「击打」——古英语 dubban。授爵时用剑面轻拍肩膀，那一拍就是 dub；由此引申为「给……加上一个称号」，于是有 dub him a hero。到了电影时代，「加上一层新的声音」也叫 dub，即配音、译制。1970 年代牙买加把抽掉人声、加重鼓与贝斯回声的混音叫 dub，后来衍生出 dubstep。记一条线：一拍剑 → 一个称号 → 一层新声。
