senses.title: Medical recovery
senses.titleCN: 医学康复：通过训练恢复身体功能
senses.definition: the process of restoring physical function after illness, injury or surgery through therapy and training
senses.definitionCN: 疾病、受伤或手术后通过治疗与训练恢复身体功能的过程
senses.example: After the stroke, months of rehabilitation helped him walk again.
senses.exampleCN: 中风后数月的康复训练帮助他重新行走。
senses.why: The noun joins re- 'again' to habilitare 'make able', from habilis 'apt'; rehabilitation is literally 'making able again'.
senses.whyCN: 该名词把 re-「再次」与 habilitare「使有能力」结合，后者出自 habilis「有能力的」；rehabilitation 字面就是「再次使有能力」。

senses.title: Return to work
senses.titleCN: 职业康复：帮助人重返工作岗位
senses.definition: the process of helping a person return to employment through retraining, adjustments or placement
senses.definitionCN: 通过再培训、岗位调整或安置帮助某人重返工作的过程
senses.example: Vocational rehabilitation retrained him as a dispatcher.
senses.exampleCN: 职业康复把他重新培训成调度员。
senses.why: Ability here is employability: the same 'make able again' is applied to a working role rather than a limb.
senses.whyCN: 这里的能力指就业能力：同一个「再次使有能力」被用于工作角色，而非肢体。

senses.title: Prison rehabilitation
senses.titleCN: 监狱改造：以教育矫正促使回归社会
senses.definition: the correctional aim of reforming offenders so they can rejoin society
senses.definitionCN: 矫正罪犯、使其能够重返社会的目标与措施
senses.example: The prison's rehabilitation programme offers literacy classes.
senses.exampleCN: 该监狱的改造计划提供识字课程。
senses.why: Corrections borrowed the medical word: a person is treated as needing restoration to social fitness, not merely punishment.
senses.whyCN: 矫正系统借用了医学词汇：人被当作需要恢复社会适应力者，而不只是受惩罚者。

senses.title: Addiction treatment
senses.titleCN: 戒毒戒酒康复：治疗依赖并重建生活
senses.definition: the treatment of drug or alcohol dependence, including detoxification, counselling and relapse prevention
senses.definitionCN: 对药物或酒精依赖的治疗，包括脱毒、咨询与防复发
senses.example: She entered rehabilitation for alcohol dependence.
senses.exampleCN: 她因酒精依赖进入康复治疗。
senses.why: Habituation is treated as a loss of control; rehabilitation aims to restore the person's capacity to live without the substance.
senses.whyCN: 成瘾被视为控制力的丧失；康复旨在恢复人不依赖该物质生活的能力。

senses.title: Post-disaster rebuilding
senses.titleCN: 灾后复原：恢复社区生活条件
senses.definition: the restoration of housing, services and livelihoods after a disaster or conflict
senses.definitionCN: 灾难或冲突之后恢复住房、服务与生计
senses.example: Rehabilitation of the flooded district began before the water fell.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水尚未退去，受灾区的复原工作就已开始。
senses.why: The word extends from bodies to communities: what is made able again is a place and its economy.
senses.whyCN: 词义从身体扩展到社区：被重新赋予能力的是一个地方及其经济。

senses.title: Habitat rehabilitation
senses.titleCN: 栖息地修复：让退化生态恢复功能
senses.definition: the restoration of a degraded ecosystem or habitat to a functioning state
senses.definitionCN: 使退化生态系统或栖息地恢复到可运作状态
senses.example: Wetland rehabilitation brought the bird population back.
senses.exampleCN: 湿地修复让鸟类种群回升。
senses.why: Ecology uses the medical frame: a damaged system is nursed back to health rather than replaced.
senses.whyCN: 生态学沿用医学框架：受损系统是被调养回健康，而非被替换。

senses.title: Speech and language therapy
senses.titleCN: 言语康复：恢复说话与理解能力
senses.definition: therapy that helps a person recover speech, language or swallowing after injury or illness
senses.definitionCN: 帮助人在受伤或患病后恢复言语、语言或吞咽能力的治疗
senses.example: Speech rehabilitation continued weekly for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 言语康复每周进行，持续了一年。
senses.why: This narrows sense 1 to communication: the ability being restored is the capacity to speak and be understood.
senses.whyCN: 这是第 1 个义项的窄化：被恢复的能力是说话并被理解的能力。

senses.title: Building rehabilitation
senses.titleCN: 建筑修复：使旧建筑重新可用
senses.definition: the renovation of an old or damaged building so that it can be used again
senses.definitionCN: 对老旧或受损建筑进行翻修，使其重新可使用
senses.example: The rehabilitation of the warehouse created forty apartments.
senses.exampleCN: 仓库的修复改造造出了四十套公寓。
senses.why: Construction uses the same logic: a structure that lost its capacity is made serviceable again instead of being demolished.
senses.whyCN: 建筑领域沿用同一逻辑：失去使用能力的结构被重新变得可用，而不是被拆除。

intro.en: Rehabilitation comes from Medieval Latin rehabilitare, built from re- 'again' and habilitare 'to make able', which rests on habilis 'apt, able'. The English noun followed the verb.
intro.cn: rehabilitation 出自中世纪拉丁 rehabilitare，由 re-「再次」与 habilitare「使有能力」构成，而后者基于 habilis「合适的、有能力的」。英语名词随后出现。

items.en: Habilis 'apt, handy' comes from habere 'to hold, have'. The ability to do something was pictured as something one holds.
items.cn: habilis「合适的、顺手的」出自 habere「持有、拥有」。做事的能力被想象成手中所持之物。

items.en: Medieval Latin habilitare meant 'to make able, fit, or qualified'. It was used for legal capacity as well as physical fitness.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 habilitare 意为「使有能力、使合格」，既用于法律资格，也用于身体适应能力。

items.en: Adding re- 'again' produced rehabilitare, 'to restore to a former capacity or good standing'. The word appears in medieval legal and medical records.
items.cn: 加 re-「再次」产生 rehabilitare「恢复到原有能力或良好地位」。该词见于中世纪法律与医学记录。

items.en: English rehabilitation appears in the seventeenth century, first in legal restoration of rights and later in medicine.
items.cn: 英语 rehabilitation 于 17 世纪出现，先指法律上恢复权利，后用于医学。

items.en: The twentieth century extended it to vocational training, prison reform, addiction treatment, ecology and building renovation.
items.cn: 20 世纪把它扩展到职业培训、监狱改革、成瘾治疗、生态与建筑翻修。

items.en: The exact first English citation is uncertain, and the precise medieval route through French or Latin is not fully documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（中世纪传入路径）：英语最早书证确切年代存疑；经由法语或拉丁的确切中世纪路径也无完整文献可证。

note.en: The first group separates the rehabilitate family; the second gives near-synonyms for recovery, reform and restoration.
note.cn: 第一组区分 rehabilitate 词族；第二组给出关于康复、改造与修复的近义词。

entries.definition: To restore someone's ability or standing. Rehabilitation is the process or programme.
entries.definitionCN: 指恢复某人的能力或地位；rehabilitation 是过程或计划。

entries.definition: Describing treatment or measures that restore ability. It modifies the programme, not names it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容恢复能力的治疗或措施，修饰计划而非命名计划。

entries.definition: The initial process of making someone able, especially in development contexts. Rehabilitation adds the idea of restoring what was lost.
entries.definitionCN: 指最初使某人获得能力的过程，尤见于发展语境；rehabilitation 增加了「恢复已失之物」的意思。

entries.definition: The colloquial shortening for a rehabilitation programme or centre. It is not used in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: rehabilitation 计划或中心的口语缩略，不用于正式写作。

entries.definition: A return to health or normal state. It can be spontaneous, while rehabilitation implies a structured programme.
entries.definitionCN: 指恢复健康或正常状态；可以是自然发生的，而 rehabilitation 暗示有组织的计划。

entries.definition: Bringing something back to its earlier condition, often with fidelity. Rehabilitation stresses renewed function more than original form.
entries.definitionCN: 指恢复到较早的状态，常强调忠于原貌；rehabilitation 更强调功能恢复而非原貌。

entries.definition: Changing something for the better, especially institutions or behaviour. Prison rehabilitation is one kind of reform.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某事物变好，尤指制度或行为；监狱改造是改革的一种。

entries.definition: Treatment aimed at healing. Rehabilitation is often delivered through therapy but is the broader programme.
entries.definitionCN: 指以治愈为目标的治疗；rehabilitation 常通过治疗实施，但范围更广。

entries.definition: The process of coming back into a group or society. It is the goal of much rehabilitation, not the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 指重新回到群体或社会的过程；它是许多康复的目标，而非全过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'again' + habilis 'able' + -ation: making able again.
normal.cn: re-「再次」+ habilis「有能力的」+ -ation：再次使有能力。

normal.en: The family runs rehabilitate, rehabilitative, rehab, habilitate, ability.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 rehabilitate、rehabilitative、rehab、habilitate、ability。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: physical rehabilitation, vocational rehabilitation, prison rehabilitation, habitat rehabilitation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：身体康复、职业康复、监狱改造、栖息地修复。

normal.en: rehab is the informal short form used for centres and programmes.
normal.cn: rehab 是中心与计划的口语缩略形式。

normal.en: The same word treats a limb, a worker, an offender, an addict, a district, a wetland and an old warehouse.
normal.cn: 同一个词可处理肢体、工人、罪犯、成瘾者、街区、湿地与旧仓库。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on parallel bars, counting each step back to walking.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶在平行杠上，数着一步步走回行走。

abstract.en: Picture a classroom inside a prison where someone sounds out a first word.
abstract.cn: 想象监狱里的一间教室，有人拼出第一个词。

abstract.en: Picture an old warehouse with its roof patched, its windows lit again.
abstract.cn: 想象一座旧仓库屋顶修补、窗户重新亮起。

examples.en: The rehabilitation unit has a treadmill, a pool and a mock kitchen.
examples.cn: 康复病区配有跑步机、泳池和模拟厨房。

examples.en: Rehabilitation of the mine site will take decades.
examples.cn: 矿区的生态修复需要数十年。

examples.en: The programme combines rehabilitation with job placement.
examples.cn: 该计划把康复训练与就业安置结合起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）+ ability（能力）」——把能力还给他 → rehabilitation 康复、复健

root: 拉丁 habere「持有」→ habilis「有能力的」→ habilitare「使有能力」→ re + habilitare；英语 rehabilitation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses restore capacity in different bodies: a patient, a worker, an offender, an addict, a flooded town, a wetland, a speaker, an old building.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项在不同对象上恢复能力：病人、工人、罪犯、成瘾者、受淹城镇、湿地、说话者、旧建筑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on parallel bars, counting steps back to walking.
core.cn: 核心意象：手扶平行杠，数着走回行走的步子。

branches.en: THE BODY: movement and speech are trained back into use.
branches.cn: 身体：运动与言语被训练回可用状态。

branches.en: WORK: ability is redefined as employability.
branches.cn: 工作：能力被重新定义为可就业性。

branches.en: BEHAVIOUR: offenders and addicts are treated as people needing restoration, not only punishment.
branches.cn: 行为：罪犯与成瘾者被当作需要恢复的人，而不只是受惩罚者。

branches.en: PLACES: a district or an ecosystem is nursed back to function.
branches.cn: 地方：街区或生态系统被调养回功能状态。

branches.en: BUILDINGS: an old structure is made serviceable instead of demolished.
branches.cn: 建筑：旧结构被重新变得可用，而非拆除。

intro.en: Rehabilitation is a medieval Latin verb of making-able, turned into a noun of action; re- adds restoration, habilis supplies ability.
intro.cn: rehabilitation 是表示「使有能力」的中世纪拉丁动词转为动作名词；re- 增加「恢复」义，habilis 提供「能力」义。

latinIntro.en: The habere family includes able, ability, habilitate, rehabilitation, habit, exhibit, inhibit and prohibit; the core sense is holding or having.
latinIntro.cn: habere 词族包括 able、ability、habilitate、rehabilitation、habit、exhibit、inhibit、prohibit，核心义是持有或拥有。

items.example: Rehabilitation followed the knee operation.
items.exampleCN: 膝盖手术后进行了康复训练。

items.meaning: to restore to ability or good standing
items.meaningCN: 使恢复能力或良好地位
items.example: The programme rehabilitates young offenders.
items.exampleCN: 该计划改造年轻罪犯。

items.example: Rehabilitative care began on the second day.
items.exampleCN: 康复护理从第二天开始。

items.example: The course habilitates nurses for rural practice.
items.exampleCN: 该课程使护士具备农村执业能力。

items.example: She regained the ability to write.
items.exampleCN: 她重新获得了书写能力。

items.example: The habit formed over years.
items.exampleCN: 这一习惯是多年形成的。

items.example: The museum exhibits local pottery.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆展出本地陶器。

items.example: Fear inhibited her from speaking.
items.exampleCN: 恐惧使她不敢发言。

definition_zh: 参与；参加；参与人数；参与权；份额参与；员工参与；政治参与；课堂参与；费用分担
definition_en: the act of taking part in an activity, the number or degree of people taking part, the right or share gained by taking part, or a formal arrangement in which members share in decisions, costs, or profits
core_image: 一只脚踏进正在转动的圈子里，圈里的节奏因为这双脚发生了变化
scene: 社区开会讨论新公园的选址，会议室里的折叠椅都坐满了。 The meeting saw participation double compared with last time.
sceneCN: 这里 participation 是「参与人数」（第 2 个义项：实际参加某项活动的人数或比例）；句意：这次会议的参与人数比上次翻了一倍。

pos.zh: 参与；参加；参与人数；参与权；份额；分担

senses.title: The act of taking part
senses.definition: the act of joining in an activity, event, or process together with others
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起加入某项活动、事件或过程的行为
senses.example: Participation in the survey was voluntary and anonymous.
senses.exampleCN: 参与这项调查是自愿且匿名的。
senses.why: Latin particeps means 'part-taker': pars 'part' plus capere 'to take'. Participation is literally taking a part for yourself in something others are already doing, one foot entering the circle.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 particeps 意为“拿取一份的人”：pars“部分”加 capere“拿取”。participation 字面上就是在一件别人已经在做的事里为自己拿一份，一只脚踏进那个圈。

senses.title: How many take part
senses.definition: the number of people who take part, or the proportion of a group that does so, often expressed as a rate
senses.definitionCN: 参加的人数，或群体中参加者的比例，通常以比率表示
senses.example: Voter participation fell below forty percent in the off-year election.
senses.exampleCN: 这次非大选年的选举中，选民参与率跌到四成以下。
senses.why: Once the act is countable, it can be measured. The circle is drawn, and the question becomes how many feet are inside it, not what each foot is doing.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个行为可以被计数，它就能被测量。圈画好了，问题变成圈里有多少只脚，而不是每只脚在做什么。

senses.title: The right to have a part
senses.definition: the recognized right or opportunity of a person or group to take part in decisions that affect them
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体参与影响自身决策的被承认的权利或机会
senses.example: The treaty guarantees public participation in land-use planning.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约保障公众参与土地利用规划的权利。
senses.why: Here the emphasis moves from the fact of joining to the door being open. Participation is the standing permission to put your foot in the circle, not merely the step itself.
senses.whyCN: 这里重点从“加入的事实”转到“门是否开着”。participation 是允许你把脚踏进圈子的长期资格，而不只是那一步动作。

senses.title: A share in money or rights
senses.titleCN: 在金钱或权益中的一份
senses.definition: a share in profits, ownership, or a financial arrangement, gained by taking part in an enterprise
senses.definitionCN: 通过参与某项事业而获得的利润、所有权或财务安排中的份额
senses.example: The fund takes a participation in the port operator's revenue.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金在这家港口运营商的收入中占有一份权益。
senses.why: The 'part' inside the word becomes literal and countable: you take a part of the money, not just a part of the work. The circle now has shares marked on it.
senses.whyCN: 词里的“部分”在这里变成字面、可数的东西：你拿的是钱的一部分，而不只是工作的一部分。圈上现在标着份额。

senses.title: Workers sharing in decisions
senses.definition: a management arrangement in which employees take part in decisions, often through councils, shares, or consultation
senses.definitionCN: 一种管理安排，让员工通过委员会、持股或协商参与到决策中
senses.example: Employee participation schemes raised retention but slowed decisions.
senses.exampleCN: 员工参与方案提高了留任率，却拖慢了决策。
senses.why: Industry applies the political circle to the workplace. Those who previously only followed instructions are given a place where the rules are decided, so the word gains an institutional sense.
senses.whyCN: 工业界把政治上的圈子搬进工作场所。原先只执行指令的人获得了一个参与定规则的位置，这个词于是多了一层制度义。

senses.title: Citizens taking part in public life
senses.definition: the involvement of citizens in elections, civic organizations, protests, or public deliberation
senses.definitionCN: 公民在选举、市民组织、抗议或公共商议中的参与
senses.example: Civic participation includes voting, volunteering, and attending hearings.
senses.exampleCN: 公民参与包括投票、志愿服务和出席听证会。
senses.why: The circle is now the city. Participation measures whether people treat public decisions as theirs to make, rather than as something done to them.
senses.whyCN: 这时的圈子是城市。participation 衡量的是人们是否把公共决策当作自己该做的事，而不是别人施加给他们的事。

senses.title: Speaking up in class
senses.definition: a student's contribution to a class through questions, answers, and discussion, often part of the grade
senses.definitionCN: 学生通过提问、回答与讨论对课堂做出的贡献，常计入成绩
senses.example: Class participation counts for a fifth of the final mark.
senses.exampleCN: 课堂参与占期末成绩的五分之一。
senses.why: The smallest circle is a seminar room. Here participation is not attendance but visible contribution: the foot must not only enter, it must move.
senses.whyCN: 最小的圈子是研讨室。这里的 participation 不是到场，而是看得见的贡献：脚不仅要踏进去，还得动起来。

senses.title: Sharing a cost or loss
senses.definition: a share of a cost, loss, or obligation that a party accepts as part of an arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 某一方在安排中接受承担的费用、损失或义务份额
senses.example: The insurer's participation in the loss is limited to ten percent.
senses.exampleCN: 保险人对该损失的承担份额限于百分之十。
senses.why: Taking part can mean taking part of the burden. The same pars appears, but now the part is a liability, and the circle is a contract.
senses.whyCN: 参与也可以意味着承担一部分负担。同一个 pars 又出现了，但这次这份是责任，圈子是一纸合同。

senses.title: How deeply one is involved
senses.definition: the degree of a person's engagement in an activity, ranging from passive presence to active commitment
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在活动中的投入程度，从被动在场到主动承诺
senses.example: The study distinguishes participation in name from participation in practice.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把名义上的参与和实际上的参与区分开来。
senses.why: Being inside the circle is not the same as dancing. This sense measures depth rather than count, which is why the same word can describe both a crowd and a single committed member.
senses.whyCN: 站在圈里和在圈里跳舞不是一回事。这个义项衡量的是深度而非数量，所以同一个词既能描述一大群人，也能描述一个真正投入的成员。

intro.en: Participation comes from Latin participatio, an action noun from participare 'to share, to partake', built on particeps 'sharing, partaking'. Particeps is a compound of pars 'part' and the -ceps form of capere 'to take, seize'. The literal image is 'taking a part'. English took the word in the 14th century for 'the state of sharing in something', and only later built the modern senses of civic, employee, and financial participation.
intro.cn: participation 来自拉丁语 participatio，是 participare“分享、参与”的动作名词，其基础是 particeps“分享的、参与的”。particeps 由 pars“部分”与 capere“拿取、抓取”的 -ceps 形式复合而成。字面意象是“拿取一份”。英语在 14 世纪借入这个词，指“分享某物的状态”，后来才发展出公民参与、员工参与与财务份额等现代义项。

items.en: Pars means 'part, piece, share'. Capere means 'to take, seize, capture'. Particeps, literally 'part-taking', describes someone who has a share in something, including a partner or an accomplice.
items.cn: pars 意为“部分、份额”。capere 意为“拿取、抓取、俘获”。particeps 字面是“拿取一份的”，描述在某事中占有一份的人，也可指同伴或同谋。

items.en: Participare develops from particeps with the sense 'to give a share of, to make someone a partner', then 'to have a share in, to take part'. Participatio is its action noun.
items.cn: participare 从 particeps 发展而来，先表示“分出份额、使某人成为伙伴”，再表示“在其中占一份、参与”。participatio 是它的动作名词。

items.en: English participation first means 'the fact of sharing or having a part in something', especially in theology, where the creature participates in the divine. The civic sense is later.
items.cn: 英语 participation 最早指“分享或在某事物中占有一份的事实”，尤用于神学，说受造物分有神性。公民参与义出现较晚。

items.en: Political economy and politics extend the word to voting, office-holding, and shares in profits. 'Participation in government' becomes a standard phrase of reform debates.
items.cn: 政治经济学与政治学把这个词扩展到投票、担任公职与利润份额。“参与政府”成为改革辩论中的标准说法。

items.en: Management theory coins employee participation; development agencies speak of participatory projects; education grades class participation. The abstract noun now covers nearly every circle a person can enter.
items.cn: 管理学提出员工参与；发展机构谈论参与式项目；教育把课堂参与计入成绩。这个抽象名词如今几乎覆盖人可能进入的每一个圈子。

items.en: Perception also contains capere, but its prefix is per- 'thoroughly', so it means 'seize completely' — grasp with the senses. Participation has pars 'part', not per-, so it means 'take a share'. The two words share a hand but not a purpose.
items.cn: perception 也含 capere，但前缀是 per-“彻底”，所以意为“彻底抓住”——用感官把握。participation 里是 pars“部分”，不是 per-，所以意为“拿一份”。两个词共享同一只手，目的却不同。

note.en: The first group follows the pars + capere family and marks the one neighbour that shares capere with a different prefix. The second group compares the words for joining in, being engaged, being present, and giving something.
note.cn: 第一组沿着 pars 加 capere 的词族，并标出一个共享 capere 但前缀不同的邻居。第二组比较表示“加入”“投入”“到场”“贡献”的几个词。

entries.definition: to take part in an activity. It is the verb behind participation, and it keeps the literal 'take a part' image.
entries.definitionCN: 参加某项活动。它是 participation 背后的动词，保留了“拿取一份”的字面意象。

entries.definition: a person who takes part. The ending -ant marks the person, while -ation marks the act or the share.
entries.definitionCN: 参加的人。-ant 词尾标记人，而 -ation 标记行为或份额。

entries.definition: a verb form used as an adjective or noun. It comes from Latin participium, 'a sharing', because it shares in the nature of both verb and adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 用作形容词或名词的动词形式。它出自拉丁语 participium“分享”，因为它同时兼有动词与形容词的性质。

entries.definition: the act of becoming aware through the senses. It shares capere 'take' but uses per- 'thoroughly', so it means 'seize completely', not 'take a share'.
entries.definitionCN: 通过感官觉察事物的行为。它共享 capere“拿取”，但用 per-“彻底”，所以意为“完全抓住”，而不是“拿一份”。

entries.definition: the state of being connected with or emotionally caught up in something. It stresses commitment and entanglement, while participation stresses taking a part.
entries.definitionCN: 与某事有联系或情感上被卷入的状态。它强调投入与牵连，而 participation 强调拿取一份。

entries.definition: active commitment of attention or effort, or a formal arrangement to meet. It is the depth sense of participation, often with a tone of deliberate choice.
entries.definitionCN: 注意力或努力的主动投入，也指正式的会面约定。它接近 participation 的深度义，常带“有意选择”的语气。

entries.definition: the fact of being present at an event. It counts bodies in the room and says nothing about whether they do anything.
entries.definitionCN: 出席某场活动的事实。它数的是房间里的身体，不说明这些人做了什么。

entries.definition: something given to a common pool, such as money, work, or ideas. It stresses what is put in, while participation stresses the act of joining.
entries.definitionCN: 投入公共池的东西，如钱、劳动或想法。它强调投入了什么，而 participation 强调加入的行为。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: pars 'part', capere 'take', particeps 'part-taker', the participle cousin, and the perception contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：pars“部分”、capere“拿取”、particeps“拿取一份的人”、同源的分词、以及与 perception 的对比。

normal.en: Pars is 'part' and capere is 'take': participation literally means taking a part, so the word always contains a share.
normal.cn: pars 是“部分”，capere 是“拿取”：participation 字面上就是拿取一份，所以这个词里永远装着份额。

normal.en: Particeps is the Latin noun for a sharer, and English partner comes from the same idea of someone who has a part with you.
normal.cn: particeps 是拉丁语里“分享者”的名词，英语 partner 也来自同一想法：一个与你共有一份的人。

normal.en: The grammatical participle is called a 'sharing' word because it shares in two parts of speech, which is participation inside grammar.
normal.cn: 语法里的分词被称为“分享”之词，因为它兼有两类词性，这就是语法内部的 participation。

normal.en: Perception has the same capere but the prefix per- 'thoroughly': perception grabs the whole object, participation takes only a part of it.
normal.cn: perception 有同一个 capere，但前缀是 per-“彻底”：感知抓住整个对象，参与只拿其中一份。

normal.en: The suffix chain is -ate, -ant, -ation: participate the act, participant the person, participation the state or share.
normal.cn: 后缀链是 -ate、-ant、-ation：participate 是动作，participant 是人，participation 是状态或份额。

abstract.en: A circle of dancers has a gap; one pair of feet fills it, and the pattern changes for everyone inside.
abstract.cn: 一圈跳舞的人留着一个缺口；一双脚填进去，圈里每个人的图案都随之改变。

abstract.en: Attendance counts chairs; participation counts what the chairs are doing.
abstract.cn: 到场数的是椅子；参与数的是椅子上的动作。

abstract.en: A shareholder owns a piece of paper that says 'a part'; a citizen owns a voice that says 'my part'.
abstract.cn: 股东持有一张写着“一份”的纸；公民拥有一个说着“我这一份”的声音。

examples.en: Public participation slowed the project but improved its design.
examples.cn: 公众参与拖慢了项目，却改进了设计。

examples.en: The participation rate among first-time voters rose sharply.
examples.cn: 首次投票者的参与率大幅上升。

examples.en: She holds a small participation in the family business.
examples.cn: 她在这家家族企业里持有少量股份。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「帕提西佩申」——帕提把一只脚“踏”进圈里，顺手拿走了其中的一份 → participation 参与；份额（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 participare「分享、参与」，出自 particeps「拿取一份的人」，由 pars「部分」+ capere「拿取」的 -ceps 形式复合；后缀 -ation 为动作名词词尾。核心是「在一件别人已经在做的事里拿取属于自己的一份」。同族含 participate、participant、participle；perception 共享 capere 但前缀为 per-，词根组合不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of participation all begin with one foot entering a circle and taking a part. What changes is what is being shared — the activity, the count, the right, the money, the decisions, the cost, or the depth of commitment.
sensesIntro.cn: participation 的九个义项都从一只脚踏进圈子、拿走一份开始。变化的是被分享的东西——活动本身、人数、权利、金钱、决策、成本，还是投入的深度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one foot entering a circle already in motion, taking a part and changing the pattern.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚踏进已经在转动的圈子，拿走一份，并改变整体图案。

chain: THE SHARE CAN BE MONEY OR BURDEN

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS DEPTH: joining in, and how far a person actually commits once inside.
branches.cn: 行为与深度：加入其中，以及进入之后真正投入多深。

branches.en: THE COUNT: a participation rate in an election or a grade for speaking in class.
branches.cn: 计数：选举中的参与率，或课堂发言的成绩。

branches.en: THE OPEN DOOR: the right of citizens or groups to take part in decisions that affect them.
branches.cn: 敞开的门：公民或群体参与影响自身决策的权利。

branches.en: THE SHARE: a portion of profit or ownership, and a portion of cost or loss.
branches.cn: 那一份：利润或所有权的份额，以及费用或损失的份额。

branches.en: THE WORKPLACE CIRCLE: employees given a place at the table where rules are decided.
branches.cn: 工作场所的圈子：员工在决定规则的那张桌旁获得一个位置。

intro.en: Participation is participation-, the stem of Latin participatio, plus English -ion from Latin -io/-ionem. The Latin compound is pars 'part' + -ceps (from capere 'take'). The family grows by changing the suffix: -ate verb, -ant person, -ation action, -atory adjective.
intro.cn: participation 是拉丁 participatio 的词干 participat- 加英语 -ion（拉丁 -io/-ionem）。拉丁复合词是 pars“部分”+ -ceps（出自 capere“拿取”）。词族通过换后缀生长：-ate 动词、-ant 人、-ation 动作、-atory 形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is pars 'part', capere 'take', particeps 'part-taker', participare 'to share', and participatio 'a sharing'. The same capere, with different prefixes, gives perception, reception, and capture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 pars“部分”、capere“拿取”、particeps“拿取一份的人”、participare“分享”、participatio“分享”。同一个 capere 配上不同前缀，还产生表示“感知”“接收”与“捕获”的词。

items.meaning: the act or state of taking a part
items.meaningCN: 拿取一份的行为或状态；参与（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: Participation in the trial is open to all residents.
items.exampleCN: 所有居民都可以参与这项试验。

items.meaning: to take a part in something
items.meaningCN: 在某事中拿取一份；参加（pars 部分 + capere 拿取 + -ate）
items.example: Ten schools participated in the study.
items.exampleCN: 十所学校参与了这项研究。

items.example: Each participant received a numbered card.
items.exampleCN: 每位参与者都领到一张编号卡。

items.meaning: organized so that people take part
items.meaningCN: 被安排成让人参与的（-ory 功能形容词）
items.example: The council runs a participatory budget.
items.exampleCN: 该委员会实行参与式预算。

items.meaningCN: 以共同决策为特征的（-ive 倾向形容词）
items.example: Participative management suits small teams.
items.exampleCN: 参与式管理适合小团队。

items.meaning: a verb form that shares in two parts of speech
items.meaningCN: 兼有两类词性的动词形式；分词
items.example: A participle borrows its ending from a verb and its job from an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 分词借用动词的词尾，又承担形容词的职能。

items.structure: Old French parçonier, from Latin partitionem 'a dividing'
items.meaning: one who shares an activity or a business with another
items.meaningCN: 与他人共同从事活动或经营的人；伙伴
items.example: She became a partner in the firm last year.
items.exampleCN: 她去年成了这家公司的合伙人。

items.meaning: a piece of a whole, or a share in something
items.meaningCN: 整体中的一块，或某物中的一份
items.example: Each student reads a different part.
items.exampleCN: 每个学生读不同的部分。

items.meaning: a taking in through the senses
items.meaningCN: 通过感官彻底拿取；知觉（per- 彻底 + capere 拿取）
items.example: Color perception varies between individuals.
items.exampleCN: 颜色知觉因人而异。

latinEntries.meaning: to give a share of, to take part in

definition_zh: 惩罚；处罚；严厉对待；粗暴使用使损坏；重创（对手）；猛烈抨击；使身体极度疲惫
definition_en: to make someone suffer for a wrong, or to treat a person or thing so harshly that it is worn down
core_image: 木槌落下，犯错的人被带离座位，去承受自己招来的那阵疼痛
scene: 夜间巡查时，看守发现一名囚犯试图翻墙逃走，于是把他单独关进一间没有窗的小屋。 The warden punished the prisoner by locking him alone in a windowless cell.
sceneCN: 这里指「因过错而使某人受苦」，对应第 1 个义项：让犯错者为自己的行为承担痛苦；句意为看守把企图逃跑的囚犯单独关进没有窗的小屋作为惩罚。画面要点：夜间走廊、翻墙的脚印、被关上的铁门；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 惩罚；处罚（及物动词，常与 for 连用说明过错）
严厉对待；粗暴使用使损坏（口语中可指物）

derivatives.zh: 由 punish 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作结果）→ 由「使人受苦这一动作」转为「所施加的那份痛苦或处罚」
由 punish 加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表能够被）→ 由「施加惩罚」转为「依法可以受罚的」
由 punish 加现在分词后缀 → 由「惩罚他人」转为形容「像惩罚一样消耗人的、折磨人的」
由 punish 加施事后缀（表施动者）→ 由「惩罚」这一动作转为「施加惩罚的那个人」
与 punish 同出拉丁 punire，加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表倾向）→ 由「施加惩罚」转为「以惩罚为目的的、惩罚性的」
与 punish 同出拉丁 poena，经古法语形成名词 → 由「惩罚这一动作」转为「作为惩罚所付的那笔代价」

senses.title: To make someone suffer for a wrong
senses.definition: to cause a person who has done wrong to undergo pain, loss or hardship
senses.definitionCN: 使做错事的人经历痛苦、损失或艰难
senses.example: The company punished the clerk for leaking the file.
senses.exampleCN: 公司因那名职员泄露文件而惩罚了他。
senses.why: Latin punire meant to make someone pay for a wrong, so the core idea is not pain for its own sake but a debt being settled through suffering.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 punire 意为让某人为过错付出代价，所以核心并不是疼痛本身，而是一笔债通过受苦被结清。

senses.title: To sentence in a court
senses.definition: to impose a legal sentence on a convicted person
senses.definitionCN: 对已被定罪的人施加法律判决
senses.example: The court punished the fraud with five years in prison.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭判处那名诈骗犯五年监禁。
senses.why: When the debt is collected by a court, the suffering is fixed by law, given a name and given a term.
senses.whyCN: 当这笔债由法庭来收取，痛苦就由法律确定，被赋予名称，也被赋予期限。

senses.title: To discipline a child or pupil
senses.definition: to correct a child or pupil by withdrawing something valued or by mild suffering
senses.definitionCN: 以收回孩子看重的某物或轻微的苦头来纠正其行为
senses.example: His parents punished him by cancelling the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 他父母取消旅行作为对他的惩罚。
senses.why: A household collects the same debt in miniature: a small wrong, a small withdrawal of what the child values.
senses.whyCN: 家庭以缩小的尺度收取同一笔债：小小的过错，配上小小地拿走孩子看重的东西。

senses.title: To treat someone with deliberate harshness
senses.titleCN: 刻意以严酷手段对待某人
senses.definition: to subject a person to prolonged harsh treatment, whether or not a rule was broken
senses.definitionCN: 使某人长时间承受严酷对待，不论是否真的违规
senses.example: The guards punished the prisoners by keeping them standing all night.
senses.exampleCN: 看守让囚犯整夜站立，以此折磨他们。
senses.why: Once pain is separated from the debt, any deliberate infliction of suffering can take the name, even where no rule exists to be broken.
senses.whyCN: 一旦疼痛与那笔债脱钩，任何刻意施加的痛苦都能叫这个名字，哪怕并不存在可供违反的规则。

senses.title: To damage something by rough use
senses.titleCN: 因粗暴使用而损坏某物
senses.definition: to wear out or damage an object by using it far harder than it was designed for
senses.definitionCN: 以远超设计承受的方式使用，使物品磨损或损坏
senses.example: Rough roads punish the tyres far more than smooth ones.
senses.exampleCN: 崎岖路面比平坦路面更伤轮胎。
senses.why: Objects cannot owe a debt, so the word transfers to rough treatment that makes a thing suffer wear, as if the thing were being made to pay.
senses.whyCN: 物品不可能欠债，于是这个词转到「粗暴对待使某物受损」上，仿佛那件东西也在被逼着付出代价。

senses.title: To defeat an opponent by a wide margin
senses.titleCN: 以压倒性优势重创对手
senses.definition: to beat an opponent so heavily that the defeat feels like a penalty
senses.definitionCN: 以极大差距击败对手，使这场失败如同一种惩罚
senses.example: The champions punished the visitors with four goals in twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军队在二十分钟内连进四球，重创了客队。
senses.why: A contest can turn a score into a debt, and a heavy defeat is that debt being collected all at once.
senses.whyCN: 比赛可以把比分变成一笔债，而一场惨败就是这笔债被一次性收走。

senses.title: To criticise sharply
senses.definition: to attack a person, work or idea with very severe public criticism
senses.definitionCN: 以极严厉的公开批评攻击某人、某作品或某观点
senses.example: The critics punished the film for its empty spectacle.
senses.exampleCN: 影评人猛烈抨击这部影片空洞的视觉堆砌。
senses.why: Words can inflict suffering too, so sharp criticism borrows the same verb and makes its target pay in reputation.
senses.whyCN: 言语也能造成痛苦，于是尖锐的批评借用了同一个动词，让对象以名声偿付。

senses.title: To exhaust the body through effort
senses.titleCN: 使身体因用力而极度疲惫
senses.definition: to strain the body so hard that the effort feels like a punishment
senses.definitionCN: 使身体承担极大负荷，让这种用力如同惩罚
senses.example: The steep climb punished legs that had not trained.
senses.exampleCN: 陡峭的山路让未经训练的腿吃尽苦头。
senses.why: The body itself can be made to pay for the effort demanded of it, so intense exertion completes the drift from moral debt to sheer physical cost.
senses.whyCN: 身体本身也能为被要求的努力付出代价，于是高强度消耗完成了从道德亏欠到纯粹身体代价的漂移。

intro.en: Punish came into English through Old French punir from Latin punire, an earlier form poenire built on poena 'penalty'. The same poena family also produced penal, penalty and punitive. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: punish 经古法语 punir 进入英语，上溯拉丁 punire，其较早形式 poenire 由 poena「罚」构成；同一个 poena 词族还生出 penal、penalty 与 punitive。年代均为约数。

items.en: The Greek noun poine named the price paid to settle a wrong, and it was borrowed into Latin as the starting point of this family.
items.cn: 希腊名词 poine 指为平息过错而付出的价，它被借入拉丁语，成为这一词族的起点。

items.en: Poena meant punishment and also the compensation that settled a wrong, and from it the verb poenire was formed.
items.cn: poena 既指处罚，也指平息过错的补偿，动词 poenire 由它构成。

items.en: Punire replaced the older poenire and meant to inflict a penalty, to avenge, to take vengeance for a wrong.
items.cn: punire 取代了较早的 poenire，意为施加处罚、报复、为过错索取代价。

items.en: Old French punir carried the Latin verb into the sense of correcting by pain, and English borrowed it around 1300.
items.cn: 古法语 punir 把这一拉丁动词带入「以痛苦纠正」的意思，英语大约在十四世纪初借入。

items.en: English punish first meant to inflict a legal penalty, then any painful correction, and finally rough handling of people or things.
items.cn: 英语 punish 最初指施加法律上的处罚，随后泛指任何带来痛苦的纠正，最后扩展到对人、对物的粗暴对待。

items.en: Punishment names the suffering as a result, punishable names what may be punished, and punitive names the intention behind a measure.
items.cn: punishment 把痛苦作为结果来命名，punishable 指可以受罚的，punitive 则指一项措施背后的惩罚意图。

note.en: The first group holds the same Latin family plus one mere look-alike; the second group offers near alternatives for the act of making someone suffer.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族的词，外加一个只是长得像的词；第二组是「使人受苦」这一动作的近义替代。

entries.definition: The noun naming the suffering imposed; the verb names the act of imposing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被施加的痛苦的名词；动词则指施加这一动作。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'liable to be punished'; it describes a legal status, not an act.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「可受处罚的」形容词；它描述的是一种法律状态，而不是动作。

entries.definition: From Latin punire with an adjective suffix; it describes the purpose of a measure rather than the deed itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁 punire 加形容词后缀而来；它描述一项措施的目的，而不是行为本身。

entries.definition: Weak and small; it merely looks like punish at the start and is not related to it in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 瘦小虚弱的；只是开头与 punish 相似，并非同源。

entries.definition: To impose a penalty, usually under a written rule; it stresses the rule, while punish stresses the suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 通常依据成文规则施加处罚；它强调规则，而 punish 强调痛苦。

entries.definition: To correct behaviour through training or punishment; reform is the aim, which punish does not imply.
entries.definitionCN: 通过训练或惩罚纠正行为；改正是目的，punish 并不含此意。

entries.definition: To punish or scold severely; it often means words rather than physical suffering and sounds formal.
entries.definitionCN: 严厉惩罚或斥责；常指言语而非肉体痛苦，语体正式。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'relating to punishment'; it cannot take an object and never names the act.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与刑罚有关的」形容词；它不能带宾语，也不指动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, the real derived family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的派生词族与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Punish goes back through French punir to Latin punire, and behind punire stands poena, the price of a wrong.
normal.cn: punish 经法语 punir 上溯拉丁 punire，而 punire 背后站着 poena，即过错的代价。

normal.en: The family keeps splitting the same idea: punishment is the suffering, punitive is the intention, punishable is the liability.
normal.cn: 这一词族不断拆分同一个观念：punishment 是那份痛苦，punitive 是那种意图，punishable 是那种责任。

normal.en: Punish almost always asks two questions: who suffers, and for what.
normal.cn: punish 几乎总要回答两个问题：谁受苦，以及为了什么。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the legal core: punish offenders, punish wrongdoing, be punished by law.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出法律内核：惩罚违法者、惩处不当行为、受法律制裁。

normal.en: The object can be a person, a body, a pair of shoes or an opponent, but the verb always means someone or something pays.
normal.cn: 宾语可以是人、身体、一双鞋或一个对手，但这个动词始终表示「有人或某物在偿付」。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where the wrong sits on one pan and the suffering is poured onto the other until the beam levels.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一端放着过错，另一端被倒进痛苦，直到横梁齐平。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt handed to someone who never asked to buy anything.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据被递给一个根本没打算买东西的人。

abstract.en: Picture a path of sharp stones laid across a field so that every step costs the walker something.
abstract.cn: 想象田野上铺着一条尖石小路，每走一步都要让行人付出点代价。

examples.en: The school punished the boys for vandalising the gym.
examples.cn: 学校因这些男孩破坏体育馆而惩罚了他们。

examples.en: Years of heavy loads had punished the truck's suspension.
examples.cn: 多年的重载已经把卡车的悬挂系统损耗得很厉害。

examples.en: The home side punished every mistake in the second half.
examples.cn: 主队在下半场抓住了每一次失误并加以重创。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕你失」——怕你失了规矩，就先让你吃一阵苦头 → 惩罚、处罚

root: 希腊 poine「为过错付出的价」→ 拉丁 poena「罚、补偿」→ 拉丁动词 poenire / punire「施罚、索偿」→ 古法语 punir → 英语 punish；同族词有 punishment、punishable、punitive、penal、penalty。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: a wrong creates a debt, and suffering collects it. The collection can be a general punishment, a court sentence, a parent's correction, deliberate harshness, wear on an object, a heavy defeat, sharp criticism, or plain physical exhaustion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着一条线展开：过错生出一笔债，而痛苦负责把它收回。收回的方式可以是泛指的惩罚、法庭的判决、父母的管教、刻意的严酷、对物品的损耗、一场惨败、尖锐的批评，或纯粹的身体消耗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mallet falls and the offender leaves his seat to bear the pain he brought about.
core.cn: 核心意象：木槌落下，犯错的人离开座位，去承受自己招来的那阵疼痛。

branches.en: BASE ACT: pain is deliberately dealt out because a wrong was done.
branches.cn: 基础动作：因为有人做错，痛苦被刻意施加出去。

branches.en: TWO COURTS: the debt is collected by a judge with a sentence, or by a parent with a withdrawn privilege.
branches.cn: 两种法庭：债由法官以判决收取，或由父母以收回特权收取。

branches.en: HARSHNESS WITHOUT A RULE: suffering continues even when no rule existed to be broken.
branches.cn: 无规之严：即便没有可供违反的规则，痛苦仍被继续施加。

branches.en: NON-HUMAN TARGETS: an object wears out under rough use, or an opponent is crushed by a score.
branches.cn: 非人对象：物品在粗暴使用下损耗，对手被比分碾碎。

branches.en: COST WITHOUT A VERDICT: words wound a reputation, and effort wrings out the body.
branches.cn: 无判决的代价：言语损伤名声，用力榨干身体。

intro.en: Punish sits at the head of an English family whose members split the ideas of act, result, liability and purpose.
intro.cn: punish 位于一个英语词族的首位，其成员分别承担动作、结果、责任与目的这几层意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin poena and the verb punire underlie punish, punishment, punishable and punitive, while the adjective poenalis leads to penal and penalty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 poena 与动词 punire 位于 punish、punishment、punishable 与 punitive 之下，而形容词 poenalis 则通向 penal 与 penalty。

items.meaning: to exact a price for a wrong
items.example: The stem appears in several English words.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在好几个英语词里。

items.meaning: to make someone suffer for a wrong
items.example: They punished him for the delay.
items.exampleCN: 他们因延误而惩罚了他。

items.example: The code punishes repeat offenders.
items.exampleCN: 该法典惩罚屡犯者。

items.example: He was punished for cheating.
items.exampleCN: 他因作弊受到惩罚。

items.example: It was a punishing schedule.
items.exampleCN: 那是一个折磨人的日程。

items.example: The punishment fitted the crime.
items.exampleCN: 这项惩罚与罪行相称。

items.example: The offence is punishable by fine.
items.exampleCN: 该违法行为可处以罚金。

items.example: The punisher rarely escapes blame.
items.exampleCN: 施罚者很少能免于责难。

items.example: They imposed punitive tariffs.
items.exampleCN: 他们加征了惩罚性关税。

items.example: The penal code was revised.
items.exampleCN: 刑法典被修订了。

items.example: The penalty was severe.
items.exampleCN: 处罚很严厉。

definition_zh: 细胞器；细胞内具有特定功能的结构
definition_en: a specialised structure inside a cell, such as a mitochondrion, chloroplast or ribosome, with a particular job
core_image: 细胞剖面图上，几个小隔间各自亮起不同颜色，像一间大屋里的小工坊
scene: 细胞剖面图上，几个小隔间各自亮起不同颜色，像一间大屋里的小工坊。 Each organelle has its own job inside the cell, from energy supply to protein assembly.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（细胞器）；句意为每个细胞器在细胞内各有职责，从供能到组装蛋白质。

pos.zh: 名词：细胞器；细胞内特定功能结构

derivatives.zh: 由「细胞器」加形容词词尾构成，义为「细胞器的」
由「细胞器」加表示「相似」的成分构成，义为「类细胞器的」
由同一「工具、器官」词根构成，义为「器官；机构」
由「器官」加表示「相似」的词尾构成，义为「类器官」

senses.title: A specialised structure inside a cell
senses.definition: any distinct subcellular structure with a defined function
senses.definitionCN: 指细胞内任何具有明确功能的独立结构
senses.example: Every organelle in the list has a known function.
senses.exampleCN: 清单上的每个细胞器都有已知功能。
senses.why: The word was coined as a diminutive of organ, a little organ inside a cell.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是「器官」的指小形式，意为细胞里的小器官。

senses.title: A membrane-bound organelle
senses.definition: an organelle enclosed by its own lipid membrane, such as a mitochondrion or a nucleus
senses.definitionCN: 指由自身脂质膜包住的细胞器，如线粒体或细胞核
senses.example: A membrane-bound organelle keeps its contents apart from the cytoplasm.
senses.exampleCN: 膜结合细胞器把自己的内容物与细胞质隔开。
senses.why: An internal membrane lets a compartment hold different chemistry from the rest of the cell.
senses.whyCN: 内部膜让一个隔间保有与细胞其余部分不同的化学环境。

senses.title: A non-membrane-bound organelle
senses.definition: a structure with a defined job but no surrounding membrane, such as a ribosome
senses.definitionCN: 指有明确功能但没有外膜的细胞结构，如核糖体
senses.example: The ribosome is a non-membrane-bound organelle.
senses.exampleCN: 核糖体是一种无膜细胞器。
senses.why: Not every organelle is a room; some are more like a machine standing in the open.
senses.whyCN: 并非每个细胞器都是房间，有些更像摆在空地上的机器。

senses.title: A named organelle with a specific role
senses.definition: a particular organelle such as a mitochondrion, chloroplast or lysosome
senses.definitionCN: 指线粒体、叶绿体或溶酶体等具体细胞器
senses.example: The mitochondrion is the organelle that releases energy from food.
senses.exampleCN: 线粒体是从食物中释放能量的细胞器。
senses.why: Once each structure was separated, it could be named and assigned a task.
senses.whyCN: 各结构被分离出来之后，便可逐一命名并分派任务。

senses.title: An organelle genome
senses.definition: the small set of genes carried inside an organelle such as a mitochondrion or chloroplast
senses.definitionCN: 指线粒体或叶绿体等细胞器内部携带的一小组基因
senses.example: The chloroplast organelle still carries its own DNA.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿体细胞器仍携带自己的遗传物质。
senses.why: Some organelles keep a remnant genome, evidence of their independent ancestry.
senses.whyCN: 有些细胞器保留残余基因组，这是它们曾独立起源的证据。

senses.title: An organelle in a single-celled organism
senses.titleCN: 单细胞生物中的细胞器
senses.definition: the equivalent structures in bacteria, protists and other unicellular life
senses.definitionCN: 指细菌、原生生物等单细胞生命中的对应结构
senses.example: A protist may use a contractile organelle to expel water.
senses.exampleCN: 原生生物可能用一种可收缩的细胞器排出水分。
senses.why: Single cells do inside one body what tissues do across many.
senses.whyCN: 单细胞在一个身体里完成组织在许多细胞间完成的事。

senses.title: The older sense of a small organ
senses.definition: in older anatomical writing, a small organ or an organ-like part
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的解剖学文献中，指小器官或类似器官的部分
senses.example: Early texts called the structure a little organelle of the body.
senses.exampleCN: 早期文献把这个结构称作身体的小器官。
senses.why: The diminutive began in anatomy and was later borrowed by cell biology.
senses.whyCN: 这个指小词最初用于解剖学，后来被细胞生物学借用。

senses.title: An engineered or diseased organelle
senses.titleCN: 被改造或发生病变的细胞器
senses.definition: an organelle modified in the laboratory or one whose failure causes disease
senses.definitionCN: 指在实验室中被改造的细胞器，或因功能失常而致病的细胞器
senses.example: A synthetic organelle can be built to store a new product.
senses.exampleCN: 可以构建一种合成细胞器来储存新产物。
senses.why: Understanding the part lets researchers repair it or replace its job.
senses.whyCN: 了解这个部件之后，研究者便能修理它或替换它的职能。

intro.en: Organelle is a diminutive of organ: Greek organon, a tool or instrument, became Latin organum and English organ, and the French diminutive ending -elle made a little organ. Cell biologists adopted it in the nineteenth century for the small bodies they saw inside cells.
intro.cn: 这个词是「器官」的指小形式：希腊语 organon「工具、器具」变成拉丁语 organum 与英语 organ，再加法语指小词尾，成为「小器官」。细胞生物学家在十九世纪用它指他们在细胞内看到的小体。

items.en: Organon meant a tool, an instrument or an organ of the body.
items.cn: 这个词意为工具、器具或身体器官。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word for an instrument or an organ.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊词，指器具或器官。

items.en: English used it for body parts, for musical instruments and for organized bodies.
items.cn: 英语用它指身体部位、乐器与有组织的机构。

items.en: The diminutive ending made a small version of a noun.
items.cn: 这个指小词尾构成名词的「小」版本。

items.en: Cell biologists used the little-organ word for the bodies visible inside cells; the exact coinage date is uncertain.
items.cn: 细胞生物学家用「小器官」这个词指细胞内可见的小体；确切造词年份不确定。

items.en: Electron microscopy and cell fractionation turned the word into a classified family of structures.
items.cn: 电子显微镜与细胞分级分离把这个词变成一组被分类的结构。

note.en: The first group shares the organ root or the diminutive ending; the second group names particular organelles and related structures.
note.cn: 第一组共享「器官」词根或指小词尾；第二组是具体细胞器与相关结构。

entries.definition: A body part with a specific function, or an instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有特定功能的器官，或指乐器。

entries.definition: A lab-grown miniature organ-like structure.
entries.definitionCN: 指实验室培养的微型类器官结构。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning of or belonging to organelles.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于细胞器的形容词。

entries.definition: Resembling an organelle in structure or function.
entries.definitionCN: 指在结构或功能上像细胞器。

entries.definition: Relating to living things or to carbon chemistry, from the same instrument word.
entries.definitionCN: 指与生物或碳化学有关的，同出「器官」词根。

entries.definition: The organelle that produces most of the cell's energy.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生细胞大部分能量的细胞器。

entries.definition: The plant organelle where photosynthesis happens.
entries.definitionCN: 指植物细胞中进行光合作用的细胞器。

entries.definition: The non-membrane-bound organelle that assembles proteins.
entries.definitionCN: 指组装蛋白质的无膜细胞器。

entries.definition: A membrane-bound compartment for storage or waste.
entries.definitionCN: 指用于储存或处理废物的膜结合隔间。

entries.definition: A body inside a cell that is not usually called an organelle.
entries.definitionCN: 指细胞内通常不称为细胞器的小体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the little organ: a workshop inside a room.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着「小器官」展开：房间里的一个个小工坊。

normal.en: Organ plus a diminutive ending: a little organ inside a cell.
normal.cn: 器官加指小词尾：细胞里的小器官。

normal.en: Membrane-bound organelles are rooms; ribosomes are machines in the open.
normal.cn: 膜结合细胞器是房间，核糖体是摆在空地上的机器。

normal.en: The mitochondrion releases energy, the chloroplast captures it.
normal.cn: 线粒体释放能量，叶绿体捕获能量。

normal.en: Some organelles keep their own DNA, a trace of independent ancestry.
normal.cn: 有些细胞器保留自己的遗传物质，是独立起源的痕迹。

normal.en: A synthetic organelle is a new workshop built on purpose.
normal.cn: 合成细胞器是特意新建的工坊。

abstract.en: Division of labour works at every scale, down to a single cell.
abstract.cn: 分工在每一个尺度上都成立，直到单个细胞之内。

abstract.en: A compartment is a promise that two chemistries will not mix.
abstract.cn: 隔间是一个承诺：两种化学环境不会混在一起。

abstract.en: Knowing what a part does is the first step to repairing it.
abstract.cn: 知道一个部件做什么，是修理它的第一步。

examples.en: The organelle was first described under an electron microscope.
examples.cn: 这个细胞器最早是在电子显微镜下被描述的。

examples.en: Each organelle carries a marker that identifies its type.
examples.cn: 每个细胞器都带有识别其类型的标记。

examples.en: Loss of the organelle stops the cell from storing starch.
examples.cn: 该细胞器的丧失使细胞无法储存淀粉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奥格内尔」——器官（奥格）缩小成「内尔」小间，就是细胞器：细胞器、小器官

root: 希腊语 organon「工具、器官」经拉丁语 organum 与英语 organ，再加法语指小词尾构成「小器官」；十九世纪被细胞生物学用来指细胞内小体，确切年份不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from any specialised cell structure to the membrane-bound and open kinds, named examples, their genomes, single-cell versions, the older anatomical sense and engineered or diseased forms.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从任何专职细胞结构出发，走向有膜与无膜两类、具体例子、它们的基因组、单细胞版本、较早的解剖义，以及被改造或病变的形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut-away cell with several small coloured workshops, each doing a different job.
core.cn: 核心意象：细胞剖面图上几个亮着不同颜色的小工坊，各自干不同的活。

branches.en: THE NAME: any specialised body, and the older anatomical sense of a little organ.
branches.cn: 名称：任何专职小体，以及较早的解剖学「小器官」义。

branches.en: THE TWO KINDS: rooms with membranes, and machines without them.
branches.cn: 两类形态：有膜的隔间，与无膜的机器。

branches.en: THE WORKERS: named organelles with known jobs, also found in single cells.
branches.cn: 工作者：有已知职责的具名细胞器，也见于单细胞生物。

branches.en: THE INHERITANCE: a small genome kept inside the organelle.
branches.cn: 遗传：细胞器内部保留的一小组基因。

branches.en: THE MADE AND THE BROKEN: engineered organelles and organelles whose failure causes disease.
branches.cn: 被造与被损：工程化细胞器，以及功能失常致病的细胞器。

intro.en: The word is one Greek noun for a tool, one Latin borrowing, one English shortening and one French diminutive ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个希腊「工具」名词、一个拉丁借词、一个英语缩短形式与一个法语指小词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word for instrument; the diminutive ending reached English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊语表示「器具」的词；指小词尾经法语进入英语。

items.example: It is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 它是整族词的来源。

items.example: Latin passed it to English.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把它传给英语。

items.example: English uses it for both flesh and music.
items.exampleCN: 英语用它指身体部位，也指乐器。

items.example: It turns organ into a little organ.
items.exampleCN: 它把「器官」变成「小器官」。

items.example: Cell biology gave the little organ its modern meaning.
items.exampleCN: 细胞生物学赋予「小器官」现代含义。

items.example: It forms organellar, belonging to organelles.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「细胞器的」。

items.example: It forms organoid, a structure resembling an organ.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「类器官」。

items.example: It forms organic from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 它由同一词根构成「有机的」。

由「细胞器」加「相似」成分构成，义为「类细胞器的」
由拉丁「器具、器官」名词构成，义为「器官」

definition_zh: 聚集；聚合；集合体；聚集物；（血小板）凝集；数据汇总；内容聚合；土壤团聚
definition_en: the act of gathering separate units into one body, the body so formed, or a technical instance of such gathering in medicine, biology, data, economics, computing, or soil science
core_image: 把散在场地上的木箱一个个码进同一间仓库：码的过程和码好的那一堆，都叫同一个名字
scene: 离心后的血样被送进分析仪，血小板凝集的曲线在屏幕上一点点抬起来。 After the blood sample is spun, platelet aggregation appears as a rising curve on the analyser screen.
sceneCN: 这里 aggregation 是「（血小板）凝集」（第 4 个义项：血细胞或颗粒在体内聚结）；句意：血样离心后，血小板凝集在分析仪屏幕上呈现为一条上升的曲线。场景要点：离心管、血浆分层、分析仪屏幕、上升的曲线、检验标签。

pos.zh: 聚集；聚合；集合体；聚集物；汇总

senses.title: The act of bringing separate things together
senses.titleCN: 把分开的事物聚拢的动作
senses.definition: the act of collecting separate people, things, or amounts into one group or total
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的人、事物或数额收集进一个群体或总数的动作
senses.example: The aggregation of the six village registers took two months.
senses.exampleCN: 把六个村的登记册汇总起来花了两个月。
senses.why: The -ation suffix names an action, not a thing: it is the herdsman's work of driving animals through the gate, seen as a process.
senses.whyCN: -ation 后缀命名的是动作，不是物件：它是牧人把牲畜赶过门去的那份劳作，被看成一个过程。

senses.title: The body that results from gathering
senses.definition: the group or mass that results from such collecting, viewed as a single body
senses.definitionCN: 由这种收集形成并被当作单一整体的群体或团块
senses.example: The federation began as an aggregation of independent guilds.
senses.exampleCN: 这个联合会最初是若干独立行会的集合体。
senses.why: Latin action nouns in -atio could name both the act and its result, and English kept both. Once the gate closes, the pen full of animals is itself an aggregation.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语以 -atio 结尾的动作名词既可指动作也可指结果，英语把两者都保留了。门一关上，装满牲畜的圈本身就是 an aggregation。

senses.title: A loose, unorganized mass
senses.definition: a heap or crowd of things gathered without order or system, a sense recorded from the 1560s
senses.definitionCN: 未经秩序或体系整理而堆聚起来的一堆物或一群人，此义记录于 16 世纪 60 年代
senses.example: The attic held an aggregation of broken chairs, lamps, and boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 阁楼里堆着一堆坏椅子、台灯和箱子。
senses.why: If nothing sorts the units, the pen shows only a random heap. The word then stresses the absence of structure rather than the fact of gathering.
senses.whyCN: 如果没有东西来整理这些单位，圈里就只剩随机的一堆。此时这个词强调的不是“聚拢”这件事，而是“没有结构”。

senses.title: Clotting or clumping inside the body
senses.definition: the clumping together of blood cells, platelets, or other particles in the body
senses.definitionCN: 血细胞、血小板或其他颗粒在体内聚结成团
senses.example: Platelet aggregation is the first step in sealing a cut vessel.
senses.exampleCN: 血小板凝集是封住破损血管的第一步。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the image at the cellular scale: cells are the flock, and they gather at a wound. The earliest English use, in the early 15th century, was already medical — the formation of a pustule.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这个意象借到细胞尺度：细胞是羊群，在伤口处聚拢。英语最早的用法在 15 世纪早期，已经是医学义——脓疱的形成。

senses.title: Animals gathered at one place
senses.definition: a temporary gathering of animals, especially birds or insects, at one place
senses.definitionCN: 动物尤其是鸟类或昆虫在同一地点的临时聚集
senses.example: An aggregation of gulls followed the trawler for its discards.
senses.exampleCN: 一群海鸥跟着拖网渔船，等着被丢弃的杂鱼。
senses.why: Here the flock is literal again. The word is preferred over herd or flock when the gathering is temporary and the animals are not a permanent social unit.
senses.whyCN: 这里“群”又回到字面。当聚集是临时的、动物并非永久社会单位时，人们更愿意用这个词而不是 herd 或 flock。

senses.title: Combining data into totals
senses.definition: the process of combining data from many sources into a single set or summary
senses.definitionCN: 把来自许多来源的数据合并成一个数据集或摘要的过程
senses.example: The dashboard performs nightly aggregation of sales records from 400 stores.
senses.exampleCN: 仪表盘每晚对 400 家门店的销售记录做一次汇总。
senses.why: Data are treated as countable units. The process sense of the suffix is applied to records, and the result is a total that can be queried.
senses.whyCN: 数据被当作可数的单位。后缀的“过程”义被用到记录上，产物就是一个可以查询的总数。

senses.title: Gathering content from many sites
senses.definition: the automatic collection of news, links, or other content from many sites into one feed
senses.definitionCN: 把新闻、链接或其他内容从许多网站自动收集进同一个信息流
senses.example: The site is a news aggregator; its value lies in aggregation, not in reporting.
senses.exampleCN: 这个网站是新闻聚合器；它的价值在于聚合，而不在于采写。
senses.why: The flock now consists of pages scattered across the web. Software plays the herdsman, and the feed is the pen the reader visits.
senses.whyCN: 现在这群“牲畜”是散落在网络上的页面。软件扮演牧人，信息流就是读者走进的那个圈。

senses.title: A combined economic measure
senses.definition: a total measure built by adding individual economic units, such as a definition of the money supply
senses.definitionCN: 把单个经济单位相加而构成的总体指标，例如对货币供应量的某种界定
senses.example: The M2 aggregation combines currency, demand deposits, and small time deposits.
senses.exampleCN: M2 这一总量指标把通货、活期存款和小额定期存款合并在一起。
senses.why: Economics must speak of millions of households at once, so it aggregates them into one number. The technical noun names one defined total, such as M2, and its plural names the several totals that are defined.
senses.whyCN: 经济学必须一次性谈论数百万家庭，于是把他们聚合成一个数字。这个技术性名词命名一个被定义的总量（如 M2），其复数则命名被定义出来的若干总量。

senses.title: Clumping of soil or mineral particles
senses.titleCN: 土壤或矿物颗粒的团聚
senses.definition: the binding of fine soil or mineral particles into larger clumps
senses.definitionCN: 细小的土壤或矿物颗粒结合成较大的团粒
senses.example: Organic matter improves soil structure by promoting aggregation of clay particles.
senses.exampleCN: 有机质促进黏土颗粒团聚，从而改善土壤结构。
senses.why: At the smallest scale the flock is a cloud of particles. The same gathering produces a clump you can hold, so the word moves from counting to physical structure.
senses.whyCN: 在最小尺度上，羊群是一团颗粒。同一种聚拢产生了可以拿在手里的团粒，于是这个词从“计数”走到了“物理结构”。

intro.en: Aggregation is not a fresh English coinage: it came whole from Medieval Latin aggregatio, the action noun of aggregare. The chain is aggregare 'drive to a flock' → aggregatio 'a driving to a flock' → English aggregation. The suffix -ation (< Latin -ationem) names an action and, by metonymy, its result, which is why the word can mean both 'the gathering' and 'the thing gathered'.
intro.cn: aggregation 不是英语后来新造的词：它整体来自中世纪拉丁语 aggregatio，即 aggregare 的动作名词。链条是 aggregare“赶成一群”→ aggregatio“赶成一群这件事”→ 英语 aggregation。后缀 -ation（< 拉丁 -ationem）命名动作，并由转喻兼指结果，所以这个词既能指“聚集”这件事，也能指“被聚起来的东西”。

items.en: First recorded in English as aggregacioun, in medicine (Chauliac), meaning 'formation of a pustule'. The technical medical use is therefore the oldest, not a modern borrowing.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为 aggregacioun，出现在医学著作（肖利亚克）中，意为“脓疱的形成”。因此医学技术义是最古老的，而不是现代才借入的。

items.en: From Medieval Latin aggregationem (nominative aggregatio), a noun of action from the past-participle stem of Latin aggregare 'collect, bring together'.
items.cn: 来自中世纪拉丁语 aggregationem（主格 aggregatio），是由拉丁语 aggregare“收集、聚拢”的过去分词词干构成的动作名词。

items.en: Aggregare is ad- 'to' + gregare 'collect into a flock', from grex (genitive gregis) 'flock'. The -ation element is the Latin -ationem, the same action-noun suffix seen in congregation and segregation.
items.cn: aggregare 是 ad-“向”+ gregare“赶成一群”，后者出自 grex（属格 gregis）“群”。-ation 成分就是拉丁语 -ationem，与 congregation、segregation 中看到的动作名词后缀相同。

items.en: The sense 'a combined whole' is recorded from the 1540s, and 'the act of collecting in an unorganized mass' from the 1560s. English thus records the product sense before the general process sense.
items.cn: “合并成的整体”义记录于 16 世纪 40 年代，“无组织地收集成一堆的动作”义记录于 16 世纪 60 年代。也就是说，英语先记录了产物义，后记录了一般过程义。

items.en: Technical compounds multiply: platelet aggregation in medicine, aggregation in statistics and economics, news aggregation and link aggregation in computing, soil aggregation in agronomy.
items.cn: 技术复合词大量增加：医学的血小板凝集、统计与经济学的加总、计算机的新闻聚合与链路聚合、农学的土壤团聚。

items.en: Congregation and segregation share the grex root but not the prefix: con- means 'together', se- means 'apart', while ag- is ad- 'to'. Aggravation looks close because of ag- and -ation, but its root is gravis 'heavy'. An identical suffix never guarantees an identical root.
items.cn: congregation 与 segregation 共享 grex 词根但前缀不同：con- 意为“一起”，se- 意为“分开”，而 ag- 是 ad-“向”。aggravation 因为 ag- 和 -ation 看起来很近，但它的词根是 gravis“重”。后缀相同绝不等于词根相同。

note.en: The first group separates the base word, the agent noun, a same-root religious noun, and a look-alike from a different root. The second group compares nouns for groups and heaps, each with a different emphasis on selection, time, technical use, or spatial closeness.
note.cn: 第一组区分基础词、施动者名词、同根的宗教名词，以及另一个词根的形近词。第二组比较表示“群体／堆集”的名词，它们分别在挑选、时间、技术用法、空间紧密度上各有侧重。

entries.definition: the verb, noun, and adjective from which aggregation is formed. The noun adds -ation and names the process or result; the base names the act or the total.
entries.definitionCN: aggregation 由它构成的那个动词、名词和形容词。名词加 -ation 后指过程或结果；基础词则指动作或总数。

entries.definition: a person, program, or site that gathers things. The -or marks the doer, while -ation marks the deed.
entries.definitionCN: 收集事物的个人、程序或网站。-or 标记施动者，而 -ation 标记行为。

entries.definition: a group assembled, especially for worship. It shares grex, but con- 'together' describes the assembled body rather than the act of driving units to it.
entries.definitionCN: 聚集起来的人群，尤指宗教会众。它共享 grex，但 con-“一起”描述的是聚成的群体，而不是把单位赶向它的动作。

entries.definition: the act of making something worse or more annoying. It comes from gravis 'heavy'; only the -ation ending and the ag- front match.
entries.definitionCN: 使事情更糟或更烦人的行为。它来自 gravis“重”；与 aggregation 相同的只有 -ation 词尾和 ag- 词头。

entries.definition: a group of things gathered, often chosen and kept because they are wanted. It implies selection and curation, not just a total.
entries.definitionCN: 收集起来的一组东西，常因需要而被挑选并保存。它含“挑选与整理”的意思，不只是加总。

entries.definition: a mass formed by gradual piling up over time. It stresses duration and quantity, not the grouping of units into one body.
entries.definitionCN: 随着时间逐渐堆积形成的量。它强调持续与数量，而不是把单位聚成一个整体。

entries.definition: a set of things or people considered together, used in art, archaeology, and ecology. It is formal and usually implies a deliberately defined set for analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 被放在一起考虑的一组物或人，用于艺术、考古与生态学。它较正式，通常暗示为分析而刻意界定的一组。

entries.definition: a small group of similar things positioned close together. It stresses spatial proximity and usually fewer, tighter units than an aggregation.
entries.definitionCN: 位置靠近的一小组相似事物。它强调空间邻近，通常比 aggregation 包含更少、更紧密的单位。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces: aggregate plus -ation, the grex family, the three prefixes that change the direction of gathering, the medical first use, and the modern technical compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 真实成分：aggregate 加 -ation、grex 词族、改变聚拢方向的三个前缀、最早的医学用法，以及现代技术复合词。

normal.en: -ation turns the verb aggregate into a noun for the process and, by metonymy, for the result — gathering and the gathered body.
normal.cn: -ation 把动词 aggregate 变成名词，既指过程，又通过转喻指结果——聚集这件事和被聚成的东西。

normal.en: The grex family points in three directions: ad- 'to' gathers into a flock, con- 'together' assembles a crowd, se- 'apart' separates from the flock.
normal.cn: grex 词族指向三个方向：ad-“向”赶进群，con-“一起”聚成众，se-“分开”离群。

normal.en: The oldest English record is medical: a pustule forming. Platelet aggregation is the same image at the scale of cells.
normal.cn: 英语最早的记录是医学的：脓疱形成。血小板凝集就是同一意象在细胞尺度上的重演。

normal.en: Modern compounds show the range: data aggregation, news aggregation, monetary aggregation, soil aggregation.
normal.cn: 现代复合词展示了范围：数据汇总、新闻聚合、货币总量、土壤团聚。

normal.en: Aggravation is not a relative: its root is gravis 'heavy'. Only the suffix and the assimilated prefix coincide.
normal.cn: aggravation 不是亲戚：它的词根是 gravis“重”。相同的只有后缀和同化后的前缀。

abstract.en: Boxes scattered on a warehouse floor are stacked into one bay; the stacking and the stack share a name.
abstract.cn: 散在仓库地上的箱子被码进同一个货位；码的动作和码好的那一堆共用一个名字。

abstract.en: A crowd at a shrine, cells at a wound, pages pulled into one feed: the same gate, three different scales.
abstract.cn: 神庙前的人群、伤口处的细胞、被拉进同一个信息流的页面：同一道门，三种不同尺度。

abstract.en: If the boxes are thrown rather than stacked, the result is still an aggregation — but the word then means a heap without order.
abstract.cn: 如果箱子是扔进去而不是码好的，结果仍是一个 aggregation——但此时这个词指没有秩序的一堆。

examples.en: The report is an aggregation of data from twelve regional offices.
examples.cn: 这份报告汇总了十二个地区办事处的数据。

examples.en: Platelet aggregation is one of the first steps in blood clotting.
examples.cn: 血小板凝集是血液凝固的最初步骤之一。

examples.en: An aggregation of seabirds formed around the trawler.
examples.cn: 一群海鸟在拖网渔船周围聚集起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿格瑞给神」——阿格瑞把散落的供品“给”拢到神前，堆成一堆 → aggregation 聚集；集合体（只借音，不表词源）

root: 由 aggregate 加 -ation 构成：aggregate 出自拉丁 aggregare（ad-「向」+ gregare「赶成一群」，源于 grex「群」），-ation 出自拉丁 -ationem，是动作名词后缀；核心是「聚拢的动作，以及聚拢后的那一堆」。与 congregation（con-「一起」）、segregation（se-「分开」）同根不同前缀。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of aggregation all name the same event at different moments: the driving in, the pen now full, the heap left unsorted, or the same clumping seen in blood, birds, databases, money, and soil. The suffix lets the word denote both the deed and its product.
sensesIntro.cn: aggregation 的九个义项都在命名同一件事的不同时刻：赶进去的过程、装满的圈、没整理的一堆，或同一聚结在血液、鸟群、数据库、货币与土壤中的重演。后缀让这个词同时指行为与产物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate units pass through one gate and remain together as a body.
core.cn: 核心意象：分开的单位通过同一道门，之后作为一个整体留在一起。

chain: THE SAME SHAPE AT OTHER SCALES
PROCESS AND PRODUCT IN ONE WORD

branches.en: THE GENERAL PAIR: one sense names the work of gathering, the other names the body that stands gathered afterwards.
branches.cn: 一般性的一对：一个义项命名聚拢的劳作，另一个命名聚拢后立在那里的整体。

branches.en: WITHOUT ORDER: when nothing sorts the units, the same word shifts from 'gathered' to 'heaped at random'.
branches.cn: 没有秩序：当没有东西整理单位时，同一个词从“被聚拢”滑向“被胡乱堆着”。

branches.en: LIVING BODIES: platelets clump at a wound and birds gather at a trawler; the flock image is applied to cells and to temporary animal crowds.
branches.cn: 活体：血小板在伤口处聚结，鸟群在渔船边聚集；羊群意象被用到细胞和临时动物群上。

branches.en: NUMBERS: records are combined into a queryable total, and whole economies are reduced to monetary aggregates.
branches.cn: 数字：记录被合并成可查询的总数，整个经济被压缩成货币总量指标。

branches.en: THE SMALLEST AND LARGEST SCALES: software gathers pages into a feed, while clay particles bind into clumps in the soil.
branches.cn: 最小与最大的尺度：软件把页面聚成信息流，黏土颗粒则在土壤中结成团粒。

intro.en: Aggregation is a textbook -ation noun: a Latin action noun borrowed whole, then used in English for both the process and the product. Its base is aggregate, whose Latin core is ad- 'to' + greg- 'flock'; every related form in English keeps that flock somewhere in its history.
intro.cn: aggregation 是典型的 -ation 名词：整体借入的拉丁动作名词，在英语里同时指过程与产物。它的基础词是 aggregate，拉丁内核为 ad-“向”+ greg-“群”；英语中每一个相关形式都在某处保留着这个“群”。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is aggregare 'bring to a flock', gregare 'gather into a flock', grex 'flock', and the action suffix -atio (-ationem). The suffix is shared with congregation and segregation, which use the same grex with different prefixes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层包括 aggregare“聚到群里”、gregare“赶成一群”、grex“群”，以及动作名词后缀 -atio（-ationem）。这个后缀与 congregation、segregation 共用，后两者用同一个 grex 配不同前缀。

items.meaning: the act or result of gathering into a whole
items.meaningCN: 聚集成整体的动作或结果（-ation 动作名词后缀）
items.example: The aggregation of the census returns took months.
items.exampleCN: 人口普查表的汇总花了几个月。

items.meaning: to gather into one body; the body or total so formed
items.meaningCN: 聚成一体；聚成的整体或总数（ad- 向 + greg- 群）
items.example: The particles aggregate in still water.
items.exampleCN: 颗粒在静水中聚集。

items.meaning: one that gathers, especially a feed or site
items.meaningCN: 聚合者；聚合器（-or 施动者）
items.example: The aggregator collects headlines every ten minutes.
items.exampleCN: 这个聚合器每十分钟收集一次标题。

items.meaningCN: 有聚集倾向的（-ive 形容词）
items.example: The ants show aggregative behaviour around sugar.
items.exampleCN: 蚂蚁在糖周围表现出聚集行为。

items.meaning: the breaking of a total into its parts
items.meaningCN: 把总数拆回各部分；分解（dis- 反向 + aggregation）
items.example: Disaggregation of the figure revealed wide regional gaps.
items.exampleCN: 把这个数字拆开之后，暴露出很大的地区差异。

items.meaning: an assembled crowd, especially for worship
items.meaningCN: 聚在一起的群体，尤指宗教会众（con- 一起 + greg- 群）
items.example: The congregation filled the old church by seven.
items.exampleCN: 七点前会众就坐满了那座老教堂。

items.meaning: the separation of one group from the rest
items.meaningCN: 把某群体与其余分开；隔离（se- 分开 + greg- 群）
items.example: Segregation of the two waste streams cut disposal costs.
items.exampleCN: 把两股废物流分开，降低了处置成本。

items.meaning: fond of company, living in groups
items.meaningCN: 群居的；爱交际的（greg- 群 + -ous）
items.example: Sheep are gregarious and panic when isolated.
items.exampleCN: 羊是群居动物，被隔离时会惊慌。

items.meaning: standing out from the flock, hence shockingly bad
items.meaningCN: 从群中突出，因而指极其糟糕（e- 出 + greg- 群）
items.example: The omission was egregious, not merely careless.
items.exampleCN: 这个遗漏是极其严重的，不只是粗心。

items.example: Latin grex gives English both aggregate and egregious.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 grex 给了英语 aggregate 和 egregious。

latinEntries.meaning: to bring to a flock, collect
